# envoy-go Behavior Contract

This file is the canonical reference for differential equivalence between envoy-go and the upstream Envoy image pinned in `ENVOY_TARGET.md` (see doctrine `D-3.3` and `D-3.7`). When a phase introduces new features, it extends the per-layer subsections below with concrete rules. When a phase's observed behavior diverges from this contract, either the contract is updated *via ADR* or the implementation is fixed — never both silently.

The contract is the contract. Do **not** consult Envoy C++ source to resolve ambiguity; settle ambiguities with an ADR in `DECISIONS.md` that extends the relevant subsection here.

---

## Equivalence Matrix (§7.2 of BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md)

| Dimension | Required equivalence |
|---|---|
| Response status | Exact |
| Response body | Byte-exact for deterministic handlers; semantically equal for filter-modified bodies |
| Response headers | Set-equal modulo documented allow-list (`server`, `date`, timing/identity headers explicitly listed) |
| Response trailers | Set-equal under the same allow-list discipline |
| HTTP/2 & HTTP/3 framing | Structurally equivalent (same frame types/order on equivalent events); not byte-equal |
| Access log records | Semantically equal after field-mapping |
| Stats output | Per-stat behavioral delta after defined load is equal between envoy-go and reference Envoy. Gauges are snapshot-equal after drain. Names + label keys + types byte-equal; HELP text ignored. Allow-list: 46 stats listed in § Stat-name mapping. All other Envoy stat names in /stats/prometheus output are ignored by the differential. |
| xDS wire behavior | ADS message sequences match the protocol state machine; effective-config diff on identical snapshots |
| Timing | Not compared by default; a phase may opt in to latency bounds |
| HTTP filter chain | Per-request equivalence on cors preflight + actual-request response shapes (status + header set + body) between envoy-go and reference Envoy. Filter iteration order, sendLocalReply encode-chain entry, and 413 overflow shape are verbatim-pinned at the ENVOY_TARGET SHA. Differential covers cors only; `envoy.filters.http.envoy_go_test` excluded (test-only); other filters in the §9 family are future-phase scope. |
| Listener filters | Per-connection chain-selection equivalence: which `filter_chain` is dispatched is byte-equal across envoy-go and reference Envoy. Verified via per-connection backend-port routing in fixture 0008. Chain-match precedence ordering, `default_filter_chain` fallback semantics, and empty-match-vs-default resolution are verbatim-pinned at the ENVOY_TARGET SHA. Differential covers chain-selection only (which backend each connection is routed to); listener-filter internal byte-level behavior (e.g., tls_inspector parser output) is unit-tested only. |
| Admin /config_dump | Body byte-equal modulo build/timestamp/uptime allow-list. Three-envelope ordering: Bootstrap, Listeners, Clusters. Allow-list: `bootstrap.node.user_agent_name`, `bootstrap.node.user_agent_build_version`, `bootstrap.node.extensions[]`, `<*ConfigDump>.last_updated` per-field allow-listed. dynamic_* arrays absent in both. (Per phase 08.1 SPEC §13.2.) |
| Admin /clusters | Tuple-set equality on `(cluster, key, value)` triples. envoy-go emits Envoy's full unconditional 28-line-per-cluster + 18-line-per-endpoint set with default constants for non-modeled fields. Allow-list: hot-path counters `cx_total`, `cx_connect_fail`, `rq_total`, `rq_active`, `rq_error` allow ±1 tolerance. (Per phase 08.1 SPEC §13.2.) |
| Admin /listeners | Body byte-equal (after framing dechunk). Single line per listener. No allow-list. (Per phase 08.1 SPEC §13.2.) |
| Admin /server_info | Body byte-equal modulo build/uptime/CLI-flags/node allow-list. The `state` field IS asserted byte-equal. Allow-list: `version`, `uptime_current_epoch`, `uptime_all_epochs`, `command_line_options.*` (subset), `hot_restart_version`, `node.user_agent_*`, `node.extensions[]` per-field allow-listed. (Per phase 08.1 SPEC §13.2.) |
| Admin /drain_listeners | Body byte-equal `OK\n` (POST); 405 + body `Method <X> not allowed, POST required.\n` (non-POST). Idempotent semantics; query-param ?graceful=true silent-ignored. Header set inherits umbrella rules; framing per phase-01 dechunk-discipline. Method-discrimination is the FIRST envoy-go endpoint with 405 enforcement (per ADR-0093 partially amending ADR-0090). |
| Admin /ready (DRAINING) | Body byte-equal `DRAINING\n` to reference Envoy v1.37.2 in DRAINING state. Status 503. DRAINING precedence over LIVE / PRE_INITIALIZING. Status 503 (matches PRE_INITIALIZING). Header set inherits umbrella rules. Per-proxy trigger script normalization per 08.2 SPEC §7.2 (envoy-go: /drain_listeners; ref Envoy: /drain_listeners + /healthcheck/fail). |
| Admin /server_info (DRAINING) | The `state` field IS asserted byte-equal (`"DRAINING"`) when both proxies are in DRAINING. Other fields per ADR-0088 allow-list. Inherits ADR-0088 allow-list for non-state fields (version, uptime_*, command_line_options, hot_restart_version, node). |
| HTTP filter `envoy.filters.http.fault` | Per-request equivalence on abort response shape (status + 4-header set + body byte-exact `fault filter abort`), delay timing (±10ms tolerance), per-route wholesale-override resolution, headers-field exact-match gate, and stat counter increments under the per-scenario differential gate (fixture 0011-http-fault). NOT asserted: header-driven fault path (deferred — ADR-0104), response_rate_limit (deferred), abort.grpc_status (deferred), HeaderMatcher non-exact variants. |
| HTTP filter `envoy.filters.http.header_mutation` | Per-request equivalence on post-mutation request headers (visible at upstream backend) and post-mutation response headers (visible at downstream client) under listener-level + per-route 3-tier configurations, including AppendAction × 4 + Remove + `keep_empty_value` boundary + multi-valued header collapse / preserve semantics + `most_specific_header_mutations_wins` cross-tier ordering (both flag values). Boot-time enforcement of the 6-name protected-header set per ADR-0111 + phase 10 §11.1. Differential gate fixture 0012-http-header-mutation. NOT asserted: header-value formatter substitution (deferred — ADR-0113), `query_parameter_mutations` (deferred — ADR-0112), H2 differential coverage. |

"Semantically equal" is defined per dimension in the subsections below. Where a dimension has no subsection yet, the matrix row is its complete definition and phases may only tighten (not relax) it.

---

## Header allow-list

The allow-list enumerates response headers whose values are permitted to differ between envoy-go and upstream Envoy without constituting a differential failure. Each entry names the header, the permitted divergence (presence-only / format-only / value-range), the phase that introduced the entry, and the ADR that justifies it.

| Header | Scope | Permitted divergence | Introduced by | Justifying ADR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `date` | Admin `/ready` response | Value is RFC 7231 IMF-fixdate, non-deterministic per request. Presence required on both upstream and subject responses; value NOT byte-compared. | Phase 01 | ADR-0015 |
| `Server` | HCM-locally-generated responses | Presence-only — Envoy: `envoy`; envoy-go: `envoy` (matches per ADR-0014 reaffirmation). Set-equality only. | Phase 04 | ADR-0044 |
| `Content-Length` | HTTP/1.1 responses | HTTP/1.1 framing-divergence-permitted (Envoy may choose Content-Length while envoy-go chooses Transfer-Encoding: chunked or vice versa; `http.ReadResponse` decodes both transparently). | Phase 04 | ADR-0044 |
| `Transfer-Encoding` | HTTP/1.1 responses | HTTP/1.1 framing-divergence-permitted (mirror of Content-Length). | Phase 04 | ADR-0044 |
| `x-envoy-*` | Routed-to-upstream HTTP/1.1 responses | Every header with this prefix; presence-not-required on subject (envoy-go does not inject these in phase 04; Envoy does). | Phase 04 | ADR-0044 |
| `x-forwarded-*` | Routed-to-upstream HTTP/1.1 responses | Every header with this prefix; presence-not-required on subject. | Phase 04 | ADR-0044 |
| `x-request-id` | Routed-to-upstream HTTP/1.1 responses | Presence-not-required on subject. | Phase 04 | ADR-0044 |
| `:status` | HCM-locally-generated H2 responses | Required + value-asserted | Phase 05.1 | ADR-0052 |
| `:method` | Routed-to-upstream H2 requests | Required + value-asserted (active per ADR-0057; phase 05.2) | Phase 05.1 | ADR-0052 |
| `:path` | Routed-to-upstream H2 requests | Required + value-asserted (active per ADR-0057; phase 05.2) | Phase 05.1 | ADR-0052 |
| `:scheme` | Routed-to-upstream H2 requests | Required + value-asserted (active per ADR-0057; phase 05.2) | Phase 05.1 | ADR-0052 |
| `:authority` | Routed-to-upstream H2 requests | Required + value-asserted (active per ADR-0057; phase 05.2) | Phase 05.1 | ADR-0052 |
| `x-ratelimit-limit` | HCM-locally-generated + routed-to-upstream responses (ratelimit filter encode side) | **Set-equal byte-exact** — NOT an allow-list "permitted divergence" entry but a set-equal-byte-exact entry per scenario (g) `x_ratelimit_headers` cross-side dispatch (parent SPEC §4.7 + AMEND-8; DRAFT_VERSION_03 byte format `<MIN.requests_per_unit>[, <rpu>;w=<window_sec>[;name="<n>"]]...` per `ratelimit_headers.cc:13-65`). Emitted on ALL dispositions (OK + OVER_LIMIT + fail-open error) when `enable_x_ratelimit_headers == DRAFT_VERSION_03`. The fail-closed reply path does NOT emit (nullptr-mutate per AMEND-8). | Phase 24.2 | ADR-0197 (in-place §Decision amendment for X-RateLimit slice per ADR-0052) |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining` | HCM-locally-generated + routed-to-upstream responses (ratelimit filter encode side) | **Set-equal byte-exact** — emission discipline identical to `x-ratelimit-limit`. Value is `<MIN.limit_remaining>` integer-ASCII per the upstream byte format. | Phase 24.2 | ADR-0197 (in-place §Decision amendment for X-RateLimit slice per ADR-0052) |
| `x-ratelimit-reset` | HCM-locally-generated + routed-to-upstream responses (ratelimit filter encode side) | **Set-equal byte-exact** — emission discipline identical to `x-ratelimit-limit`. Value is `<MIN.duration_until_reset.seconds>` integer-ASCII per the upstream byte format. | Phase 24.2 | ADR-0197 (in-place §Decision amendment for X-RateLimit slice per ADR-0052) |

**Phase 24.2 X-RateLimit allow-list extension note:** the three `x-ratelimit-*` rows are set-equal BYTE-EXACT (NOT "permitted-divergence" — the cross-side scenario (g) at fixture `0032-http-ratelimit` asserts byte equality between envoy-go and reference Envoy v1.37.2). The rows are listed in this table so operators consulting the response-header allow-list see the three headers explicitly, but the per-row divergence column ANCHORS `Set-equal byte-exact` rather than presence-only / format-only / value-range. The emission is gated by `enable_x_ratelimit_headers == DRAFT_VERSION_03` (the upstream-default `OFF` arm emits nothing — set-equal vacuously). On the OVER_LIMIT path the headers are injected by the encode hook BEFORE the AMEND-8 [a]+[b]+[c] header order assembly so the X-RateLimit headers are visible to downstream alongside the `x-envoy-ratelimited` + RLS-supplied + filter-config response headers. On the fail-closed error path (`failure_mode_deny=true` + RLS error) the encode hook does NOT run (the `SendLocalReply` constructs the reply without encoder participation per AMEND-8 nullptr-mutate); the headers are NOT emitted; the set-equal contract holds vacuously (both sides omit). MIN-status selection across multi-descriptor responses is by `limit_remaining` with insertion-order tie-break (= descriptor-list order = action-list order per AMEND-6; the FIRST equal-minimum status wins).

## Stat-name mapping

The mapping describes, for each emitted stat, the canonical Envoy stat name, the envoy-go internal name (if different), the tag set, and the flows under which values are required to be exact. When a phase introduces a new stat subsystem, it extends this table.

### Flattening rules SN1–SN8 (per ADR-0061; introduced by phase 06.1)

```
Rule SN1: Name segments matching `cluster.<n>.<rest>` extract `<n>` as label
          `envoy_cluster_name` and prefix `<rest>` with `envoy_cluster_`.

Rule SN2: Name segments matching `http.<stat_prefix>.<rest>` extract <stat_prefix>
          as label `envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix` and prefix <rest> with `envoy_http_`.

Rule SN3: Name segments matching `listener.<addr>.<rest>` extract <addr> as label
          `envoy_listener_address` and prefix <rest> with `envoy_listener_`.

Rule SN4: Names ending `_Nxx` where N ∈ {1..5} flatten to a base name with the
          trailing class digit STRIPPED (so the metric name ends in literal `_xx`),
          plus a label `envoy_response_code_class` whose value is the single class
          digit as a string (`"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, `"4"`, `"5"`). Empirically verified
          against reference Envoy v1.37.2 at the `ENVOY_TARGET.md`-pinned image
          (server SHA `5afe27fb338b16d5bb06b3a7198bcd581b4e3dee`) on 2026-04-27; see
          empirical evidence block below.

          Examples (canonical):
              cluster.foo.upstream_rq_2xx
                → envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="2",envoy_cluster_name="foo"}
              http.ingress_http.downstream_rq_5xx
                → envoy_http_downstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="5",envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix="ingress_http"}

          Counter-examples (NOT what Envoy emits):
              ✗ envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_2xx{...}            -- digit suffix preserved (wrong)
              ✗ ...{envoy_response_code_class="2xx",...}       -- label value with literal "xx" (wrong)
              ✗ envoy_cluster_upstream_rq{envoy_response_code_class="2",...}  -- _xx stripped entirely (wrong)

          Empirical evidence (verbatim excerpt from reference-Envoy /stats/prometheus
          scrape under a 5-request load with statuses [200,200,404,200,500] through
          HCM stat_prefix=ingress_http to cluster c_backend):

              # TYPE envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx counter
              envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="2",envoy_cluster_name="c_backend"} 3
              envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="4",envoy_cluster_name="c_backend"} 1
              envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="5",envoy_cluster_name="c_backend"} 1
              # TYPE envoy_http_downstream_rq_xx counter
              envoy_http_downstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="1",envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix="ingress_http"} 0
              envoy_http_downstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="2",envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix="ingress_http"} 3
              envoy_http_downstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="3",envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix="ingress_http"} 0
              envoy_http_downstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="4",envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix="ingress_http"} 1
              envoy_http_downstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="5",envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix="ingress_http"} 1

          Negative-confirmation grep (entire 1181-line scrape, no matches):
              grep -E 'envoy_[a-z_]*_(1xx|2xx|3xx|4xx|5xx)' /stats/prometheus  # -> 0 matches

          Tag-extractor regex source: Envoy v1.37.2
          source/common/config/well_known_names.cc, the `RESPONSE_CODE_CLASS`
          tag entry. Source-tree commit pin = the v1.37.2 release tag, server-side
          version-string SHA `5afe27fb338b16d5bb06b3a7198bcd581b4e3dee` (matches
          ENVOY_TARGET.md). The regex captures the inner `\dxx` token from the
          stat suffix `_<class>xx`, removes the entire `_<class>xx` from the stat
          name (yielding the base name ending `_xx` after the standard rename), and
          emits the captured digit as the `response_code_class` tag value.

Rule SN5: Server-scope names (`server.<rest>`) flatten to `envoy_server_<rest>`
          with no extracted labels.

Rule SN6: HELP text is best-effort English, NOT byte-equal to Envoy's HELP. The
          differential equivalence claim is on values + label keys + types only.

Rule SN7: Histograms are not emitted by 06.1. (Forward-looking.)

Rule SN8: Per-endpoint cluster stats are not emitted by 06.1. (Forward-looking.)
```

`<stat_prefix>` is read from HCM config (already plumbed from phase 04). `<addr>` is the listener bind address normalized like Envoy does (e.g., `0.0.0.0:10000` → `0.0.0.0_10000`). `<n>` is the cluster name as configured in the bootstrap.

The three `ring_hash_lb.*` gauges are registered + Set ONCE at ring build, and ONLY when `lb_policy: RING_HASH` (the `registerClusterMetrics` type-asserts `*ringHashLB`; reference parity). They are STATIC (the ring is immutable) and CROSS-SIDE-EXACT — keyed only on `(minimum_ring_size, hash_function, host count, weights)`, NOT on endpoint addresses (e.g. 1026 / 342 / 342 for a 3-equal-host default cluster, identical on subject and reference). See `### Load balancer — ring_hash (RING_HASH)`.

The two `maglev_lb.*` gauges are registered + Set ONCE at table build, and ONLY when `lb_policy: MAGLEV` (the `registerClusterMetrics` type-asserts `*maglevLB`; reference parity). They are STATIC (the table is immutable) and CROSS-SIDE-EXACT — keyed only on `(table_size, host count, weights)`, NOT on endpoint addresses (`min = floor(M/N)`, `max = ceil(M/N)`; e.g. 21845 / 21846 for a 3-equal-host default-65537 cluster, identical on subject and reference). There is NO `maglev_lb.size` gauge (the table size is config-known, unlike ring_hash's computed `ring_hash_lb.size`). See `### Load balancer — maglev (MAGLEV)`.

The four `lb_subsets_*` stats are registered ONLY when `lb_subset_config` is present (the `registerClusterMetrics` type-asserts `*subsetLB`; reference parity). `lb_subsets_active` (gauge) + `lb_subsets_created` (counter) are Set / Add ONCE at build to the distinct-subset count (envoy-go pins the semantically-correct ×1 count — the reference's 33× magnitude artifact is NOT mirrored; a recorded departure, so these two are NOT cross-side-equal). `lb_subsets_selected` (counter) + `lb_subsets_fallback` (counter) are incremented from `subsetLB.Pick` (+1 per subset hit / +1 per fallback path respectively) — the FIRST stats a `loadBalancer` Inc's from its own `Pick` path; they are request-counted and CROSS-SIDE-EQUAL (the `0064` `StatsAsserter` cross-equal prong). See `### Load balancer — subset (lb_subset_config)`.

**ADR-0059 §Decision AMENDMENT cross-reference (per phase 21 AMEND-7):** the float-valued-gauge int64 encoding convention added at phase 21 codifies three value-classes layered atop the unchanged `*stats.Gauge` int64 primitive: (1) time-typed gauges as int64 nanoseconds direct via `Gauge.Set(d.Nanoseconds())` — envoy-go-strict departure from upstream's milliseconds; stat NAMES preserve byte-exact upstream (`sample_rtt_msecs`, `min_rtt_msecs`); (2) ratio-typed gauges as int64 ×1000 via `Gauge.Set(int64(ratio * 1000))` — matches upstream's integer-millis convention; gives 3 decimal places of precision over the bounded `[0.5, 2.0]` domain (the `gradient` gauge); (3) bool-typed gauges as int64 0/1 via `Gauge.Set(stats.BoolToInt(b))` — NEW `internal/stats/conv.go` `BoolToInt(b bool) int64` sibling helper (~10 LoC; cross-phase reusable). The unchanged `*stats.Gauge` primitive is the only structural delta; the convention is layered at each callsite (gradient + sampleRTTMsecs + minRTTMsecs + minRTTCalculationActive) and documented at each metric's `# HELP` text per Rule SN6 best-effort English. Cross-references: ADR-0186 (paired phase-21 ADR; consumer); ADR-0059 §Decision AMENDMENT body (DECISIONS.md line ~2109); SPEC §3.2 + AMEND-7.

**Phase 13 (buffer filter) note:** The `envoy.filters.http.buffer` filter shipped in phase 13 contributes ZERO new entries to this table. The filter has no filter-specific counter namespace at all (confirmed empirically at phase 13 SPEC §11.5 — reference Envoy v1.37.2 emits NO `envoy_http_buffer_*` counter family). Buffer-filter overflow is observable on the envoy-go side via the existing `downstream_rq_4xx` HCM counter (rendered via Rule SN4 status-class flattening as `envoy_http_downstream_rq_xx{envoy_response_code_class="4",envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix="<HCM stat_prefix>"}`). The Envoy-only HCM counters `downstream_rq_too_large` (increments on every 413) and `downstream_rq_completed` (increments on every completed request) are NOT in this table; they are filtered out of the differential per the `### Twin-series filter discipline` allow-list discipline below.

### Twin-series filter discipline (per empirical-verification scrape)

> **Twin-series filter discipline (per empirical-verification scrape):** Envoy v1.37.2 ALSO emits two twin metric families that envoy-go does NOT emit and the differential fixture (§7) MUST filter out before per-counter delta comparison: (a) `envoy_cluster_external_upstream_rq_xx` (the "external" upstream-rq twin Envoy uses to split internal vs external traffic via `internal_traffic` config); (b) `envoy_listener_http_downstream_rq_xx` (a listener-scoped HCM-rq twin keyed by both listener address and HCM stat_prefix); plus the per-exact-status family `envoy_cluster_upstream_rq{envoy_response_code="200"}` (a separate metric family with `envoy_response_code` label, distinct from `envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx`'s `envoy_response_code_class` label). The fixture's allow-list enumerates exactly the 13 unique Prometheus names this SPEC ships; everything else in the Envoy scrape is ignored.

> **Phase 09 fault-stat route-A note (forward-pointer per ADR-0107).** Phase 09 takes route A for `fault.response_rl_injected` (emit a permanently-zero counter rather than omit the line) — the twin-series-discipline analog but with envoy-go-side emission. Reference Envoy v1.37.2 emits `envoy_http_fault_response_rl_injected{...}` even when `response_rate_limit` is unconfigured; envoy-go matches the surface so the differential allow-list does not have to per-line-skip. The 22-name table above reflects the route A choice. When `response_rate_limit` lands in a future phase, the same registered counter starts incrementing without any framework change.

> **Phase 15 bandwidth_limit twin-series histogram extension (per ADR-0138 §Decision (vi) + phase 15 SPEC §1.1 amendment 9 + §13.4):** Envoy v1.37.2 emits 2 UNCONDITIONAL transfer-duration histograms per active stat_prefix (`<prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.request_transfer_duration` + `<prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.response_transfer_duration`) — fire regardless of `enable_response_trailers` setting. envoy-go MVP per phase-06.1 "counters + gauges only" baseline emits NO histograms. Differential fixture 0017's `expectations.yaml` allow-lists both via this twin-series-filter discipline. Prometheus surface seen by operators: `envoy_<prefix>_http_bandwidth_limit_<dir>_transfer_duration_bucket{}` + `_sum` + `_count` series on Envoy side, ABSENT on envoy-go side. Future re-activation: histogram-emit-infra phase lands `*stats.Registry.Histogram` + Prometheus `histogram_*` extractor; `filterStats` extends with 2 histogram fields keyed by `stat_prefix`.

## Access log field mapping

*Introduced by phase 06.2. Justified by ADR-0066 (architecture: in-tree file sink + AsyncFileSink + drop-newest backpressure), ADR-0067 (reject log_format at parse), ADR-0068 (this subsection — three-tier per-record per-field equivalence matrix), ADR-0069 (server.accesslog_dropped counter naming).*

The access-log field mapping enumerates every operator in the Envoy default
access-log format (15 operators in identical positions on every record) per
ADR-0066, the per-operator equivalence tier per ADR-0068's three-tier matrix,
and the empirical-pin block recording the verbatim format-string shape from
reference Envoy v1.37.2. The differential equivalence claim (the
"Semantically equal after field-mapping" predicate from the Equivalence
Matrix row at line 18) IS the three-tier matrix below.

### 15-operator default format (per ADR-0066; empirical-pin in §11 of the 06.2 SPEC)

[<START_TIME>] "<:METHOD> <:PATH> <PROTOCOL>" <RESPONSE_CODE> <RESPONSE_FLAGS>
<BYTES_RECEIVED> <BYTES_SENT> <DURATION> <RESP-SVC-TIME> "<X-FORWARDED-FOR>"
"<USER-AGENT>" "<X-REQUEST-ID>" "<:AUTHORITY>" "<UPSTREAM_HOST>"

### Three-tier matrix (per ADR-0068)

Tier E (exact byte-equal cross-side; 7 operators):
  :METHOD, :PATH, PROTOCOL, RESPONSE_CODE, BYTES_SENT, USER-AGENT, :AUTHORITY

Tier F (format-only — parses to expected shape on both sides; cross-side value
not asserted equal; 3 operators):
  START_TIME (RFC3339 ms-precision UTC, within workload wall-clock window)
  DURATION (int ms ≥ 0)
  UPSTREAM_HOST (`<host>:<port>` for routed; `-` for direct_response)

Tier S (subject must emit `-`; reference unconstrained; 5 operators):
  RESPONSE_FLAGS, BYTES_RECEIVED, RESP(X-ENVOY-UPSTREAM-SERVICE-TIME),
  X-FORWARDED-FOR, X-REQUEST-ID

Counts: 7 + 3 + 5 = 15 (= the operator count in the format).

### X-ENVOY-ORIGINAL-PATH?:PATH fallback note (per 06.2 SPEC §6.1)

Operator #3 in the format is %REQ(X-ENVOY-ORIGINAL-PATH?:PATH)% — emit the
original-path header if present, else fall through to :PATH. Neither side
emits X-ENVOY-ORIGINAL-PATH on fixture 0006's workload (envoy-go does not
inject it; reference Envoy doesn't either, because fixture 0006 has no
path_rewrite-bearing route); both sides emit :PATH via the fallback. A
future phase introducing path-rewriting must re-evaluate fixture 0006's
Tier-E/F expectations under the new behavior.

- Sinks other than `envoy.access_loggers.file` + `envoy.access_loggers.http_grpc` + `envoy.access_loggers.open_telemetry` (stdout / tcp_grpc — silently-ignored per ADR-0041 06.2 amendment). The gRPC ALS sink (`http_grpc`) is SUPPORTED as of phase 44.1 (ADR-0255 — see `### Access log — gRPC Access Log Service (ALS) streaming sink` below). The OTLP sink (`open_telemetry`) is SUPPORTED as of phase 45.1 (ADR-0258 — see `### Access log — OpenTelemetry (OTLP) access-log sink` below).
- Per-route access-log filters (`access_log[].filter` — silently-ignored).
- Log rotation, fsync, durability ceilings (out of scope per SPEC §2.1).
- Trailers in access logs (deferred to gRPC family per ADR-0058).
- Access-log records for ctx-cancelled requests (skipped per the H2 zero-status sentinel, SPEC §2.1).
- SIGTERM-while-record-pending drain semantics (Phase 08's deliverable).

## Access log — gRPC Access Log Service (ALS) streaming sink

*Introduced by phase 44.1 (the Observability family's FIRST row, core leg). Justified by ADR-0255 (the gRPC ALS streaming sink — a `GrpcAccessLogSink` over a typed `ALSClient` over the phase-18 `grpcclient.Dialer`), composing on ADR-0066/0067 (the phase-06.2 `Sink` abstraction + the 10-field `Record`) + ADR-0158 (the `AuthClient` typed-wrapper precedent). Buffering (`buffer_size_bytes`/`buffer_flush_interval`) added at phase 44.2 (ADR-0256).*

**What triggers it.** An HCM `access_log[]` entry with `typed_config` = `envoy.extensions.access_loggers.grpc.v3.HttpGrpcAccessLogConfig`. The config is parsed into an `ALSConfig{ClusterName, LogName}` (`Bootstrap.ALSConfigs`), LIFTING gRPC ALS out of the ADR-0041 silent-ignore set. At boot, `main.go` dials `common_config.grpc_service.envoy_grpc.cluster_name` (an H2-required cluster) via the `grpcclient.Dialer`, builds an `ALSClient` + a `GrpcAccessLogSink`, and appends the sink to the existing `sinks` list (alongside any file sink). The sink fires on every request regardless of downstream codec (the access log is emitted from the HCM emit hooks, not codec-gated).

**The streamed structured fields.** The sink opens `AccessLogService.StreamAccessLogs` lazily (on the first record), sends `identifier { node, log_name }` ONCE per stream (identifier-once; `node` sourced nil-safe from `bootstrap.node.id`/`.cluster`), then streams events as structured `HTTPAccessLogEntry`s batched per the buffer policy (§The buffer machinery below). The 10-field `Record`→`HTTPAccessLogEntry` mapping populates: `common_properties` (`start_time`, `duration`, `upstream_remote_address`); the top-level `protocol_version` ENUM (`Record.Protocol` string → `HTTPAccessLogEntry_HTTPVersion`; `HTTP/1.1`→`HTTP11`); `request` (`request_method` enum, `path`, `authority`, `user_agent`); `response` (`response_code`, `response_body_bytes`). On a `Send` error the writer reconnects + re-sends the record once (re-arming the identifier) before dropping it (logged, not counted).

**The buffer machinery (44.2, ADR-0256 — `buffer_size_bytes`/`buffer_flush_interval`).** The writer goroutine ACCUMULATES `HTTPAccessLogEntry`s into a pending buffer (tracking the running sum of per-entry serialized bytes, `proto.Size(entry)` == the C++ `ByteSizeLong`) and flushes the whole batch — all pending entries in one `StreamAccessLogsMessage.http_logs.log_entry[]` — on EITHER the byte-sum reaching `buffer_size_bytes` (the SIZE trigger; the crossing entry is INCLUDED) OR a `buffer_flush_interval` timer elapsing (the TIMER trigger), whichever fires first (AMEND-BUF-1). Defaults: `buffer_size_bytes` **16384** (wrapper-absent), `buffer_flush_interval` **1s** (absent/zero — a hard `time.NewTicker(<=0)` panic-guard coerced at the parse layer); an EXPLICIT `buffer_size_bytes: 0` degenerates to flush-every-entry (which is the 44.1 fixed-flush behavior, AMEND-BUF-2). `logs_written` increments by `len(buf)` per flush — it counts ENTRIES, BATCH-INVARIANT (NOT once per message, AMEND-BUF-4). On `Close`, the pending buffer is FLUSHED before `CloseAndRecv` (AMEND-BUF-5 — no entry already handed to the sink is silently dropped at shutdown). On a stream-OPEN failure or a SECOND consecutive `Send` failure the whole pending batch is DROPPED (logged, NOT counted — bounding memory under a sustained receiver outage; matches the 44.1 open-failure-drops policy). envoy-go's sink is PROCESS-GLOBAL (one buffer); the reference buffers PER-WORKER-THREAD — a legitimate framing divergence, so the `0082-grpc-access-log-buffering` differential asserts the per-entry payload aggregated across messages + a subject-side `maxBatchSize >= 2` batching proof (AMEND-BUF-3).

**The header capture (44.3, ADR-0257 — `additional_{request,response}_headers_to_log`).** The sink captures the configured request/response header VALUES at the HCM emit hooks into the entry's `request.request_headers` / `response.response_headers` `map<string,string>` (lowercase KEY, verbatim VALUE; missing ⇒ OMITTED, present-empty ⇒ empty-string entry [presence is the discriminator]; multi-value ⇒ comma-joined in wire order — AMEND-HDR-1/2/3). Each configured header NAME is lowercased ONCE at parse time into `ALSConfig.{Request,Response}HeaderNames`; the HCM filter captures the UNION of all gRPC-ALS sinks' configured names into a `Record` two-map extension (allocated ONLY when the union is non-empty — so when NO sink configures additional headers, incl. `0081`/`0082`, the maps stay nil and the emitted proto is byte-identical), and `buildHTTPAccessLogEntry` maps each sink's OWN configured subset out of the union (per-sink fan-out correct). The response-header capture reads the FINAL DOWNSTREAM response (the Envoy-mutated `server: envoy` etc.), so the `0083-grpc-access-log-headers` differential captures BACKEND-ORIGIN headers only (`content-type`), avoiding the Envoy-synthesized `server`/`date`/`x-envoy-*` that differ side-to-side (AMEND-HDR-4 — the header-capture analog of the query-less constraint). NO header-capture stat (surface UNCHANGED at 1189, AMEND-HDR-5). **Known departure (H1):** a configured `additional_request_headers_to_log` name of `host` is NOT captured on the HTTP/1.1 path — Go's net/http promotes the Host into `Request.Host` (out of `Request.Header`), so the header lookup omits it; the authority is already surfaced as the first-class `request.authority` field. (The HTTP/2 path scans `:authority`/headers directly and is unaffected.)

**The query-less FAITHFUL constraint (AMEND-ALS-2).** `request.path` is PATH-ONLY: envoy-go's `Record.Path = r.URL.Path` carries no query string, whereas the reference's `request.path` includes the query. The `0081-grpc-access-log` differential drives a query-less path to keep the field cross-side EXACT — a documented faithful constraint, NOT a behavior bug.

**The cross-side-assertable subset (AMEND-ALS-3/4).** Stream/message FRAMING legitimately varies side-to-side (the reference opens a fresh stream per sequential request + reuses/batches under burst; envoy-go uses one reused identifier-once stream) — so the differential asserts the per-entry PAYLOAD aggregated across messages, NOT framing. The deterministic cross-side-EXACT subset is 7 structured fields: `request.{request_method, path[query-less], authority, user_agent}` + `response.{response_code, response_body_bytes}` + the top-level `protocol_version` (`HTTP11`). The `common_properties.{start_time, duration, upstream_remote_address}` + subject-absent reference fields (`scheme`/`request_id`/`upstream_cluster`/`access_log_type`/`response_code_details`/wire-byte counts) stay UNasserted.

**STRICT-REJECT set (ADR-0080).** Boot is rejected for: `tcp_logs`/`TcpGrpcAccessLogConfig` (TCP ALS unsupported), a non-V3 `transport_api_version`, `google_grpc` (only `envoy_grpc` is supported), and an empty `cluster_name`.

**The 2 stats (AMEND-ALS-1).** `access_logs.grpc_access_log.logs_written` (counter — ++ per entry successfully `Send`'d, BATCH-INVARIANT under buffering: `Add(len(buf))` per flush) + `access_logs.grpc_access_log.logs_dropped` (counter — ++ per channel-full overflow drop, the drop-newest backpressure idiom). Process-global STATIC names (NOT `log_name`-scoped, NOT cluster-gated) ⇒ +2 to BOTH the H2 (1189) and non-H2 (1185) stat-surface totals. `logs_dropped` counts channel-full overflow ONLY (a post-reconnect-failure loss is logged, not counted).

**PARSE-ACCEPT-but-INERT (deferred to later legs).** `additional_{request,response}_trailers_to_log` and `AccessLog.filter` are accepted at parse but have no runtime effect (a strict-reject-until-the-leg posture would fail-boot a real operator config — a worse divergence). (`buffer_size_bytes`/`buffer_flush_interval` were INERT at 44.1 and are now SUPPORTED as of 44.2 — see §The buffer machinery. `additional_{request,response}_headers_to_log` were INERT through 44.2 and are now SUPPORTED as of 44.3 — see §The header capture.)

### Applies to
- Phase 44.1 onward (the gRPC ALS streaming sink — `internal/accesslog/grpcsink.go`/`mapping.go`/`stats.go` + `internal/grpcclient` `ALSClient` + the `internal/bootstrap` `ALSConfig` parse arm + the `main.go` wiring), exercised via fixture `0081-grpc-access-log` (cross-side EXACT, driver-owned `accessloggrpc` receiver) + the `internal/accesslog` unit tests (including the full-package `-race` writer-goroutine gate).
- Phase 44.2 onward (the `buffer_size_bytes`/`buffer_flush_interval` flush triggers — the buffer machinery in `GrpcAccessLogSink.run()` + the `ALSConfig` buffer fields + the `accessloggrpc` batch exposure), exercised via fixture `0082-grpc-access-log-buffering` (cross-side aggregated payload + subject-side `maxBatchSize >= 2`).
- Phase 44.3 onward (the `additional_{request,response}_headers_to_log` header capture — the `ALSConfig` header-name lists + the `Record` two-map extension + the `accesslog.CaptureHeaders` helper + the HCM emit-hook capture/response-threading + the per-sink `buildHTTPAccessLogEntry` filter), exercised via fixture `0083-grpc-access-log-headers` (cross-side EXACT captured request maps + `content-type` response map + the absent-name OMIT proof).

### Does not yet apply to
- `additional_{request,response}_trailers_to_log` trailer capture (PARSE-ACCEPT-but-INERT).
- `AccessLog.filter` per-log filters (PARSE-ACCEPT-but-INERT).
- TCP ALS (`tcp_logs`/`TcpGrpcAccessLogConfig`), non-V3 transport, `google_grpc` (all STRICT-REJECT at boot).
- The query string on `request.path` (envoy-go `Record.Path` is path-only — AMEND-ALS-2 faithful constraint).
- Full `AccessLogCommon` population, `request_trailers` (future Observability rows). (The OTLP access logger is SUPPORTED as of phase 45.1 — see `### Access log — OpenTelemetry (OTLP) access-log sink` below.)

## Access log — OpenTelemetry (OTLP) access-log sink

*Introduced by phase 45.1 (the Observability family's SECOND row, core leg). Justified by ADR-0258 (the OTLP access-log streaming sink — an `OTLPAccessLogSink` over a typed `OTLPLogsClient` UNARY wrapper over the phase-18 `grpcclient.Dialer`), composing on ADR-0066/0067 (the phase-06.2 `Sink` abstraction + the `Record`) + ADR-0158 (the typed-wrapper precedent) + ADR-0255/0256 (the phase-44 gRPC-ALS sink/buffer machinery reused). The project's THIRD `accesslog.Sink` and FIRST consumer of an out-of-tree proto module (`go.opentelemetry.io/proto/otlp`, promoted transitive→direct).*

**What triggers it.** An HCM `access_log[]` entry with `typed_config` = `envoy.extensions.access_loggers.open_telemetry.v3.OpenTelemetryAccessLogConfig`. The config is parsed into an `OTLPConfig{ClusterName, LogName, BufferSizeBytes, BufferFlushInterval, DisableBuiltinLabels}` (`Bootstrap.OTLPConfigs`), LIFTING OTLP out of the ADR-0041 silent-ignore set (via the shared `parseCommonGrpcAccessLogConfig` helper refactor-extracted from the phase-44 ALS parse path). At boot, `main.go` dials `common_config.grpc_service.envoy_grpc.cluster_name` (an H2-required cluster) via the `grpcclient.Dialer` (HOISTED to fire when EITHER the ALS or OTLP family is configured — an OTLP-only boot still gets a Dialer), builds an `OTLPLogsClient` + an `OTLPAccessLogSink`, and appends the sink to the existing `sinks` list (alongside any file / gRPC-ALS sink). The sink fires on every request regardless of downstream codec.

**The built-in mapping (the LEAN record — D-OTLP-BUILTINS).** The 2026-06-26 live probe (contrib-v1.37.2) pinned a LEANER built-in record than the brainstorm assumed: the pure built-in `LogRecord` carries ONLY `time_unix_nano` (= `Record.StartTime.UnixNano()`) — NO `observed_time`, severity, body, or `LogRecord.attributes` (those are 45.2 operator templating). The "built-in labels" are 4 `Resource.attributes`, ALWAYS all four keys in a fixed order: `log_name`, `zone_name` (= `node.locality.zone`), `cluster_name` (= `node.cluster`), `node_name` (= `node.id`). `disable_builtin_labels: true` drops them ALL wholesale (an empty `Resource`) — all-or-nothing, NOT per-label. There is NO built-in method/path/severity mapping.

**The Export envelope + the UNARY RPC.** The sink BATCHES `LogRecord`s and Exports a batch as ONE `ExportLogsServiceRequest` over the UNARY `opentelemetry.proto.collector.logs.v1.LogsService.Export` RPC (no stream, no identifier, no `CloseAndRecv` — simpler than the gRPC-ALS streaming sink). The envelope is one `ResourceLogs` (Resource = the built-in labels) → one `ScopeLogs` (Scope ABSENT) → the batched `LogRecord`s.

**The buffer machinery (the reused 44.2 fields).** The writer goroutine ACCUMULATES `LogRecord`s into a pending buffer (tracking the running sum of `proto.Size(lr)`) and flushes the whole batch — one `Export` — on the FIRST of three triggers: the byte-sum reaching `buffer_size_bytes` (the SIZE trigger; an EXPLICIT `0` ⇒ flush-every-entry), a `buffer_flush_interval` timer elapsing (the TIMER trigger), or `Close` draining the pending buffer. Defaults: `buffer_size_bytes` **16384**, `buffer_flush_interval` **1s** (the `<=0` `time.NewTicker` panic-guard coerced at the parse layer). On an `Export` error the writer retries the WHOLE batch ONCE; a second consecutive failure drops the batch (logged, NOT counted — bounding memory under a sustained outage). `logs_written` increments by `len(buf)` per successful flush — it counts RECORDS, BATCH-INVARIANT. On a channel-full `Submit` the new record is dropped (drop-newest), `logs_dropped` Inc'd, with a rate-limited diagnostic. `Close` flushes the pending buffer (within `closeDrainGrace`) then cancels the `Export` ctx for bounded shutdown.

**STRICT-REJECT set (ADR-0080).** Boot is rejected for: a non-V3 `transport_api_version`, `google_grpc` (only `envoy_grpc` is supported), an empty `cluster_name`, AND `formatters` (custom formatter extensions, out of scope — STAYS rejected at 45.2). As of phase 45.2 (ADR-0259) `body` / `attributes` / `resource_attributes` are LIVE (no longer rejected — see "The operator engine" below), but two NEW parse-time rejects fire: an operator outside the curated `Record`-mapped set (in a `body`/`attributes` template), and a non-`string`/`kvlist`/`array` `AnyValue` value-type (`int_value`/`bool_value`/`double_value`/`bytes_value`) in any of `body`/`attributes`/`resource_attributes`.

**The operator engine (45.2 — ADR-0259).** `body` (an `AnyValue`) and each `attributes` value (a `KeyValueList`) are PER-RECORD command-operator-templated against the access-log `Record` (the curated operator set = `%START_TIME%` / `%REQ(:METHOD|:PATH|:AUTHORITY|USER-AGENT)%` / `%PROTOCOL%` / `%RESPONSE_CODE%` / `%BYTES_SENT%` / `%DURATION%` / `%UPSTREAM_HOST%`) and emitted as `LogRecord.body` / `LogRecord.attributes`. A value may be a `string` OR a nested `kvlist`/`array`, recursively substituted at every `string` leaf (structure preserved); every substituted leaf is emitted as `stringValue` (no typed-int promotion — matching the reference). Config `int`/`bool`/`double`/`bytes` value-types STRICT-REJECT at parse; operators OUTSIDE the curated set STRICT-REJECT at parse (a documented envoy-go-strict departure — some valid-Envoy operators boot-reject in envoy-go; the mirror of the reference's own unknown-operator boot-reject; `%REQ(USER-AGENT)%` is the only header operator; `%REQ(:PATH)%` is query-stripped under H1, a documented departure). `resource_attributes` (a `KeyValueList`) are emitted as extra `Resource.attributes` — LITERAL (request operators pass through verbatim — resource scope, built once per logger), appended AFTER the 4 built-in labels and SURVIVING `disable_builtin_labels` (which gates ONLY the 4 built-ins). The stat surface is UNCHANGED (1191 — the operator engine adds NO stat).

**The 2 stats (AMEND-OTLP-STATS).** `access_logs.open_telemetry_access_log.logs_written` (counter — ++ per record successfully Exported, BATCH-INVARIANT: `Add(len(buf))` per flush) + `access_logs.open_telemetry_access_log.logs_dropped` (counter — ++ per channel-full overflow drop). Process-global STATIC names (NOT `log_name`-scoped, NOT cluster-gated) ⇒ +2 to BOTH the H2 (1191) and non-H2 (1187) stat-surface totals. The OTLP sink owns its OWN `logs_dropped` (NOT a reuse of the gRPC-ALS counter).

**PARSE-ACCEPT-but-INERT.** `stat_prefix` (field 6) is read-and-ignored (no per-sink stat scoping yet — a strict-reject would fail-boot a real operator config).

**The cross-side-assertable subset.** The Export RPC framing legitimately varies side-to-side, so the `0084-otlp-access-log` differential asserts the per-record PAYLOAD aggregated across messages, NOT framing (AMEND-ALS-3 carried forward): the record COUNT + the `time_unix_nano` PRESENCE (the VALUE is non-deterministic) + the 4 `Resource` label KEYS + the `log_name` VALUE.

### Applies to
- Phase 45.1 onward (the OTLP access-log streaming sink — `internal/accesslog/otlpsink.go`/`otlpmapping.go`/`stats.go` + `internal/grpcclient` `OTLPLogsClient` + the `internal/bootstrap` `OTLPConfig` parse arm + the shared `parseCommonGrpcAccessLogConfig` helper + the `main.go` wiring), exercised via fixture `0084-otlp-access-log` (cross-side EXACT, driver-owned `test/helpers/otlplogs` receiver) + the `internal/accesslog` unit tests (including the `disable_builtin_labels` arm + the full-package `-race` writer-goroutine gate).
- Phase 45.2 onward (the operator engine — `internal/accesslog/otlpformat.go`: the registry + `CompileOTLPTemplate`/`CompileOTLPValue`/`ValidateOTLPValue` + per-record `Eval` over the `AnyValue` tree; the exported `OTLPTemplate`/`OTLPValueTemplate`/`OTLPAttrTemplate`; the lifted parse arms + the `buildLogRecord`/`buildResource` extensions + the grown `NewOTLPAccessLogSink` signature), exercised via fixture `0085-otlp-access-log-operators` (cross-side EXACT on the templated `body` + `attributes` incl. nested `kvlist`/`array` + the literal `resource_attributes` pass-through) + the `FuzzCompileOTLPValue` fuzzer + the subject-side `disable_builtin_labels`-survival / unsupported-operator / bad-value-type unit tests.

### Does not yet apply to
- `stat_prefix` honoring (PARSE-ACCEPT-but-INERT).
- Operators outside the curated `Record`-mapped set + arbitrary `%REQ()%`/`%RESP()%` header operators beyond `%REQ(USER-AGENT)%` (STRICT-REJECT at boot — a documented envoy-go-strict departure; widening the set needs new `Record` fields + emit-hook plumbing).
- `formatters` (custom formatter extensions — STRICT-REJECT at boot, out of scope).
- non-V3 transport, `google_grpc` (STRICT-REJECT at boot).

## Request tracing — sampling/request-id engine + span emission + OTLP export

*Introduced by phase 46.1a (the header-engine sub-leg) and completed by phase 46.1b (the span emission + OTLP export sub-leg) — together the 46.1 (core+OTLP) leg of the Observability family's THIRD row. CLOSES ADR-0260 (§Context drafted at SPEC-46.1 §13; §Decision/§Consequences body at the 46.1b IMPL). The project's FIRST request-tracing subsystem and FIRST genuinely-new request-path Go package (`internal/tracing`) in a long stretch; ZERO new go.mod modules (the trace config protos resolve at the already-present `go.opentelemetry.io/proto/otlp v1.0.0` and `go-control-plane/envoy v1.32.4`).*

**What triggers it.** An HCM `tracing` block whose `provider` is the OpenTelemetry tracer (`envoy.config.trace.v3.OpenTelemetryConfig`). The block is parsed in the HCM filter (`internal/filter/hcm/config.go:parseFilterWithCtx`, NOT `bootstrap.go` — D-TRACE-CONFIG-HOME) into a `tracing.TracingConfig{ClientSampling, RandomSampling, OverallSampling float64; ServiceName, ClusterName string}` on the `Filter` (alongside a `*tracing.HCMCounters` + a `tracing.RandSource` = `tracing.CryptoRand{}`), LIFTING the HCM `tracing` field out of the ADR-0041 silent-ignore set. The three `Percent` knobs default to **100.0** when absent (an explicit `0` is a valid 0% and is preserved). The `ServiceName`/`ClusterName` are stored for the 46.1b exporter/Resource and are UNUSED at 46.1a (no collector is dialed yet; the cluster need not resolve at 46.1a). Byte-identical to before when no HCM `tracing` provider is configured — the engine is dormant and registers no counters (the full 88-dir differential is the regression anchor).

**The per-request decision (the §11 live-probe precedence — `tracing.Decide`, a pure `(http.Header, *TracingConfig, RandSource) → Decision`).** Run at the HCM dispatch seam (H1 `connection.go`, H2 `h2dispatch.go`), guarded by `if f.tracingConfig != nil`:
1. An incoming **W3C `traceparent`** (valid `00-<32hex trace>-<16hex parent>-<2hex flags>`, all-zero trace-id/parent-id rejected) ⇒ CONTINUE: keep its trace-id, set the new span's parent = the incoming parent-id, `Sample` = its sampled-bit — AUTHORITATIVE, bypassing the local `random_sampling`/`overall_sampling` caps. Decision class `not_traceable`.
2. else **`x-client-trace-id`** present AND a `Float64` roll `< client_sampling` ⇒ FORCE: sampled, class `client_enabled`.
3. else **`random_sampling`** roll decides; class `random_sampling`. (A suppressed client-force — `client_sampling=0` — falls THROUGH to this random roll.)
4. THEN **`overall_sampling`** caps the LOCALLY-decided sample (steps 2–3 only, NOT a continued trace); `overall=0` suppresses BOTH random and client-force.

**`x-request-id` generation + the byte-14 trace-reason stamp (D-TRACE-REQUESTID).** The request gets an `x-request-id` REGARDLESS of the sampling decision — GENERATED when absent (a canonical lowercase UUIDv4) or PRESERVED-verbatim-and-stamped when present (ONLY canonical string index 14 — the version-nibble char — overwritten). Index 14 encodes the trace reason: **`4` = NoTrace** / **`9` = Sampled** (random/overall) / **`b` = Client** (`x-client-trace-id` force). The new `x-request-id` + a W3C `traceparent` (`00-<trace>-<fresh span>-<flags>`) + a verbatim `tracestate` pass-through are INJECTED toward the upstream at the dispatch seam — REVISING the `router.go:763` no-`x-request-id` invariant, but ONLY under a configured provider (the router itself still injects nothing; the HCM tracing engine does).

**STRICT-REJECT set (ADR-0080) — envoy-go-strict departs from the PERMISSIVE reference.** The reference boots permissively (silently ignoring most unsupported tracing knobs); envoy-go-strict ACCEPTs only the 3 `Percent` knobs + the OTel provider's `grpc_service.envoy_grpc.cluster_name` + `service_name`, and STRICT-REJECTs at parse: a non-OpenTelemetry provider, `google_grpc` transport, an empty `cluster_name`, `custom_tags`, `verbose`, `max_path_tag_length`, a PRESENT `spawn_upstream_span` (non-nil, even `false` — D-TRACE-SPAWN-UPSTREAM-SPAN), and the OTel `http_service`/`resource_detectors`/`sampler` sub-fields.

**The 5 stats (D-TRACE-STATS).** 5 HCM-scoped counters `http.<stat_prefix>.tracing.{client_enabled, health_check, not_traceable, random_sampling, service_forced}`, registered in `parseFilterWithCtx` (the shared `http.<stat_prefix>.` prefix is already `IsValidName`-guarded for the `downstream_rq_*` block). `client_enabled` / `not_traceable` / `random_sampling` are LIVE (the §11 decision classes); `health_check` + `service_forced` register but stay 0 at 46.1a (no health-check detection / `x-envoy-force-trace` honoring in scope). The counters are DYNAMIC — they register ONLY under a configured tracing HCM ⇒ +5 to BOTH the H2 (1191 → **1196**) and non-H2 (1187 → **1192**) stat-surface totals when tracing is configured. The 2 tracer-scoped `tracing.opentelemetry.{spans_sent,spans_dropped}` counters are 46.1b (+2 → **1198** H2 / **1194** non-H2 — LAZILY registered, only when ≥1 exporter builds at filter-parse).

**The cross-side-assertable subset (`0086-tracing-request-id`).** The random `x-request-id`/`traceparent`/span-id VALUES vary, so the differential asserts STRUCTURE — all CROSS-SIDE EXACT: each forwarded plain-request `x-request-id` is 36-char UUID-shaped with index-14 `9` (Sampled) and a `00-<32hex>-<16hex>-01` `traceparent`; each continuation request CONTINUES the inbound trace-id AND its `x-request-id` carries index-14 `9` (the inbound `traceparent` flags `01` ⇒ the trace IS sampled ⇒ the reason nibble reflects that — see the note below); the subject-side counters are `random_sampling == numPlain`, `not_traceable == numCont`, the other three `0`. **SPEC §11 probe-error correction (IMPL Task 10b):** the SPEC §11 pin read "a continued trace keeps nibble `4`," but the live `0086` re-probe showed the reference stamps the CONTINUATION `x-request-id` nibble `9` for an inbound-SAMPLED trace (the `x-request-id` reason reflects the actual SAMPLE STATUS, NOT the local-vs-continued provenance). envoy-go's engine was corrected to MATCH (continued+sampled ⇒ reason `Sampled`/`9`; continued+not-sampled ⇒ `NoTrace`/`4`) — so the continuation nibble is now CROSS-SIDE EXACT, NOT a departure. The decision CLASS (the counter) stays `not_traceable` for a continued trace (the counter reflects the local-decision provenance; the nibble reflects the sampled status — two distinct axes).

### — span emission + OTLP export (phase 46.1b)

*Introduced by phase 46.1b (the completing sub-leg of the 46.1 core+OTLP leg). CLOSES ADR-0260.*

**What it adds.** When a sampled `Decision` reaches the `accesslog_emit.go` seam and `f.exporter != nil`: `BuildServerSpan(dec, inputs)` constructs a `Span` (the 16 built-in attrs; start = dispatch time from `Decision`, end = stream-complete time), then `f.exporter.Submit(span)` queues it for export. This runs at FUNCTION HEAD — BEFORE the `len(f.accessLog)==0` early-return (a tracing HCM typically has no `access_log` block). Not-sampled requests (`!dec.Sample`) skip the build call entirely.

**The 16 built-in span attributes (all STRING per `reference_wire_format_both_sides_see_same_bytes`).** `http.url`, `http.method`, `http.protocol`, `http.status_code`, `http.request_size`, `http.response_size`, `http.user_agent`, `peer.address` (upstream host), `upstream_cluster`, `upstream_cluster.name`, `node_id`, `zone`, `guid:x-request-id`, `http.host`, `component` (fixed `"proxy"`), `downstream_cluster` (fixed `"-"`). The reference cpp OTel tracer (`contrib-v1.37.2`) emits `http.status_code`/`request_size`/`response_size` as STRING `AnyValue`s; envoy-go matches the wire format. **`upstream_cluster`/`upstream_cluster.name` carry empty values** — the upstream cluster NAME is NOT plumbed to the emit seam in envoy-go (the same documented framework gap as the Lua bridge's `UpstreamCluster()` returning `""`); these attr KEYS are always present; the `0087` differential does NOT assert them cross-side by value. A coverage boundary; revisit if/when the framework plumbs upstream-cluster identity to stream-completion.

**The `OTLPExporter` + `ExporterProvider`.** The `OTLPExporter` (`internal/tracing/exporter.go`) mirrors `OTLPAccessLogSink` — bounded channel (4096) + writer goroutine + size/interval/close buffering + retry-once + drop-newest; flushes span protos over the UNARY `TraceService.Export` via the `OTLPTracesClient` typed wrapper (`internal/grpcclient/grpcclient.go`, the `OTLPLogsClient` precedent). The `ExporterProvider` is per-bootstrap process-singleton built UNCONDITIONALLY at boot (INERT until `ExporterFor` runs at filter-parse); it memoizes one `OTLPExporter` per cluster by `sync.Once`, lazily registering `tracing.opentelemetry.{spans_sent,spans_dropped}` on first use (keeping the no-tracing baseline byte-stable).

**The `log.Fatalf` collector-cluster gate (envoy-go-strict departure — AMEND-TRACE-NO-BOOT-REJECT).** A missing or non-H2 collector cluster in the HCM `tracing` block surfaces as a parse error bubbled from `ExporterFor` at listener-manager construction (`hcm: tracing exporter: …` → `log.Fatalf`). The reference boots permissively (silently ignoring a missing collector). The envoy-go-strict fail-fast departure per ADR-0080.

**The 2 tracer-scoped counters (+2 → 1198).** `tracing.opentelemetry.spans_sent` (counter — BATCH-INVARIANT `Add(len(buf))` per successful `Export` flush) + `tracing.opentelemetry.spans_dropped` (counter — ++ per channel-full overflow drop). Process-global STATIC names, LAZILY registered (only when ≥1 exporter builds). +2 to BOTH H2 (**1196 → 1198**) and non-H2 (**1192 → 1194**) stat-surface totals ONLY when tracing is configured.

**The `0087-tracing-otlp` differential.** Cross-side asserts: span COUNT; `name == "ingress"`; `kind == SPAN_KIND_SERVER`; `trace_id` PRESENT; `parent_span_id` PRESENT on continuation spans (the W3C `traceparent` prong); the 14 cross-side-stable attr KEYS present (the two `upstream_cluster*` attrs are key-present, value OMITTED). Subject-side: `spans_sent >= N` + `spans_dropped == 0`. Four deliberate breaks + the not-sampled negative (unit tests). 20/20 flake-gate GREEN; full-package `-race` clean.

**The no-route-match (404) path injection-gap (deferred follow-on).** The 46.1b emit seam passes `nil` decision for pre-route-match failures (consistent with 46.1a) ⇒ no span built. A known parity boundary — reference Envoy generates `x-request-id` at the connection-manager layer regardless of route match. To revisit at 46.2.

### Request tracing — Zipkin tracing provider + B3 propagation

*Introduced by phase 46.2 (the SECOND-and-FINAL chartered tracing leg — the Zipkin provider + B3 propagation, the by-exporter split's second leg). ANCHORS ADR-0261. The project's SECOND tracing exporter and FIRST non-gRPC tracing exporter — and the FIRST consumer of the phase-22 `httpclient.ClusterDispatch` HTTP-over-cluster primitive (ADR-0177) outside the Lua/wasm `httpCall` surface. ZERO new Go packages (all within `internal/tracing`), ZERO new go.mod modules (the v2 JSON is stdlib `encoding/json`; `ZipkinConfig` resolves at the already-imported `config/trace/v3`).*

**What triggers it.** An HCM `tracing` block whose `provider` is the Zipkin tracer (`envoy.config.trace.v3.ZipkinConfig`). The `NewConfig` provider dispatch routes the OTel `typed_config` to the existing OTLP path and the Zipkin `typed_config` to a new Zipkin arm (a `ProviderKind` discriminant + a `ZipkinSettings` sub-struct on `TracingConfig`; `ClusterName` reused for the `collector_cluster`).

**The provider-agnostic decision is REUSED.** A Zipkin-provider HCM runs the SAME full-fidelity sampling/request-id decision the 46.1a engine produces (the `x-request-id` byte-14 trace-reason, the three `Percent` knobs, the incoming-context-continues-authoritatively precedence) and builds the SAME per-request SERVER `Span` (start at dispatch, end at the `accesslog_emit.go` seam). 46.2 changes ONLY the propagation codec, the export transport/wire, and the span `name`.

**B3 propagation (the W3C `traceparent` analog).** The trace context is extracted/continued/injected in **B3** instead of `traceparent`: EXTRACT accepts EITHER the single `b3` header (`<traceid>-<spanid>-<sampled>[-<parentspanid>]`, 64-or-128-bit traceid) OR the multi-header `X-B3-{TraceId,SpanId,ParentSpanId,Sampled,Flags}` set; INJECT toward the upstream is the MULTI-HEADER `X-B3-*` set (`X-B3-TraceId`/`X-B3-SpanId`/`X-B3-Sampled` + `X-B3-ParentSpanId` only when continued). **The incoming SPAN-id becomes our continued server span's parent** (the 4th `b3` field / `X-B3-ParentSpanId` is accepted-but-ignored as the caller's grandparent, per SPEC §11 D-TRACE-ZIPKIN-B3). The extract is a wire-derived untrusted-input boundary — `FuzzExtractB3` (fuzzers 48 → 49). The `DecideWithContext` seam lifts the trace-context extract to the HCM caller (codec-dispatched: `ExtractB3` vs `ExtractTraceparent`); `Decide` stays a thin `traceparent` wrapper — byte-stable.

**The Zipkin v2 JSON export (the `toProto` analog).** Each sampled span is EXPORTED as a Zipkin **v2 JSON** span — `name` = the request authority (the provider-neutral `Span.Authority`; the OTLP encoder keeps the `"ingress"` constant), `kind:"SERVER"`, `timestamp`/`duration` in MICROseconds, 14 STRING `tags` (the OTLP-16 roster MINUS `node_id`/`zone`), `shared`/`parentId` per `shared_span_context` (`shared_span_context:true` [the Envoy default] ⇒ the server span REUSES the incoming span-id as its own `id` + `"shared":true` + no `parentId`; `:false` ⇒ a child `id` + `parentId` = the incoming span-id). A batch is a JSON ARRAY POSTed over an HTTP/1 `POST <collector_endpoint>` (`Content-Type: application/json`) to the `collector_cluster` via `httpclient.ClusterDispatch` (the `ZipkinExporter` — bounded channel + writer goroutine + retry-once + drop-newest, the `OTLPExporter` shape). The POST `Host` is `collector_hostname` when set, else the `collector_cluster` name. The `upstream_cluster`/`upstream_cluster.name` (framework gap — `reference_tracing_upstream_cluster_framework_gap`) and `peer.address` (env-specific) tags emit but are value-UNasserted cross-side.

**STRICT-REJECT set (ADR-0080).** `collector_endpoint_version` ≠ `HTTP_JSON` (`HTTP_PROTO`/`GRPC`/the deprecated `0` — each its own reject arm), `split_spans_for_request == true`, and an empty `collector_cluster` are STRICT-REJECTed at parse (plus the SHARED HCM-level rejects carried from 46.1a).

**The `log.Fatalf` collector-cluster boot-reject (REFERENCE-PARITY — NOT a departure).** A missing collector cluster `log.Fatalf`-rejects at exporter build (the `ExporterProvider` Zipkin arm's `HasCluster` pre-check). UNLIKE the permissive OTLP boot (AMEND-TRACE-NO-BOOT-REJECT, an envoy-go-strict departure), the reference Envoy ALSO boot-rejects a missing Zipkin collector cluster (`envoy.tracers.zipkin: unknown cluster '<name>' initializing config` → exit 1), so envoy-go's cluster-exists gate is reference-parity here.

**The 2 tracer-scoped counters (+2 → 1200).** `tracing.zipkin.spans_sent` (counter — BATCH-INVARIANT `Add(len(buf))` per successful 2xx POST) + `tracing.zipkin.spans_dropped` (counter — ++ per channel-full overflow drop). Process-global STATIC names, LAZILY registered (only when ≥1 Zipkin exporter builds). +2 to BOTH the H2 (**1198 → 1200**) and non-H2 (**1194 → 1196**) stat-surface totals ONLY when a Zipkin provider is configured (the no-tracing baseline stays byte-stable).

**The `0088-tracing-zipkin` differential.** Cross-side EXACT (poll-to-converge, aggregated per-span over a driver-owned `test/helpers/zipkincollector` HTTP receiver): span COUNT; `name == <fixed authority>`; `kind == "SERVER"`; `timestamp>0`/`duration>0`; the deterministic VALUE-assertable tag subset; the B3 continuation prong (a fixed incoming trace-id ⇒ every span's `traceId` == it + the `shared`/`parentId` model per `shared_span_context`). UNasserted: `traceId`/`id` VALUES (except the continuation prong), timing VALUES, `localEndpoint`, POST framing. Four deliberate breaks all LIVE (`-count=1`); 20/20 flake-soak GREEN; full-package `-race` clean (`internal/tracing` + `internal/filter/hcm`).

### Applies to
- Phase 46.1a onward (the header-level tracing engine — the new `internal/tracing` package [`config.go` (`TracingConfig` + `NewConfig` + the 8 STRICT-REJECT arms) · `rand.go` (the `RandSource` seam + `CryptoRand`) · `requestid.go` (UUID generate/preserve/byte-14 stamp) · `propagation.go` (W3C `traceparent`/`tracestate` extract/inject) · `decision.go` (`Decide` — the full sampling precedence) · `stats.go` (`HCMCounters`)] + the HCM-filter parse arm + the H1/H2 dispatch wiring + the `config/trace/v3` blank-import), exercised via fixture `0086-tracing-request-id` (cross-side `x-request-id` nibble + `traceparent` continuation via the `HTTPHeaderMutation` echo backend + subject-side `tracing.*` counters) + the `internal/tracing` unit tests (decision precedence / request-id / propagation / config-reject / counter registration) + `FuzzStampRequestID` + `FuzzExtractTraceparent` + the HCM parse/dispatch unit tests (H1+H2; the no-tracing byte-stable guard).
- Phase 46.1b onward (the span emission + OTLP export sub-leg — `internal/tracing/span.go` [`Span`/`KV`/`SpanInputs`/`BuildServerSpan`/`toProto`] + `internal/tracing/exporter.go` [`OTLPExporter` bounded-channel sink + `Exporter` interface + `ExporterProvider` memoized-per-cluster + `TracesClient` seam] + `internal/tracing/stats.go` [`tracing.opentelemetry.{spans_sent,spans_dropped}` lazy counters] + `internal/grpcclient` [`OTLPTracesClient` UNARY wrapper] + the HCM `builtins.Deps.TracingExporters` threading + the `accesslog_emit.go` span-end wiring + `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` boot wiring), exercised via fixture `0087-tracing-otlp` (cross-side span count + `ingress`/SERVER + `trace_id`/`parent_span_id` + 14 attr keys, driver-owned `test/helpers/otlptrace` receiver) + the `internal/tracing` span/exporter unit tests (incl. `TestSpanEmit_*_NotSampledNoExport`) + the HCM exporter-provider unit tests.
- Phase 46.2 onward (the Zipkin provider + B3 propagation — `internal/tracing/b3.go` [`ExtractB3`/`InjectB3`; single `b3` + multi `X-B3-*`] + `internal/tracing/zipkin.go` [`ZipkinExporter` + the v2 JSON span encoder] + the `Span.Authority` carry + the `DecideWithContext` extract seam + the `ProviderKind`/`ZipkinSettings` parse dispatch + the Zipkin STRICT-REJECT arms + the `ExporterProvider` Zipkin arm + `HasCluster` boot-reject + the `tracing.zipkin.{spans_sent,spans_dropped}` lazy counters + the HCM provider-aware extract/inject + the `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` `zipkinTransportAdapter` wiring), exercised via fixture `0088-tracing-zipkin` (cross-side EXACT on span count + `name`/`kind`/tags + the B3 continuation prong, driver-owned `test/helpers/zipkincollector` HTTP receiver) + the `internal/tracing` b3/encoder/exporter unit tests (incl. the `HTTP_PROTO`/`split_spans_for_request`/cluster-miss subject-side rejects) + `FuzzExtractB3`.

### Does not yet apply to
- `health_check` / `service_forced` decision classes (counters register but stay 0 — no health-check detection / `x-envoy-force-trace` honoring in scope).
- H2 decode-side observation of the injected headers (the H2 inject mutates the upstream-forwarded header set only, not the decode-side map; H1 mutates `req.Header` which is both).
- The no-route-match (404) path injection-gap: no span/inject for a no-route 404 (the 46.1b emit seam passes `nil` ⇒ no span, consistent with 46.1a). A known parity boundary — to revisit at 46.2.
- `custom_tags`, `spawn_upstream_span`, `http_service`, `resource_detectors`, `sampler` — STRICT-REJECTED at parse; deferred to future rows.
