## Stats sinks — the metrics_service gRPC sink (per phase 47.1 ADR-0262)

**What triggers it.** A bootstrap-level `stats_sinks[]` entry whose `typed_config` is `envoy.config.metrics.v3.MetricsServiceConfig` — the FIRST consumer of the bootstrap `stats_sinks[]` field (silently ignored to date per ADR-0064), LIFTED from that silent-ignore set. The config is parsed into a `StatsSinkConfig{ClusterName}` (`Bootstrap.StatsSinkConfigs`) + a top-level `Bootstrap.FlushInterval` (from `stats_flush_interval`, default **5s**). At boot, when ≥1 such entry is present, `main.go` builds — per config — a `MetricsServiceClient` over the configured `grpc_service.envoy_grpc.cluster_name` (an H2-required cluster, via the `grpcclient.Dialer`) + a `MetricsServiceSink`, plus a single `Flusher` over all sinks, started AFTER `bs.Stats.Freeze()`.

**What it does.** Every `stats_flush_interval` the `Flusher` snapshots the frozen process-global `stats.Registry` (`Walk`) and streams it over the CLIENT-streaming `MetricsService.StreamMetrics` RPC as `io.prometheus.client.MetricFamily` protos: the first message of each stream carries `identifier{node{id,cluster}}` (re-armed on a reconnect), each message carries the full-registry batch as `envoy_metrics`. The mapping is cumulative/no-labels: each `Counter` → a `COUNTER` family at its absolute value; each `Gauge` → a `GAUGE` family; the FULL dotted internal name (tags inlined); ZERO `LabelPair`s; a flush-time `timestamp_ms`; empty `help`. Histograms have no envoy-go analog (ADR-0060), so only COUNTER/GAUGE families are produced. On a `Send` error the writer re-opens the stream once and re-sends the whole batch (re-arming the identifier); on a full channel a flush is dropped (drop-newest) and a rate-limited diagnostic logged.

**Strict-rejects (boot).** REFERENCE-PARITY (the reference also rejects, exit 1): a missing/non-H2 metrics cluster (`log.Fatalf` at sink build, via the Dialer gate) + a deprecated non-V3 `transport_api_version` (`AUTO`/`V3` accepted). envoy-go-STRICT (ADR-0080 — the reference BOOTS these): `report_counters_as_deltas:true`, `emit_tags_as_labels:true`, a non-default `histogram_emit_mode`, a sibling sink TypeURL (an EXPLICIT per-sibling reject naming the offending + the supported `metrics_service` TypeURL), `google_grpc`, an empty `cluster_name`, and `stats_flush_on_admin`. All boot-rejects are SUBJECT unit tests (no fixture dirs).

**+0 self-stats (D-MS-STATS-FINAL).** The sink registers NO `metrics_service`-scoped stat — MATCHING the reference (zero self-stats) AND sidestepping the self-referential subtlety of a STATS sink (a self-counter would appear in its own next flush). A deliberate departure from the 45.1/46.1 exporter-counter convention; channel-full drops are LOGGED, not counted. Stat surface UNCHANGED at **1200** (non-H2 **1196**).

**Byte-stable when unconfigured.** No `stats_sinks[]` metrics_service entry ⇒ no `Flusher`/sink builds, no goroutine, zero stats registered (a bare `stats_flush_interval` is parsed-and-inert). The full **91-dir** differential is the regression anchor.

**The `0089-stats-sink-metrics-service` differential.** Cross-side EXACT against contrib-v1.37.2 over TWO driver-owned per-side `MetricsService` receivers (NOT one shared — the periodic flush means the reference streams for the whole test; a shared receiver would contaminate the subject snapshot and defeat subject-side deliberate breaks). K=7 requests/side; poll each side's receiver to converge the deterministic COUNTER NAME-SUBSET (`cluster.<backend>.upstream_rq_total`, `http.<stat_prefix>.downstream_rq_total`, `http.<stat_prefix>.downstream_rq_2xx`) to == K + the identifier node. ASSERT both sides: the subset present with `type==COUNTER` and `value==K`; `node.id`/`.cluster` == the configured values. UNasserted: the whole family set/count (surfaces differ cross-side — no envoy-go histograms), `timestamp_ms`, `help`, non-deterministic gauges, identifier `user_agent_*`/`extensions[]`, message/stream framing. Four deliberate breaks (value/type/identifier/disabled-flush) all LIVE on the subject side; 20/20 flake-soak; full-package `-race` clean (`internal/statssink` — the Flusher ticker + sink writer goroutine are background mutators).

**`report_counters_as_deltas: true` — per-flush Counter DELTAs (per phase 47.2a ADR-0263).** When the `stats_sinks[]` metrics_service entry sets `report_counters_as_deltas: true`, envoy-go emits — per COUNTER family — the per-flush DELTA (`current − last_flushed`) instead of the cumulative absolute value. A PER-SINK last-value map keyed by the full dotted family name (`internal/statssink/delta.go` `deltaState`) holds the cross-flush state, applied in `MetricsServiceSink.Submit`: the first flush / a counter's first appearance emits `current − 0` = the absolute (the empty-map zero default — no special first-flush branch); an unchanged counter emits a **0 delta and is STILL emitted** (the full counter set every flush); the metric type stays `COUNTER`; deltas are non-negative (monotone u64 counters). GAUGES stay ABSOLUTE — the knob applies to counters only. The transform builds a NEW batch (rebuilt COUNTER families; GAUGE/non-COUNTER families shared by pointer) and NEVER mutates the shared `Flusher` snapshot fan-out. Absent/`false` ⇒ the 47.1 cumulative absolute path is value-identical. The `report_counters_as_deltas:true` strict-reject is LIFTED (reference-parity-accept — the reference boots it); every OTHER 47.1 reject (sibling TypeURLs / `emit_tags_as_labels:true` / non-default `histogram_emit_mode` / `stats_flush_on_admin` / non-V3 / `google_grpc` / empty cluster) STAYS strict. Stat surface UNCHANGED at **1200** (+0; non-H2 **1196** — the delta map is internal per-sink bookkeeping).

**The `0090-stats-sink-metrics-service-deltas` differential.** Cross-side EXACT against contrib-v1.37.2 (the 0089 two-per-side-receiver shape with `report_counters_as_deltas: true`). Because the delta sink breaks 0089's `value == K` (a single flush is partial), the assertion is the per-name RUNNING DELTA-SUM == K across flushes (under deltas, idle flushes add 0 so the SUM stays K). A POST-CONVERGENCE STABILITY BARRIER is required: a single-window request burst makes the first flush's delta indistinguishable from the absolute, so the driver waits past convergence (idle flushes confirming the SUM no longer climbs) before asserting — otherwise the delta path and the absolute path are observationally identical. Two deliberate breaks (emit-absolute / skip-the-latch) both explode the running SUM and were verified to FAIL via the barrier.

**`emit_tags_as_labels: true` — tag SEGMENTS → `LabelPair`s (per phase 47.2b ADR-0264).** When the `stats_sinks[]` metrics_service entry sets `emit_tags_as_labels: true`, envoy-go emits — per metric family, BOTH Counter AND Gauge — the family's tag SEGMENTS as `MetricFamily.metric[].label[]` `LabelPair`s instead of inlining them into the family name. The tag VALUE is STRIPPED from the family `name` — the residual DOTTED name is kept (dots collapsed, tag value removed: `cluster.<backend>.upstream_rq_total` → `name="cluster.upstream_rq_total"`, NOT the Prometheus `envoy_`-flattened base) — and emitted as a label keyed by the Envoy DOTTED tag-name (`envoy.cluster_name`, `envoy.http_conn_manager_prefix`, `envoy.listener_address`, `envoy.response_code_class` — only the leading `envoy_` → `envoy.`, the rest underscored), SORTED by key. The response-code-class `_Nxx` suffix collapses to `_xx` + an `envoy.response_code_class=N` label (a single name yielding MULTIPLE labels — `downstream_rq_2xx` → `name="http.downstream_rq_xx"` + `{envoy.http_conn_manager_prefix, envoy.response_code_class="2"}`). An untagged name keeps its full dotted name with an EMPTY label set. The transform REUSES the `internal/stats/name.go` SN1–SN9+SN4 rules via the SHARED `stats.ExtractTags` core (`flattenToProm` is now a thin Prometheus projection over the same core — byte-identical) projected to the metrics_service dotted form by a sink-owned `labelMapper` (`internal/statssink/label.go`) applied in `MetricsServiceSink.Submit` PARALLEL to the 47.2a `deltaState` (compose order delta-THEN-labels — delta rewrites the Counter VALUE, labels rewrite the NAME+LABEL, orthogonal). The metric `type` and `value` are UNCHANGED (cumulative-absolute — unless `report_counters_as_deltas` is ALSO set, in which case the Counter carries its per-flush delta WITH the labels; the two knobs compose). The transform builds the sink's OWN families (new `MetricFamily`/`Metric`/sorted `LabelPair`s, value pointer shared read-only) and NEVER mutates the shared `Flusher` snapshot fan-out. Absent/`false` ⇒ the 47.1 full-dotted-name/zero-labels path is byte-identical. The `emit_tags_as_labels:true` strict-reject is LIFTED (reference-parity-accept — the reference boots it); every OTHER reject (sibling TypeURLs / non-default `histogram_emit_mode` / `stats_flush_on_admin` / non-V3 / `google_grpc` / empty cluster) STAYS strict. After 47.2b BOTH `MetricsServiceConfig` knobs are CONSUMED. Stat surface UNCHANGED at **1200** (+0; non-H2 **1196** — the label transform is a sink-owned mapping).

**The `0091-stats-sink-metrics-service-labels` differential.** Cross-side EXACT against contrib-v1.37.2 (the 0090 two-per-side-receiver shape with `emit_tags_as_labels: true`, values CUMULATIVE — NOT deltas). The labels knob keeps 0089's CUMULATIVE value model, so `0091` asserts the deterministic counter subset's `{residual-name, sorted LabelPair[]}` split + last-seen `value == K` (NO delta-SUM stability barrier — that was a 47.2a/`0090` concern). The receiver gains an additive `{name, sorted-labels}`-keyed `FamilyWithLabels` surface (multiple families share a residual name under labels — `cluster.upstream_rq_total` for both `c_backend` AND `c_metrics`); `Family`/`FamilySum`/`Messages` STAY for 0089/0090 non-regress. Four deliberate breaks ((a) full inlined name no labels / (b) Prometheus underscore key `envoy_cluster_name` / (c) Prometheus flattened name / (d) dropped SN4 2xx label — (d) ALSO trips the `internal/stats` byte-identity guard) all LIVE on the subject side; 20/20 flake-soak; full-package `-race` clean on BOTH `internal/statssink` AND `internal/stats` (the shared `ExtractTags` is now on the flush path).

### Stats sinks — the statsd UDP sink (per phase 48 ADR-0265)

**What triggers it.** A bootstrap-level `stats_sinks[]` entry whose `typed_config` is `envoy.config.metrics.v3.StatsdSink` — the SECOND consumer of the bootstrap `stats_sinks[]` field (after phase-47 `metrics_service`), LIFTED from the `bootstrap.go` sibling-reject (the dispatch `else` arm now NAMES BOTH supported sinks — `metrics_service` AND `statsd` — per `reference_strict_reject_sibling_typeurl_gap`). The config is parsed by `parseStatsdSinkConfig` into a `StatsdSinkConfig{UDPAddress, Prefix}` (`Bootstrap.StatsdSinkConfigs` — a PARALLEL slice alongside `StatsSinkConfigs`), reusing the same top-level `Bootstrap.FlushInterval` (`stats_flush_interval`, default **5s**). The `statsd_specifier` oneof's `address` (a `socket_address{address, port_value}`) is joined to a `host:port` `UDPAddress` string at parse; `prefix` defaults to `envoy`. At boot, when ≥1 such entry is present, `main.go` runs a SECOND build loop — per config a `StatsdSink` (envoy-go's FIRST `net.UDPConn`, dialed via `net.ResolveUDPAddr`+`net.DialUDP` at `NewStatsdSink`) — fanned into the SAME `statsSinks []Sink` slice the metrics_service sinks join; the flusher-build gate is generalized to build when EITHER sink kind is present, and the single `Flusher` is started AFTER `bs.Stats.Freeze()`.

**What it does.** Every `stats_flush_interval` the sink-agnostic `Flusher` snapshots the frozen process-global `stats.Registry` and hands the same `[]*dto.MetricFamily` batch to each `Sink`. The `StatsdSink.Submit` writes ONE statsd line per metric as a UDP datagram to the configured address: `<prefix>.<name>:<value>|c` for each COUNTER family (the value is the **per-flush DELTA** — the canonical statsd increment), `<prefix>.<name>:<value>|g` for each GAUGE family (the value is the **absolute** current value). `<name>` is the FULL dotted internal name with tags INLINED and ZERO labels (the proto "does not support tagged metrics" — no SN-rule machinery); `<prefix>` is joined `prefix + "." + name` (default `envoy`). The counter→delta transform reuses the landed `internal/statssink/delta.go` `deltaState` VERBATIM, sink-private and ALWAYS-on (no knob — delta is INTRINSIC to the statsd `|c` semantics; CONTRAST the metrics_service `report_counters_as_deltas` knob): first flush / first appearance emits `current − 0` = the absolute; the gauge→absolute split MATCHES the `|c`/`|g` mapping exactly. `Submit` is SYNCHRONOUS (no channel, no writer goroutine — a UDP `Write` never blocks on a peer and the `Flusher` calls `Submit` serially); a `Write` error is rate-limit-logged-and-DROPPED (UDP is lossy; NOT counted). `Close` is idempotent (`sync.Once`).

**Strict-rejects (boot).** envoy-go-STRICT (ADR-0080 — this row is UDP-only): a `tcp_cluster_name` `statsd_specifier` (statsd-over-TCP — DEFERRED). REFERENCE-PARITY (the reference's PGV also rejects, exit 1): a missing `statsd_specifier` / nil `socket_address`. A sibling/unknown sink TypeURL is rejected by the shared dispatch `else` arm (naming both supported sinks). `socket_address.protocol` is ACCEPTED-and-IGNORED (envoy-go dials UDP regardless). An unresolvable UDP address `log.Fatalf`s at sink build (`NewStatsdSink`). All boot-rejects are SUBJECT unit tests (no fixture dirs).

**+0 self-stats.** The sink registers NO `statsd`-scoped stat (the metrics_service precedent — zero self-stats, sidestepping the self-referential STATS-sink subtlety; Write-drops are LOGGED, not counted), and adds NO sink cluster (UDP, not a managed cluster). Stat surface UNCHANGED at **1200** (non-H2 **1196**); confirmed by `internal/statssink`'s `TestNoNewStat_StatsdRegistrationGuard`.

**Byte-stable when unconfigured.** No `stats_sinks[]` statsd entry ⇒ no `StatsdSink` builds, no UDP dial, zero stats registered. The full **94-dir** differential is the regression anchor.

**The `0092-stats-sink-statsd` differential.** Cross-side against contrib-v1.37.2 over TWO driver-owned per-side UDP receivers (`test/helpers/statsdrecv` — NOT a BackendKind, tail STAYS **38**; the `reference_periodic_sink_differential_two_receivers` shape with a hard `Close()`). Because the statsd `|c` is a per-flush DELTA, the assertion is the per-name running DELTA-SUM == K across flushes plus a POST-CONVERGENCE STABILITY BARRIER (idle flushes confirming the SUM no longer climbs — else the first flush's delta is indistinguishable from the absolute; `reference_delta_sink_differential_stability_barrier`) on a 3-counter subset (`cluster.<backend>.upstream_rq_total`, `http.<stat_prefix>.downstream_rq_total`, `http.<stat_prefix>.downstream_rq_2xx`), plus an ABSOLUTE-gauge subset (`cluster.<backend>.membership_total == 1 |g`). NOTE: the gauge subset uses `membership_total` (registered UNCONDITIONALLY for every cluster — == endpoint count), NOT `membership_healthy` (registered ONLY on clusters WITH `health_checks` configured; the `0092` cluster has none, so the subject never emits it — a noted pre-existing envoy-go behavior, not a phase-48 bug). The reference's statsd `address` MUST be a LITERAL IP (statsd rejects hostnames), resolved via the NEW `differential.HostGatewayIP` harness helper (a throwaway `alpine:3` container resolving `host.docker.internal` under `ExtraHosts: host-gateway` — the bridge gateway on native Linux, the VM→host gateway on Docker Desktop; container→host UDP delivery empirically verified — NOT the Docker `bridge` IPAM gateway, which under Docker Desktop is the VM-internal interface and reaches nothing). Three deliberate breaks ((a) absolute-not-delta / (b) wrong prefix-or-type / (c) barrier-masks-(a)) all LIVE on the subject side; 20/20 flake-soak; full-package `-race` clean.

### Stats sinks — the dog_statsd UDP sink with tags (per phase 49 ADR-0266; batching per phase 50 ADR-0267)

**What triggers it.** A bootstrap-level `stats_sinks[]` entry whose `typed_config` is `envoy.config.metrics.v3.DogStatsdSink` — the THIRD consumer of the bootstrap `stats_sinks[]` field (after phase-47 `metrics_service` and phase-48 `statsd`), LIFTED from the `bootstrap.go` sibling-reject (the dispatch `else` arm now NAMES ALL THREE supported sinks — `metrics_service`, `statsd`, AND `dog_statsd` — per `reference_strict_reject_sibling_typeurl_gap`). The config is parsed by `parseDogStatsdSinkConfig` into a `DogStatsdSinkConfig{UDPAddress, Prefix}` (`Bootstrap.DogStatsdSinkConfigs` — a PARALLEL slice alongside `StatsSinkConfigs`/`StatsdSinkConfigs`), reusing the same top-level `Bootstrap.FlushInterval` (`stats_flush_interval`, default **5s**). The `dog_statsd_specifier` oneof's ONLY member `address` (a `socket_address{address, port_value}`) is joined to a `host:port` `UDPAddress` string at parse; `prefix` defaults to `envoy`. At boot, when ≥1 such entry is present, `main.go` runs a THIRD build loop — per config a `DogStatsdSink` (a SECOND, independent `net.UDPConn`, dialed via `net.ResolveUDPAddr`+`net.DialUDP` at `NewDogStatsdSink`) — fanned into the SAME `statsSinks []Sink` slice the metrics_service and statsd sinks join; the flusher-build gate is generalized to a three-way OR (build when ANY sink kind is present), and the single `Flusher` is started AFTER `bs.Stats.Freeze()`.

**What it does.** Every `stats_flush_interval` the sink-agnostic `Flusher` snapshots the frozen process-global `stats.Registry` and hands the same `[]*dto.MetricFamily` batch to each `Sink`. The `DogStatsdSink.Submit` writes ONE DogStatsd line per metric as a UDP datagram to the configured address: `<prefix>.<residual-name>:<delta>|c[|#tags]` for each COUNTER family (the value is the **per-flush DELTA**, over a SECOND, INDEPENDENT sink-private `deltaState` — reusing `internal/statssink/delta.go` VERBATIM, NEVER shared with any `StatsdSink` instance), `<prefix>.<residual-name>:<abs>|g[|#tags]` for each GAUGE family (the value is the **absolute** current value). `<residual-name>` is `stats.ExtractTags`'s residual dotted name (tag-value segments removed, dots preserved — the SAME core the metrics_service `emit_tags_as_labels` knob uses, consumed here DIRECTLY rather than via the `labelMapper`); `<prefix>` is joined `prefix + "." + residual-name` (default `envoy`). The extracted tags are formatted `envoy.<key>:<value>` pairs, comma-joined, appended as an inline `|#tag1:val1,...` suffix in the extractor's NATURAL (unsorted, SN4-prepended) order — NOT sorted (a deliberate departure from `labelMapper`'s sorted convention, justified by reference-parity — the live probe showed the reference does not alphabetically sort a DogStatsd tag suffix, `reference_dogstatsd_tag_order_unsorted`); a name with zero extracted tags emits with NO `|#` suffix at all. `Submit` is SYNCHRONOUS (no channel, no writer goroutine — the `StatsdSink` shape); a `Write` error is rate-limit-logged-and-DROPPED. `Close` is idempotent (`sync.Once`). envoy-go has no histograms (ADR-0060), so only `|c`/`|g` lines are produced.

**Strict-rejects (boot).** REFERENCE-PARITY (the reference's PGV also rejects, exit 1): a missing `dog_statsd_specifier` / nil `socket_address`. A sibling/unknown sink TypeURL is rejected by the shared dispatch `else` arm (naming all three supported sinks). `socket_address.protocol` is ACCEPTED-and-IGNORED (envoy-go dials UDP regardless). An unresolvable UDP address `log.Fatalf`s at sink build (`NewDogStatsdSink`). All boot-rejects are SUBJECT unit tests (no fixture dirs).

**`max_bytes_per_datagram` batching (phase 50, ADR-0267).** An EXPLICIT `max_bytes_per_datagram` on a bootstrap `dog_statsd` `stats_sinks[]` entry is now HONORED — the phase-49 strict-reject was LIFTED. envoy-go accumulates consecutive formatted DogStatsd lines (in the SAME registry-walk emission order the `Submit` loop already produces — never reordered, never deduped) into a growing per-flush buffer, flushing it as one UDP datagram whenever appending the NEXT line would make the buffer STRICTLY exceed the configured cap (a buffer that lands EXACTLY at the cap after appending still fits — the boundary is INCLUSIVE, live-proven both directions with a byte-exact two-line pair at cap=75 vs cap=74). A single line whose own formatted length exceeds the cap is sent alone in its own oversized datagram, with NO error, no drop, and no truncation (live-proven up to 218 bytes against a 120-byte cap, zero truncation across 715 oversized datagrams). An ABSENT `max_bytes_per_datagram` (or an explicit `0`) continues to emit EXACTLY one line per datagram, byte-identical to phase 49 — no special-cased branch is needed for either the absent/zero-cap case or the oversized-single-line case; both fall out of the SAME general two-comparison accumulate-then-flush-on-overflow algorithm. Batching is a purely TRANSPORT-layer concern applied strictly AFTER line formatting — the delta-state transform, `stats.ExtractTags` tag extraction, and the DogStatsd line format are ALL byte-for-byte UNCHANGED from phase 49.

**+0 self-stats.** The sink registers NO `dog_statsd`-scoped stat (the metrics_service/statsd precedent) and adds NO sink cluster (UDP, not a managed cluster). Stat surface UNCHANGED at **1200** (non-H2 **1196**); confirmed by `internal/statssink`'s `TestNoNewStat_DogStatsdRegistrationGuard`.

**Byte-stable when unconfigured.** No `stats_sinks[]` dog_statsd entry ⇒ no `DogStatsdSink` builds, no second UDP dial, zero stats registered. The full **96-dir** differential is the regression anchor.

**The `0093-stats-sink-dogstatsd` differential.** Cross-side against contrib-v1.37.2 over TWO driver-owned per-side UDP receivers (the extended `test/helpers/statsdrecv` — NOT a BackendKind, tail STAYS **38**; the `reference_periodic_sink_differential_two_receivers` shape with a hard `Close()`, cloning the `0092` driver). Because `stats.ExtractTags` runs BEFORE the wire format, the deterministic COUNTER subset's wire names differ from `0092`'s raw dotted names: `cluster.upstream_rq_total` tagged `envoy.cluster_name`, `http.downstream_rq_total` tagged `envoy.http_conn_manager_prefix`, and `http.downstream_rq_xx` (the SN4 `_2xx`→`_xx` wire-name REWRITE — not merely "the same name plus a tag") tagged `envoy.response_code_class`+`envoy.http_conn_manager_prefix`. The assertion is the per-name running DELTA-SUM (via the NEW `DeltaSumTagged(name, tags)` accessor, disambiguating an EXACT tag-set match) `== K` across flushes plus a POST-CONVERGENCE STABILITY BARRIER (`reference_delta_sink_differential_stability_barrier`), plus the tag SET match (order-independent `maps.Equal`), plus an ABSOLUTE-gauge-plus-tag subset (`cluster.membership_total == 1 |g` tagged `envoy.cluster_name` — `membership_total`, NOT `membership_healthy`, the `0092` precedent, `reference_membership_total_vs_healthy_gauge`). `DeltaSumTagged` (not the plain per-name `DeltaSum`) is REQUIRED because the bootstrap's own admin interface emits internal HCM stats under `stat_prefix "admin"` which collapse, via the SAME SN2 hoist, to the IDENTICAL residual wire names as the test listener's — differing only in the `envoy.http_conn_manager_prefix` tag VALUE — so a plain per-name sum never converges (observed LIVE, stuck at `K+1`). The reference's dog_statsd `address` MUST be a LITERAL IP (no DNS resolution), resolved via a LOCAL `hostGatewayIP` helper duplicated verbatim from the `0092` driver (NOT the exported `differential.HostGatewayIP`, to avoid a same-package import-cycle risk). Three deliberate breaks ((a) absolute-not-delta / (b) dropped-or-wrong tags / (c) barrier-masks-(a)) all LIVE on the subject side; 20/20 flake-soak; full-package `-race` clean on BOTH `internal/statssink` AND `internal/stats`.

**The `0094-stats-sink-dogstatsd-batching` differential (phase 50, ADR-0267).** Clones the `0093` two-per-side-UDP-receiver-plus-hard-`Close()` shape verbatim (distinct prefix `dsdbpfx`; the SAME `hostGatewayIP` LOCAL-helper duplication) with a bootstrap-level `max_bytes_per_datagram: 200` on BOTH sides and a deliberately LONG 172-character `backendName` (confirmed via a real `len()` check, not hand-estimated — D-DSDB-CAP): the `envoy.cluster_name`-tagged lines (`cluster.upstream_rq_total` at 230 bytes, `cluster.membership_total` at 229 bytes) EACH ALONE exceed the 200-byte cap and are forced oversized-alone, while the `envoy.http_conn_manager_prefix`-tagged lines (78/103 bytes, unchanged short `statPrefix="hcm_local"`) stay short enough to co-batch together under the cap. Assertions: (a) the SAME `0093` delta-SUM-with-stability-barrier + tag-set + absolute-gauge-plus-tag subset, proving batching does not alter WHAT is sent or its extracted tags; (b) `srv.MaxLinesInAnyDatagram() > 1` on each side — real co-location was observed, not merely tolerated; (c) `srv.LinesInDatagram(clusterTaggedName) == (1, true)` on each side — the oversized cluster-tagged line was NEVER co-batched with anything. Two deliberate breaks LIVE on the subject side: (a) force one-line-per-datagram unconditionally regardless of the cap (assertion (b) fails); (b) silently drop an overflowing line instead of flush-then-append (assertion (a)'s delta-SUM undercounts below K). Plus the 20/20 flake-soak and the full-package `-race` clean on BOTH `internal/statssink` AND `internal/stats`.

### Does not yet apply to (stats sinks)
- non-default `histogram_emit_mode` + `stats_flush_on_admin` (metrics_service) + the statsd `tcp_cluster_name` transport + sibling sink TypeURLs (graphite / OTLP-metrics) + statsd/dog_statsd timers/`|ms` (no histograms — ADR-0060) — STRICT-REJECTED at 47.1/47.2a/47.2b/48/49. Both `MetricsServiceConfig` knobs (`report_counters_as_deltas` 47.2a + `emit_tags_as_labels` 47.2b) are CONSUMED; the statsd sink is UDP-`address`-only; the dog_statsd sink's `address`/`prefix`/`max_bytes_per_datagram` are ALL now consumed (phase 49 + phase 50).
- Histograms (no envoy-go analog, ADR-0060) — the reference's `HISTOGRAM` families have no envoy-go counterpart.
- A drain-flush at shutdown (the ticker stops on `ctx.Done`; the sink's `Close` drains the in-flight stream).

## Bootstrap config validation (per phase 51 ADR-0268)

**What triggers it.** A `--mode validate` CLI flag on `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` (mirroring upstream Envoy's own flag verbatim), OR direct use of the new public `github.com/esalaine/envoy-go/validate` package — the FIRST non-`internal/`/non-`cmd/`/non-`test/` package in this repo, existing purely because Go's `internal/` import-path restriction blocks any external module from reaching `internal/bootstrap`/`internal/cluster`/`internal/listener` directly. `validate.Bootstrap(r io.Reader, baseDir string, allowH2C bool) error` validates a Bootstrap config read from `r`; `validate.BootstrapFile(path string) error` opens `path` and validates it with `allowH2C=false`. `baseDir` resolves relative file paths within the config (TLS certs, Lua scripts) the same way `main.go`'s own `filepath.Dir(cfgPath)` does.

**What it does — validation depth.** `validate.Bootstrap` reuses the SHARED `internal/boot.Construct` function — the SAME function `cmd/envoy-go/main.go`'s normal boot path calls — so the two paths can never silently diverge on what "valid" means. It performs FULL CONSTRUCTION: `bootstrap.Load` (parse), `cluster.NewManagerWithBaseDir` (cluster manager + upstream TLS cert resolution), and `boot.Construct` (every listener's full filter chain — route tables, HTTP/network/listener filters, TLS certificate loading, Lua script compilation) via `listener.NewManagerWithBaseDirAndAllowH2C`. It stops BEFORE any socket bind, any admin-server start, or any background loop (health checks, outlier detection, stats flush) — exploiting the ALREADY-LANDED "construct vs. bind" seam inside `listener.NewManagerWithBaseDirAndAllowH2C`/`lm.Start`. It also SKIPS access-log file opens and stats-sink UDP dials entirely (passing a nil sink slice into `boot.Construct` — neither has dry-run diagnostic value: a UDP dial never proves reachability, and a real file open is an unwanted side effect of a "just checking" operation). No change to WHAT is validated anywhere — every existing strict-reject/parse-arm across `internal/bootstrap`/`internal/cluster`/`internal/listener` is reused byte-for-byte.

**Public API shape.** A single fail-fast error (the first error encountered), matching this project's existing internal validation style throughout — NOT multi-diagnostic. Returns `nil` if the configuration is valid.

**The `--mode validate` CLI flag.** Exit codes mirror upstream Envoy plus this project's own convention: **`0`** valid (prints `"configuration OK"` to stdout); **`1`** invalid (the config file cannot be opened, or `validate.Bootstrap` returns an error — printed to stderr); **`2`** usage error (an unrecognized `--mode` value, or a missing `-c`). The handler calls `validate.Bootstrap` DIRECTLY (not the convenience `BootstrapFile` wrapper) so the pre-existing `-allow-h2c` test-only flag continues to compose — `BootstrapFile` hardcodes `allowH2C=false`. Absent/empty `--mode` is byte-identical to the pre-phase-51 boot behavior.

**Byte-stable / zero differential surface.** This phase has NO wire behavior to compare against a live reference Envoy — it is a refactor (extracting the ALREADY-SEPARATED "construct" half of the boot sequence into `internal/boot`, plus a no-`Deps` `internal/filter/http/builtins` registration package) plus a new entry point. The FULL EXISTING 96-fixture differential suite (unchanged) is the byte-stability regression anchor, proving the extraction changed nothing observable about any previously-landed feature.

**No new fuzzer (D-VALIDATE-FUZZER).** Every input `internal/boot.Construct`/`validate.Bootstrap` consumes has already passed `bootstrap.Load`'s untrusted-YAML-parse boundary (covered by the existing bootstrap-config fuzzers); the construction-tail code operates on an already-validated `*bootstrap.Bootstrap` struct, not raw untrusted bytes.

### Does not yet apply to (bootstrap config validation)
- xDS-sourced (not just static-file) dry-validation.
- An admin-API-exposed live-reload-and-validate endpoint.
- An RTDS/SDS validate companion.

## Timing tolerances

_to be filled per-phase as needed._

Timing is not compared by default. A phase may opt in to latency bounds (p50 / p95 / p99 vs upstream, wall-clock or CPU-normalized) by adding a subsection here naming the fixture, the bound, and the measurement methodology. Opt-ins are additive; removing one requires a superseding ADR.

- **Fault filter delay accuracy: ±10ms (per phase 09 §11.2 empirical pin).**
  envoy-go's `time.AfterFunc` timer-driven async-resume matches Envoy v1.37.2's
  fault delay accuracy within ±10ms across the 50/100/200/500ms sweep.
  Empirical worst-case overhead observed: +3.6ms (Envoy v1.37.2 was tested;
  envoy-go's overhead is similar). The differential fixture 0011-http-fault's
  driver bucketizes elapsed timings (fast vs delayed) to absorb CI scheduling
  jitter while still distinguishing the wholesale-override no-delay path from
  the inherited-delay path.

- **Local rate-limit token-bucket refill boundary: ±10ms (per phase 11 ADR-0116 + SPEC §11.7 empirical pin).**
  fixture 0013 scenario 3 (refill-after-fill_interval): t=250ms refill boundary ±10ms wall-clock. Per ADR-0116 + §11.7 empirical (BRAINSTORM ±20ms hypothesis narrowed; PLAN author may widen back to ±20ms with retry-with-deadline harness if CI flakes per SPEC §12 D4).

- **Bandwidth-limit throttle wall-clock tolerance: ±70ms per-side (per phase 15 ADR-0137 + SPEC §7.3 + §11.P9 + Task-14 per-side discipline adoption).**
  Phase 15's Path B-async body algorithm emits one body-blast at the end of the throttle window; Envoy's reference Path A rate-paced chunk-emit pattern emits chunks at `fill_interval` cadence with `chunk_size = limit_kbps × 1024 × fill_interval_seconds` bytes per tick (KiB/s units per phase 15 SPEC §1.1 amendment 6). Total wall-clock throttle-time observably equivalent within ±70ms across body sizes 100 bytes to 51 KiB and `limit_kbps` values 1 to 100 (per phase 15 SPEC §11 empirical test matrix at probes A/B/L). **Task-14 empirical pin:** the SPEC §11.P9(c) "cross-side total-throttle-time converges within ±70ms" predicate was REFUTED for bodies within initial-burst capacity (Envoy's initial-burst-discount + per-request bump-on-active-side-regardless-of-body diverges from envoy-go's deterministic ceil-formula + DecodeData-driven bump). Adopted discipline: **each side asserted independently within ±70ms of its predicted target** (NOT cross-side wall-clock delta). Fixture 0017's driver asserts per-scenario per-side wall-clock within tolerance; the ±70ms window absorbs `time.AfterFunc` Linux granularity (typically 1-5ms minimum) plus CI scheduling jitter plus initial-burst-capacity approximation variance.

## Admin API

The envoy-go admin server is a single HTTP/1.1 plaintext bind allocated by `internal/admin.Server.Start()` (per phase 01 contract; reused unchanged in 06.1 and 08.1). Eight endpoints are registered on the same `*http.ServeMux`: `/ready` (phase 01), `/stats/prometheus` (phase 06.1), `/config_dump`, `/clusters`, `/listeners`, `/server_info` (phase 08.1), `POST /drain_listeners` (phase 08.2; NEW mutating endpoint), `GET /stats` (phase 32.1; NEW flat internal-name text endpoint). Phase 08.2 also extends `/ready` + `/server_info` for the DRAINING state.

**Framing deviation (all eight admin endpoints).** envoy-go's `net/http` server emits `Content-Length` (the body is buffered before write); upstream Envoy v1.37.2 emits `transfer-encoding: chunked`. The differential harness dechunks upstream responses before byte-comparing the body. This deviation was first documented for `/ready` at phase 01 (per ADR-0015 paragraph 3) and extends unchanged to all eight endpoints. No allow-list entry; the dechunk is structural.

**Header set (all eight admin endpoints, post-framing-normalization).** The lowercase wire-form header set is `content-type`, `cache-control: no-cache, max-age=0`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `date: <IMF-fixdate>`, `server: envoy` (per ADR-0014). All eight endpoints emit this set via the shared `writeAdminHeaders` helper. The differential harness uses the existing case-insensitive header comparator (introduced for phase 01).

**Method discrimination posture.** Upstream Envoy v1.37.2 does NOT enforce method discrimination on the six 08.1 read-only endpoints (POST/PUT/DELETE return 200 with the same body as GET — empirical pin in 08.1 SPEC §11.8). envoy-go matches Envoy parity on those six endpoints (no method check; Go stdlib `http.ServeMux` dispatches on path only). The 08.2 mutating endpoint `POST /drain_listeners` DOES enforce method discrimination: non-POST methods return 405 with body `Method <METHOD> not allowed, POST required.\n` per 08.2 SPEC §11.4 empirical pin (ADR-0093 partially amending ADR-0090).

### /ready

*Introduced by phase 01. Justified by ADR-0015 (pre-init contract) and ADR-0014 (Server header value). Captured evidence: `docs/envoy-go/phases/01-static-bootstrap-config/upstream-ready-observation.md`.*

#### Ready-state response (authoritative)

Upstream Envoy v1.37.2 emits (in wire order, lowercase header names):

- **Status line:** `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`
- **Body:** `LIVE\n` (5 bytes: `0x4c 0x49 0x56 0x45 0x0a` — trailing LF, NOT CRLF)
- **content-type:** `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`
- **cache-control:** `no-cache, max-age=0`
- **x-content-type-options:** `nosniff`
- **date:** RFC 7231 IMF-fixdate (non-deterministic; see allow-list above)
- **server:** `envoy` (no version suffix — per ADR-0014)
- **transfer-encoding:** `chunked` (upstream framing)

The phase-01 envoy-go subject emits byte-exact equivalent headers + body, with ONE documented framing deviation: the subject emits `Content-Length: 5` instead of `transfer-encoding: chunked`. The differential harness (Task 14) dechunks upstream responses to the raw body bytes before comparison, neutralising the framing difference. Upgrading the subject to chunked framing is a phase-02+ follow-up, not a phase-01 gate.

Header name case: HTTP/1.1 header names are case-insensitive per RFC 7230 §3.2. Upstream emits lowercase (`content-type`); the envoy-go subject emits Go `net/http` canonical case (`Content-Type`). The differential diff (Task 14) compares header names case-insensitively.

#### Pre-init response

Per ADR-0015, the pre-init `/ready` window is not exercised by the phase-01 differential test — `cmd/envoy-go` fires `admin.MarkReady` before printing the harness readiness sentinel, so the harness only observes the ready state. The subject emits a documented-but-test-irrelevant pre-init response:

- **Status line:** `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable`
- **Body:** `PRE_INITIALIZING\n` (17 bytes)
- **Content-Length:** `17`
- Other headers as in the ready response (`Content-Type`, `Cache-Control`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Server`, `Date`).

Upstream v1.37.2's actual pre-init bytes were unobservable from the minimal bootstrap used in Task 7 (60 probes across two tight loops captured no non-200 response). A later phase that successfully captures upstream pre-init bytes supersedes this subsection via a new ADR.

**DRAINING-state response (08.2 NEW).** When `drain.Manager.State() == DRAINING`, the handler returns 503 Service Unavailable with body `DRAINING\n` (9 bytes; uppercase `DRAINING` followed by single newline) per 08.2 SPEC §11.2 empirical pin. The DRAINING check has precedence over both LIVE and PRE_INITIALIZING — once drain has fired, /ready returns the DRAINING body even if MarkReady has been called and even if /server_info would otherwise return state="LIVE". Header set inherits the umbrella rules.

**Empirical evidence (verbatim Envoy v1.37.2 `/ready` during DRAINING):** see 08.2 SPEC §11.2.

**Equivalence claim.** Body byte-equal to reference Envoy v1.37.2 in DRAINING state. Status 503 byte-equal.

**Forward-pointer note.** ADR-0015 (pre-init contract for /ready) is **partially superseded by ADR-0097**: the LIVE / PRE_INITIALIZING two-state coverage extends to LIVE / PRE_INITIALIZING / DRAINING three-state coverage. ADR-0015's verbatim pre-init body and pre-init status are preserved; ADR-0097 adds the DRAINING branch and the precedence rule.

### /stats/prometheus

See `## Stat-name mapping` for the body-shape contract (Prometheus text exposition format with the SN1–SN8 flattening rules per ADR-0061). Header set + framing inherit the umbrella rules above.

### /config_dump

**Body shape.** `application/json` via `protojson.MarshalOptions{Multiline: true, Indent: " ", UseProtoNames: true, EmitUnpopulated: true}` over `*adminv3.ConfigDump{Configs: []*anypb.Any{...}}` with three sub-envelopes in this order: `BootstrapConfigDump`, `ListenersConfigDump`, `ClustersConfigDump`. No `dynamic_*` arrays (no xDS).

**Empirical evidence (verbatim Envoy v1.37.2 `/config_dump`, first 50 lines):** see 08.1 SPEC §11.1.

**Equivalence claim.** Body byte-equal to reference Envoy v1.37.2 modulo: `bootstrap.node.user_agent_name`, `bootstrap.node.user_agent_build_version`, `bootstrap.node.extensions[]`, `<*ConfigDump>.last_updated` allow-listed (envoy-go emits empty / partial values; Envoy auto-populates).

### /clusters

**Body shape.** `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`. 10 cluster-level lines + 18 per-endpoint lines per cluster. Cluster ordering: alphabetical by cluster name. Endpoint ordering: bootstrap-declared order. envoy-go emits the same Envoy default constants (`1024`, `3`, `healthy`, empty locality, `false`, `0`, `-1`) for fields it does not model (circuit breakers, active health checking, locality tags, success rate); see 08.1 SPEC §5.3 for the verbatim line set.

**Empirical evidence (verbatim Envoy v1.37.2 `/clusters`):** see 08.1 SPEC §11.2.

**Equivalence claim.** Tuple-set equality on `(cluster_name, key, value)` triples. Hot-path counters `cx_total`, `cx_connect_fail`, `rq_total`, `rq_active`, `rq_error` allow ±1 tolerance (round-robin LB distribution skew across the 5-request §7.3 load).

**M-1 carry-forward note.** Cluster-name validation is a pre-existing M-1 vulnerability identified in 07.2 REVIEW; the `<cluster>::<key>::<value>` separator is not escaped. An embedded `::` in a cluster name would corrupt the format. envoy-go matches Envoy parity (Envoy also does not escape); the M-1 fix-when-it-lands closes both surfaces simultaneously.

### /listeners

**Body shape.** `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`. One line per listener: `<listener_name>::<bind_addr>` where `<bind_addr>` is `host:port`. Listener ordering: alphabetical by listener name. Trailing newline.

**Empirical evidence (verbatim Envoy v1.37.2 `/listeners`):** see 08.1 SPEC §11.3.

**Equivalence claim.** Body byte-equal (after framing dechunk). Single line per listener; no additional fields. The JSON form (`?format=json`) is structurally richer (returns `{"listener_statuses": [...]}`); deferred per ADR-0089.

### /server_info

**Body shape.** `application/json` via the same protojson MarshalOptions as `/config_dump`. Field set populates `version`, `state`, `uptime_current_epoch`, `uptime_all_epochs`, `node` (from bootstrap), partial `command_line_options{config_path}`, `hot_restart_version: "disabled"`. State enum (08.2 EXTENDED): `LIVE` (post-MarkReady, drain has not fired), `PRE_INITIALIZING` (pre-MarkReady, drain has not fired), `DRAINING` (drain has fired — supersedes LIVE and PRE_INITIALIZING). `INITIALIZING` is documented in `adminv3.ServerInfo_State` but unreachable in envoy-go's static-bootstrap-only model (08.1 SPEC §11.7).

**Empirical evidence (verbatim Envoy v1.37.2 `/server_info`, first 70 lines):** see 08.1 SPEC §11.4.

**Equivalence claim.** Body byte-equal modulo: `version`, `uptime_current_epoch`, `uptime_all_epochs`, `command_line_options.*` (subset on envoy-go side; Envoy emits ~40 fields), `hot_restart_version`, `node.*` (same allow-list as `/config_dump`). The `state` field is byte-equal (`"LIVE"` on both sides post-MarkReady without drain).

**Equivalence claim extension (08.2).** The `state` field IS asserted byte-equal across both proxies in DRAINING (`"DRAINING"` literal, per 08.2 SPEC §11.2 empirical pin). The 08.1 byte-equal claim for `"LIVE"` post-MarkReady is unchanged.

**Forward-pointer note.** ADR-0088 is **amended** by ADR-0098 (NOT superseded — purely additive per ADR-0088 consequence (c) verbatim). The ADR-0088 amendment record adds DRAINING to the enum-coverage table and refers to ADR-0098 for the timing semantics.

### /drain_listeners

*Introduced by phase 08.2. Justified by ADR-0093 (method discrimination; partially amends ADR-0090) and ADR-0097 (drain trigger semantics).*

**Body shape (POST).** `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`. Body verbatim `OK\n` (3 bytes; capital `OK` followed by single newline) per 08.2 SPEC §11.1 empirical pin against Envoy v1.37.2. Status 200 OK. The handler is fire-and-forget — 200 OK is emitted BEFORE drain completes; the operator polls /ready or /server_info to observe drain progress. Idempotent — subsequent POSTs during DRAINING return 200 with the same body without re-firing the drain trigger (sync.Once-guarded internally).

**Method discrimination.** Non-POST methods (GET, PUT, DELETE, HEAD) return `405 Method Not Allowed` with body `Method <METHOD> not allowed, POST required.\n` per 08.2 SPEC §11.4 empirical pin. This is the FIRST admin endpoint in envoy-go with method enforcement; partially amends ADR-0090's no-method-discrimination posture (which applies uniformly to read-only endpoints; ADR-0093 records the qualification).

**`?graceful=true` query-param.** Silently accepted (per ADR-0041's silent-ignore precedent). envoy-go's drain is always graceful by construction (the three-state machine has no non-graceful immediate-stop variant); the query-param has no semantic effect.

**Side effects.** First POST: `drain.Manager.Drain()` called (Live → Draining transition); subsequent POSTs: no-op. The endpoint does NOT trigger process exit — the operator-driven drain stays in DRAINING indefinitely until SIGTERM/SIGINT (or kill -9).

**Cross-trigger note.** Upstream Envoy v1.37.2 separates the listener-side drain (POST /drain_listeners — does NOT flip /ready or /server_info to DRAINING) from the load-balancer-disposition flip (POST /healthcheck/fail — DOES flip /ready and /server_info to DRAINING). envoy-go's MVP UNIFIES these triggers under a single drain manager: POST /drain_listeners DOES flip /ready and /server_info to DRAINING in envoy-go (the BODY shapes match Envoy verbatim per §11.2; the TRIGGERS differ at the wiring level). The differential gate's per-proxy trigger script normalizes per 08.2 SPEC §7.2.

**Empirical evidence (verbatim Envoy v1.37.2 `POST /drain_listeners`):** see 08.2 SPEC §11.1.

**Empirical evidence (verbatim Envoy v1.37.2 `GET/PUT/DELETE/HEAD /drain_listeners`):** see 08.2 SPEC §11.4.

**Equivalence claim.** Body byte-equal to reference Envoy v1.37.2 (after framing dechunk). Method-discrimination behavior asserted byte-equal — non-POST returns 405 with the templated body across both proxies. Header set inherits the umbrella rules.

**Forward-pointer note.** ADR-0090 (no-ACL admin-endpoint security posture; no method discrimination on read-only endpoints) is **partially amended** by ADR-0093: the no-ACL posture is preserved verbatim; the no-method-discrimination posture is qualified to read-only endpoints only.

### /stats

*Introduced by phase 32.1 (`network-filter-redis-upstream-pool-seam-and-codec`). Justified by D-S32.1-5 (the 32.1 `StatsAsserter` flat-`/stats` scrape requirement — the `redis.<stat_prefix>.` and `cluster.<name>.*` names not yet in `/stats/prometheus` pending the 32.2 `redis.` tag-extractor arm). Implemented in `internal/admin/stats.go`; routed through `writeAdminHeaders` (the shared 4-header helper).*

**Body shape.** `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`. One stat per line in `name: value\n` format (LF line endings, no trailing blank line), sorted ascending by internal stat name. All registered stats are emitted at their current integer value. This is the flat internal-name text form — the counterpart to `/stats/prometheus` (which applies the `name.go` tag-extractor arms and emits Prometheus text exposition format). envoy-go-strict endpoint (upstream Envoy's flat `/stats` text form differs in detail; this endpoint is introduced for the internal-name `StatsAsserter` scrape — not a byte-equivalence target against the reference).

**Equivalence claim.** NOT asserted byte-equal to reference Envoy's `/stats` (upstream Envoy's flat stat text uses a different format and namespace). The `0055` `StatsAsserter` scrapes THIS endpoint on BOTH sides (reference + subject) and compares the NAMED stat values by internal name (both sides use the same internal names for `redis.<sp>.*` + `cluster.<name>.*`), so the cross-side value equality is the meaningful assertion — not body byte-equality of the entire document.

**Header set.** Inherits the umbrella rules (all eight admin endpoints share the `writeAdminHeaders` 4-header set: `content-type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`, `cache-control: no-cache, max-age=0`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `date`, `server: envoy`).

### Applies to

- phase 08.1 and phase 08.2 envoy-go admin subsystem.
- all eight endpoints: `/ready`, `/stats/prometheus`, `/config_dump`, `/clusters`, `/listeners`, `/server_info`, `POST /drain_listeners` (08.2 NEW), `GET /stats` (32.1 NEW — flat internal-name text; `name: value\n`, sorted; introduced for the `0055` `StatsAsserter` scrape, D-S32.1-5).
- `/ready` DRAINING-state body `DRAINING\n` (503; ADR-0097 partially supersedes ADR-0015).
- `/server_info` DRAINING-state `state: "DRAINING"` (ADR-0098 amends ADR-0088).
- ENVOY_TARGET pin v1.37.2 (contrib) at `sha256:7edd5b0fd763d32c3dfcfd0061f9c2ea63eebd8cdf7f88d974d3adfc99453be8` (ADR-0227, superseding ADR-0008).

### Does not yet apply to

- HTTP/2 over admin (admin stays HTTP/1.1).
- TLS on admin (admin stays plaintext).
- Other mutating endpoints — `POST /reset_counters`, `POST /quitquitquit`, `POST /healthcheck/*`, `POST /reopen_logs`, `POST /runtime_modify`, `POST /logging` deferred per ADR-0089.
- JSON form of `/clusters` and `/listeners` — `?format=json` deferred per ADR-0089.
- Query-param filtering on `/config_dump` — `?resource=`, `?mask=`, `?include_eds=` deferred per ADR-0089.
- `RoutesConfigDump`, `SecretsConfigDump`, `ScopedRoutesConfigDump`, `EndpointsConfigDump` envelopes deferred per ADR-0089.
- Other deferred admin endpoints — `/runtime`, `/certs`, `/memory`, `/heap_dump`, `/cpuprofiler`, `/heapprofiler`, `/contention`, `/logging`, `/listeners/<name>/*`, `/init_dump` deferred per ADR-0089.
- ACL / authentication on admin port (no-ACL posture per ADR-0090).
- Method discrimination on read-only endpoints (Envoy parity per SPEC §11.8; 405 enforcement deferred for read-only; mutating endpoint /drain_listeners DOES enforce per ADR-0093).
- Path normalization beyond Go stdlib `http.ServeMux` (trailing-slash returns Go stdlib `404 page not found`, NOT Envoy's admin help page; allow-listed for trailing-slash behavior — envoy-go's body diverges from Envoy's body, but the status code matches).

## Graceful drain

The envoy-go drain machinery transitions the process from LIVE → DRAINING → exit (via SIGTERM/SIGINT) or LIVE → DRAINING (via POST /drain_listeners; no exit). The state machine lives in the `internal/drain` package (08.2 NEW; ADR-0091); the drain manager is a single-instance lock-free state machine with three states (LIVE / DRAINING / DRAINED) and an in-flight counter.

### Drain triggers

Two operator workflows trigger drain in envoy-go:

1. **SIGTERM or SIGINT:** drain-then-exit. The signal causes `cmd/envoy-go/main.go`'s top-level context to cancel; the main goroutine then calls `drain.Manager.Drain()`, waits on `drain.Manager.Done()` (or a 30s timeout per ADR-0095), then proceeds to per-cluster connection-pool teardown + listener-socket close + admin server close + access-log flush. The total drain window is bounded by the 30s timeout.

   **Deliberate divergence from Envoy v1.37.2** (per 08.2 SPEC §11.7 empirical pin): upstream Envoy v1.37.2 SIGTERM is immediate-exit-without-drain (the log shows `caught ENVOY_SIGTERM` → `shutting down server instance` → `exiting` within ~7ms; no drain delay). envoy-go's design choice (ADR-0092) is to honor the operator-ergonomic expectation that SIGTERM = graceful drain (the dominant Kubernetes / cluster-orchestrator workflow). The differential equivalence claim does NOT exercise the SIGTERM path; the divergence is contract-level.

2. **POST /drain_listeners admin endpoint:** drain-without-exit. The handler triggers `drain.Manager.Drain()` synchronously and returns 200 OK before drain completes. The proxy stays running in DRAINING indefinitely; the operator separately issues SIGTERM/SIGINT (or kill -9) at a later time to actually exit.

Both triggers result in the same drain BEHAVIOR (state transition, listener stop-accepting, in-flight completion, /ready and /server_info responses). They differ only in the post-drain disposition (exit vs. stay-running).

### Drain semantics

When drain fires (state transitions LIVE → DRAINING):

- **New connections rejected via accept-then-FIN.** The Listener Accept loop's fast-path checks `drain.Manager.IsDraining()` on each iteration; an Accept-ed conn during DRAINING is immediately closed (`conn.Close()` → kernel sends FIN) without filter-chain dispatch. Per 08.2 SPEC §11.5 empirical pin: the TCP 3-way handshake completes; the client observes "Empty reply from server" on its first read attempt. NOT listener-socket-close (which would produce kernel RST-on-no-listener for new connections).

- **In-flight requests complete normally.** The HCM filter chain's `decodeHeaders`/`encodeFinalize` pair calls `drain.Manager.Inc()`/`Dec()` to track per-request in-flight count; the drain manager's `Done()` channel closes when the in-flight counter reaches 0 (or the 30s timeout fires). Per 08.2 SPEC §11.3 empirical pin: in-flight HTTP/1.1 requests during drain receive full body delivery with status 200 (no abort), and the response carries NO `Connection: close` header — the keep-alive connection remains open after the response (subsequent requests on the same conn extend the drain window via further Inc calls; deliberate MVP simplification, per-conn drainable-close-at-next-idle-window deferred).

- **TCP-proxy connections complete at connection-close.** TCP-proxy filter's `OnNewConnection`/`OnConnectionClose` pair calls `Inc()`/`Dec()` per connection (correct because TCP-proxy has no per-request semantic).

- **/ready returns 503 DRAINING\n** (per 08.2 SPEC §11.2 verbatim). Operators / load balancers observe the DRAINING signal and stop sending traffic.

- **/server_info returns `state: "DRAINING"`** (per ADR-0098 amending ADR-0088).

- **Idempotent.** Subsequent Drain() calls (e.g., a second POST /drain_listeners, or SIGTERM after a prior /drain_listeners) no-op — the state transition has already fired (sync.Once-guarded).

### Drain timeout

The drain timeout is a hardcoded 30s in envoy-go MVP (per ADR-0095). Envoy v1.37.2's default is 600s (per 08.2 SPEC §11.7 + 08.1 SPEC §11.4 verbatim `"drain_time": "600s"`). The divergence is deliberate to keep test-suite cost tractable; the drain BEHAVIOR is the equivalence claim, not the timeout VALUE. Operator-knob to configure the timeout is deferred to a future runtime / hot-restart family phase.

The drain strategy in upstream Envoy v1.37.2 is `"Gradual"` (the only strategy in the v1.37.2 default-config flow per 08.2 SPEC §11.7 + 08.1 SPEC §11.4). envoy-go's drain is graceful-by-construction (no IMMEDIATE strategy); the strategy concept is not modeled.

### Connection-level drain semantics

Phase 08.2 does NOT implement per-connection drainable closure at next-idle-window (Envoy supports this via `drain_strategy: "Gradual"`'s back-off). HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections during drain do NOT receive `Connection: close` on the in-flight response (per 08.2 SPEC §11.3 empirical pin matching Envoy parity); subsequent requests on the same conn during DRAINING are processed normally (extending the drain window). HTTP/2 connections during drain emit GOAWAY at drain-trigger (envoy-go MVP design choice; not asserted differentially per 08.2 SPEC §2.1 deferral note).

### Drain manager API surface

- `internal/drain.New(timeout time.Duration) *drain.Manager` — constructor; state initialized to Live.
- `(m *Manager).State() drain.State` — atomic load; returns Live or Draining.
- `(m *Manager).Drain()` — sync.Once-guarded; transitions Live → Draining; arms the Done rendezvous.
- `(m *Manager).Done() <-chan struct{}` — channel closes when inflight reaches 0 after Drain has fired.
- `(m *Manager).Inc()` / `(m *Manager).Dec()` — atomic increment/decrement of inflight counter.
- `(m *Manager).IsDraining() bool` — Listener Accept-loop fast-path; equivalent to State() == Draining.
- `(m *Manager).Timeout() time.Duration` — returns the configured timeout (read-only).

### Applies to

- phase 08.2 envoy-go drain subsystem.
- the SIGTERM/SIGINT-handler in `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` (ADR-0092; deliberate divergence from Envoy parity).
- the POST /drain_listeners admin endpoint (ADR-0093; method discrimination per Envoy parity).
- the /ready DRAINING-state body (ADR-0097; partially supersedes ADR-0015).
- the /server_info DRAINING-state field (ADR-0098; amends ADR-0088).
- ENVOY_TARGET pin v1.37.2 (contrib) at `sha256:7edd5b0fd763d32c3dfcfd0061f9c2ea63eebd8cdf7f88d974d3adfc99453be8` (ADR-0227, superseding ADR-0008).

### Does not yet apply to

- Hot restart / parent-child handoff (deferred to runtime / hot-restart family per ADR-0099).
- POST /quitquitquit endpoint (semantic overlap with SIGTERM + /drain_listeners; deferred per ADR-0089 + ADR-0099).
- POST /healthcheck/fail endpoint (envoy-go MVP unifies the listener-drain and load-balancer-disposition triggers under /drain_listeners + the drain manager; /healthcheck/fail stays deferred per ADR-0089).
- Per-listener selective drain (`/listeners/<name>/drain` admin sub-routes deferred per ADR-0089).
- `drain_strategy` per-listener (default GRADUAL only; IMMEDIATE strategy deferred).
- Configurable drain timeout (hardcoded 30s; operator-knob deferred per ADR-0095).
- Per-connection drainable closure at next-idle-window.
- Drain manager interaction with xDS (no xDS yet; deferred).
- HTTP/3 drain semantics (no H3 in MVP; deferred to HTTP/3 + QUIC family).
- Drain progress JSON body on /server_info (envoy-go matches Envoy's empty-of-this-field behavior).
- `Connection: drain` custom response header (Envoy emits no such header per 08.2 SPEC §11.3).
- Multi-instance drain coordination (operator's load-balancer responsibility).

## Test harness host networking

Rules governing how fixtures reach a host-side backend from inside the reference Envoy container. These rules are harness-runtime constraints (not equivalence-matrix dimensions), but they are part of the contract because they determine whether a fixture is valid on the pinned reference image.

### DNS — `host.docker.internal` requires `dns_lookup_family: V4_ONLY`

Every fixture whose reference bootstrap uses `host.docker.internal` as a cluster endpoint address MUST set `dns_lookup_family: V4_ONLY` on that cluster.

- **Introduced by:** phase 00 (fixture `0000-tcp-echo`).
- **Justification ADR:** `ADR-0010` in `DECISIONS.md`.
- **Rule:** a `STRICT_DNS` (or other DNS-resolving) cluster whose `socket_address.address` is the literal string `host.docker.internal` must carry `dns_lookup_family: V4_ONLY` at the cluster level.
- **Reason:** Docker Desktop (Linux) resolves `host.docker.internal` to both IPv4 and IPv6 records. Envoy's DNS resolver, left to default (`AUTO`), may select the IPv6 record, which Docker Desktop does not bridge from container to host — the connection fails with "Network is unreachable" and the differential run stalls until the context deadline. `V4_ONLY` eliminates the selection and keeps the fixture deterministic across Docker Desktop, CI runners, and docker-ce hosts.
- **Applies to:** TCP, HTTP/1.1, and HTTP/2 fixtures on this pin.
- **Does not yet apply to:** HTTP/3 / QUIC fixtures — QUIC is UDP and the dual-stack routing behavior differs; the rule must be re-evaluated (via a superseding ADR) when the first QUIC fixture lands.
- **Host-side backend bind address:** because the Docker-provided host gateway on Docker Desktop is a non-loopback IP, host-side test backends MUST bind to `0.0.0.0` (not `127.0.0.1`). A loopback-only bind is unreachable from the container.
- **`extra_hosts` wiring:** CI and developer environments typically need `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` on the reference container (set via `testcontainers-go`'s `HostConfigModifier` in `test/differential/harness.go`). Fixtures inherit this from the harness; they do not re-declare it.

Future fixtures that need a different reachability pattern (e.g. container-to-container, or IPv6-on-purpose) add a new rule under this heading via ADR. The V4_ONLY rule above is never silently relaxed — any deviation is an ADR that explicitly supersedes ADR-0010 on the relevant scope.

## TCP proxy

*Introduced by phase 02. Justified by ADR-0024 (per-cluster RR scope) and SPEC §5.4 / §5.5 / §5.8.*

### Response-body byte-equivalence (asserted)

For any fixture whose subject and reference both terminate a TCP connection through `envoy.filters.network.tcp_proxy` (proto `envoy.extensions.filters.network.tcp_proxy.v3.TcpProxy`) backed by a STATIC (subject) or STRICT_DNS (reference) cluster of echo backends, the differential harness compares the concatenated **response bodies** byte-for-byte. Trivially holds for echo backends (each backend reflects the request bytes); for non-echo backends a phase-specific subsection extends this rule.

### Half-close propagation (asserted)

Both proxies must propagate `CloseWrite()` (FIN on the write side) from downstream-to-upstream and from upstream-to-downstream independently — i.e., the dataplane is a true bidirectional pipe with independent half-closes, not a request-response pair. Phase 02 inherits this property from phase 00's `netConn` + `halfClose` byte pump (lifted verbatim per ADR-0023).

### Load-balancer endpoint-selection sequence (NOT asserted)

Cross-proxy LB endpoint-selection sequence is **not** a differential equivalence dimension. Each proxy must be RR-correct **in its own right** (per-proxy distribution): for an N-pick run against a cluster of M endpoints, the per-backend accept count distribution must equal a perfect mod-M partition when `M | N`. This is a **local correctness property** asserted via the optional `DistributionAsserter` interface in `test/differential/fixture/fixture.go`.

The cross-proxy sequence is not asserted because:
- Upstream Envoy's RR LB is per-worker-thread with a randomized starting offset; the absolute sequence of endpoints selected for N consecutive connections is not reproducible across runs or workers.
- The envoy-go subject's RR is per-cluster with a deterministic starting point at index 0 (ADR-0024 + SPEC §5.4 sequence-starts-at-0 invariant); the sequence is reproducible within a single subject process but does not match upstream's randomized sequence.

A phase that needs cross-proxy LB sequence equivalence (e.g., a hash-based LB phase under the load-balancing family) supersedes this subsection with a new ADR documenting the assertion mechanism. Reference-side distribution exactness (fixture `0001-tcp-proxy-rr` and, inherited, `0002-tls-tcp`) depends on the reference container's `--concurrency 1` pin per ADR-0028.

### Load balancer — least_request (LEAST_REQUEST)

*Introduced by phase 34 (the Load-balancing family OPENS). Justified by ADR-0232 (the LB acquire/release seam) + ADR-0233 (the least_request policy).*

Phase 34 lands the project's first LB policy beyond phase-02 ROUND_ROBIN. `cluster.Manager` accepts `Cluster.LbPolicy LEAST_REQUEST` on the LEGACY enum path (the same path ROUND_ROBIN uses; the `Cluster.load_balancing_policy` extension point stays deferred).

**Acceptance + config (`Cluster.LeastRequestLbConfig`, the `lb_config` oneof member field 37).** `choice_count` defaults to **2** when the config is absent (or a mismatched oneof member is set — see below); when set it must be **`>= 2`** (a hand-rolled PGV-parity gate — the manager calls no PGV); a set value is used **verbatim with NO clamp** at `choice_count > len(endpoints)` (reference parity — a legal config, e.g. `choice_count: 10` over 3 endpoints, makes the policy quasi-deterministic).

**P2C selection semantics (the upstream v1.37.2 mirror).** Un-weighted power-of-two-choices: sample `choice_count` host indices **with replacement** (`rng() % n` per draw — duplicates possible, no clamp); pick the host with the **strictly fewest** outstanding active requests (strict `<` on the raw per-endpoint active count); **first-drawn wins ties**. The weighted `weight/(active+1)^bias` formula belongs to upstream's EDF path, which engages ONLY under unequal host weights or slow_start — the equal-weight MVP takes pure P2C, and `active_request_bias` never enters the computation. The RNG is a crypto-seeded mutex-guarded `math/rand/v2` PCG (injectable in tests). The per-endpoint active counters are LB-internal `atomic.Int64` state, NOT registry stats.

**cx-as-rq active-count semantics (the active counter's unit).** The per-endpoint counter counts **open connections attributable to a pick**: +1 at `Pick` (conn-producing paths), −1 at the connection's final Close (or immediately on dial failure / non-conn picks). For TCP-proxied traffic this is EXACTLY the reference's semantics (live-pinned: per-host `rq_active == cx_active` 1:1; tcp_proxy charges one rq per cx). For the H1 connection pool, an idle pooled connection RETAINS its +1 hold from dial until its FINAL close (caller close, `PutIdleH1` overflow drop, or `closePool` drain) — real upstream load, the documented HTTP idle-pooled-conn approximation boundary.

**Per-side RNG non-equivalence (NOT cross-side-exact; band-proven).** Both proxies' P2C selection is RNG-driven on independent streams (upstream's RNG is per-worker-thread crypto-seeded; the subject's is per-cluster crypto-seeded), so the absolute selection sequence is NEVER cross-side-equal. Fixture `0059-lb-least-request` proves the policy DISTRIBUTIONALLY via the FIRST band-based `AssertDistribution` use (a hold-4/burst-60 skew workload over 3 reused `TCPEcho` backends at `choice_count: 10`): asserted **PER SIDE** as {conservation `c1+c2+c3 == 64`, starvation `c1 <= 12`, concentration `c2 >= 16`} on the sorted per-backend accept counts. Each band leg is proven live by a deliberate-break under `-count=1` (an inverted comparison fails concentration; a no-op release fails starvation; a corrupt `StatsAsserter` want fails the stats prong).

**Departures + coverage boundaries (recorded here per the §9 byte-stable-reject lineage):**
- **NEW lb-policy reject text.** The remaining `CLUSTER_PROVIDED`/`LOAD_BALANCING_POLICY_CONFIG` are rejected at config-parse with `cluster: %q: unsupported lb_policy %s (supported: ROUND_ROBIN, LEAST_REQUEST, RANDOM, RING_HASH, MAGLEV)` — the supported-list extended at phase 37 (MAGLEV retired from the rejected set → the FIFTH accepted policy; see `### Load balancer — maglev (MAGLEV)` below). `CLUSTER_PROVIDED` is now the LONE recorded LB-policy departure / retarget trigger: the reference parse-ACCEPTS the five enum-path policies envoy-go accepts, so envoy-go's continued rejection of `CLUSTER_PROVIDED` (which needs a cluster-supplied LB the static path has no shape for) is the next departure. No fixture pins the text (it lands unit-level in `manager_test.go`, whose `TestManager_Error_UnsupportedLBPolicy` doubly-hit-RETARGETED its trigger from `Cluster_MAGLEV` — now accepted — to `Cluster_CLUSTER_PROVIDED`, the phase-34/35/36 accept-of-N-forces-retarget-to-N+1 pattern).
- **`active_request_bias` / `slow_start_config` DEPARTURE rejects.** Set under `lb_policy: LEAST_REQUEST` → rejected at config-parse (the reference parse-accepts them and they alter its picks; `slow_start_config` engages the reference's EDF path, and `active_request_bias` goes live the instant host weights become unequal — a dimension envoy-go silently ignores entirely). Fail-fast rather than silently diverging (the thrift AMEND-T7 lineage).
- **Mismatched `lb_config` oneof member — silent-ignore (PARITY).** A mismatched oneof member (e.g. `ring_hash_lb_config` under `LEAST_REQUEST`, or `least_request_lb_config` under `ROUND_ROBIN`) is silently ignored — reference parity (validate-accepts silently) AND behavior-inert (both sides default identically: `GetLeastRequestLbConfig()` nil → choice_count 2). The existing under-ROUND_ROBIN posture stays byte-stable.
- **Direct-pick consumers' load invisibility (coverage note).** The two non-conn `PickEndpoint()` consumers — httpclient's `request.URL.Host` rewrite + the thriftproxy pick-without-dial no-healthy-host probe — release IMMEDIATELY (they hold no connection), so their picks are invisible to least_request's active counters. A documented coverage boundary, not a bug.
- **`upstream_rq_total` per-side on the TCP path.** On `0059`'s stats prong: cross-equal `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_total == 64` + `membership_total == 3` + `upstream_cx_active == 0` (quiesced); PER-SIDE `upstream_rq_total` (reference = 64 [tcp_proxy charges rq-per-cx]; subject = 0 [the tcpproxy path never calls `IncUpstreamRqTotal` — a pre-existing boundary this fixture pins]).
- **NO new fuzzer / NO new BackendKind (deliberate firsts).** Phase 34 decodes no wire bytes → NO new fuzzer (the FIRST no-fuzzer phase since the fuzzing regime began; a manufactured fuzzer over no decoder is a dead assertion). `0059` reuses `TCPEcho` → NO new BackendKind (tail stays 33).
- **Stat surface UNCHANGED at 1116.** ZERO lb-policy stat-name delta (live-confirmed empty `/stats` name-set diff between LEAST_REQUEST and ROUND_ROBIN; the reference's `cluster.<name>.lb_*` roster exists identically-at-0 under both policies and is NOT mirrored — unchanged posture). The FIRST zero-stat-delta phase since the surface began moving.

### Load balancer — random (RANDOM)

*Introduced by phase 35 (the Load-balancing family's SECOND row). Justified by ADR-0234 (the random policy); REUSES the ADR-0232 LB acquire/release seam UNCHANGED (the seam's FIRST reuse).*

Phase 35 lands the project's THIRD LB policy (after phase-02 ROUND_ROBIN + phase-34 LEAST_REQUEST). `cluster.Manager` accepts `Cluster.LbPolicy RANDOM` on the LEGACY enum path (the same path ROUND_ROBIN + LEAST_REQUEST use; the `Cluster.load_balancing_policy` extension point stays deferred).

**Acceptance (NO config message).** RANDOM has NO config message — `Cluster.RandomLbConfig` does not exist in the v1.32.4 surface (zero config knobs; the simplest family surface). The manager's `case clusterv3.Cluster_RANDOM` is a BARE construction: `newRandom(endpoints)` — NO config-parse arm, NO PGV gate. (RANDOM's locality-weighting config lives only on the deferred `load_balancing_policies.random.v3` extension-point proto.)

**Uniform-pick semantics (the upstream v1.37.2 mirror).** Stateless uniform random: ONE draw `i := int(rng() % uint64(n))`, return `endpoints[i]` — mirroring upstream `RandomLoadBalancer::peekOrChoose` EXACTLY. It consults NO active counters, runs NO power-of-two loop, holds NO per-pick state, and applies NO tie-break (the contrast with least_request's P2C, which draws `choice_count` times and picks the strictly-fewest-active host). The RNG is the SAME crypto-seeded mutex-guarded `math/rand/v2` PCG least_request uses (the package-private `newPCGRNG()` helper, REUSED verbatim — `random.go` calls it directly, no extraction; injectable via `newRandomWithRNG` in tests). `randomLB` returns the shared `noopRelease` (it holds no per-endpoint state — the seam's "zero cost" reuse).

**Healthy-set boundary (no health checking → all-hosts sampling).** Healthy-host filtering happens upstream of the pick in the reference's shared base (priority/healthy/panic); with no health checking, envoy-go's RANDOM degenerates to all-hosts sampling (the Upstream-robustness family's boundary — the same posture as least_request).

**Per-side RNG non-equivalence (NOT cross-side-exact; band-proven).** Both proxies' selection is RNG-driven on independent crypto-seeded streams, so the absolute selection sequence is NEVER cross-side-equal. Fixture `0060-lb-random` proves RANDOM STAYS uniform DISTRIBUTIONALLY via the SECOND band-based `AssertDistribution` use — the REUSED `0059` hold-4/burst-60 skew stimulus over 3 reused `TCPEcho` backends, with the assertion INVERTED (the contrapositive of least_request): asserted **PER SIDE** as {conservation `c1+c2+c3 == 64`, uniform-floor `each >= 6`, uniform-ceiling `each <= 40`} on the per-backend accept counts. RANDOM stays uniform-band DESPITE the held-conn load imbalance (it never consults the counters), where least_request would skew away from the held endpoint. Each band leg is proven live by a deliberate-break under `-count=1` (see below).

**Departures + coverage boundaries:**
- **Mismatched `lb_config` oneof member — silent-ignore (PARITY).** A mismatched oneof member (e.g. `least_request_lb_config` or `ring_hash_lb_config` set under `RANDOM`) is silently ignored — reference parity AND behavior-inert (the `lb_config` oneof has NO `random` member, so the manager never reads it on the RANDOM path). The construction is unconditionally bare.
- **D-S35-2 shared-RNG-message cosmetic note.** `newRandom` calls the shared `newPCGRNG()` directly and ACCEPTS its seed-error message verbatim — `"cluster: least_request: seed rng"`. This path is reachable ONLY on a `crypto/rand` read failure (effectively unreachable); the `least_request:` prefix under a RANDOM cluster is a recorded COSMETIC note, NOT a behavior divergence (a wrapper would double-wrap or force an edit to `newPCGRNG`, which the SPEC AMEND-R5 forbids).
- **The 0060 anti-skew band re-tune (IMPL-time empirical amendment to D-S35-3).** The SPEC anticipated `{floor 12, ceiling 32}` (~2.5σ), which empirically FLAKED 2/20 on the natural multinomial tail (`P(X<12) ≈ 0.0032`, `P(X>32) ≈ 0.0020` per sample; 6 samples/run). The PLAN's pinned PRINCIPLE {conservation + uniform-floor + uniform-ceiling} authorized widening within the band; the constants were re-tuned at IMPL Task 6 to `{floor 6, ceiling 40}` (~4–5σ; per-sample `P(X<6) ≈ 2e-6`, `P(X>40) ≈ 3e-7`) — proven flake-free over **60/60** runs (two `-count=20` batches + the 3 `-count=1` breaks; observed per-backend extremes 14–31, comfortably inside `[6,40]`). The wider band STILL bites all three deliberate breaks. Final constants: `K=4` held, `S=60` burst, `sum==64`, `uniformFloor=6`, `uniformCeiling=40`.
- **The 3 deliberate-break liveness proofs (`-count=1`, go-test caching defeated).** (i) `case Cluster_RANDOM`'s `newRandom(endpoints)` → `newLeastRequest(endpoints, …)` (the canonical anti-skew break — least_request consults the held-conn counters) fails the uniform FLOOR (`backend[1]=2 < 6`); (ii) `Pick`'s `rng() % n` → `0` (single-host pin) fails the uniform CEILING (`backend[0]=64 > 40`); (iii) the `StatsAsserter` `upstream_cx_total` want 64 → 99 fails the stats prong (both sides observe 64). Each: applied → `-count=1` FAIL → `git restore` → diff-clean; never committed broken.
- **NO new fuzzer / NO new BackendKind (now family expectations).** RANDOM decodes no wire bytes → NO new fuzzer (fuzzers stay **42**). `0060` reuses `TCPEcho` → NO new BackendKind (tail stays **33**). These are the phase-34 family-level firsts, now ESTABLISHED expectations.
- **Stat surface UNCHANGED at 1116 (the SECOND zero-delta phase).** ZERO lb-policy stat-name delta (live-confirmed empty `/stats` name-set diff between RANDOM and ROUND_ROBIN, 455 == 455). The `0060` `StatsAsserter` set: `upstream_cx_total`/`membership_total`/quiesced-active CROSS-EQUAL; `upstream_rq_total` PER-SIDE (reference = 64 [tcp_proxy charges rq-per-cx]; subject = 0 [the tcpproxy path never calls `IncUpstreamRqTotal`] — the same boundary `0059` pins).

### Load balancer — ring_hash (RING_HASH)

*Introduced by phase 36.1 (the Load-balancing family's THIRD row; the project's FIRST consistent-hashing policy). Justified by ADR-0236 (the ring_hash policy) + ADR-0235 (the LB hash-key seam extension — the seam's FIRST extension, the ADR-0232 PICK-INPUT half). The 36.1 leg lands the seam + the `ringHashLB` + the manager gate + the tcp_proxy `source_ip` plane; the 36.2 leg adds the HTTP route `hash_policy` plane.*

Phase 36.1 lands the project's FOURTH LB policy (after phase-02 ROUND_ROBIN + phase-34 LEAST_REQUEST + phase-35 RANDOM) and its FIRST consistent-hashing policy. `cluster.Manager` accepts `Cluster.LbPolicy RING_HASH` (`envoy.config.cluster.v3`, enum value 2) on the LEGACY enum path (the same path the other three use; the `Cluster.load_balancing_policy` extension point stays deferred).

**Acceptance + the `RingHashLbConfig` two-layer gate.** `lb_policy: RING_HASH` with no `ring_hash_lb_config` is accepted with the defaults {minimum_ring_size 1024, maximum_ring_size 8388608, hash_function XX_HASH} (the manager self-supplies the doc-comment defaults — the v1.32.4 zero value is nil, NOT generated). `ring_hash_lb_config` carries `minimum_ring_size` (proto field 1), `hash_function` (field 3 — `XX_HASH`=0 default / `MURMUR_HASH_2`=1), `maximum_ring_size` (field 4). The HAND-ROLLED gate (the manager calls no PGV — the phase-34 `choice_count` precedent) mirrors the reference's TWO validation layers byte-for-byte: (a) the PGV per-field bound — `minimum_ring_size`/`maximum_ring_size` `> 8388608` → `cluster: %q: ring_hash_lb_config.{minimum,maximum}_ring_size: value must be less than or equal to 8388608`; (b) the RUNTIME cross-field check — `minimum_ring_size > maximum_ring_size` (post-default) → `cluster: %q: ring hash: minimum_ring_size (%d) > maximum_ring_size (%d)` (distinct wording from the PGV layer; there is NO `min ≤ max` PGV rule — AMEND-RH1). All reject arms land UNIT-LEVEL in `manager_test.go` (NO cross-side boot-reject dir — no fixture pins them; both sides reject identically).

**Ketama consistent-hash ring semantics (the upstream v1.37.2 mirror).** The `ringHashLB` (`internal/cluster/ringhash.go`) builds an immutable ring ONCE at construction, mirroring `RingHashLoadBalancer` EXACTLY: for each endpoint, `ceil(minimum_ring_size / N)` ring points (the equal-weight MVP — the running-sum scale formula collapses to this under equal weights; weighted-ring richness deferred), each keyed `hash("<addr>:<port>_<i>")` (`_` literal + decimal index, no padding) — `xxHash64(key)` seed 0 for the default `XX_HASH`, `murmurHash2(key, 0xc70f6907)` for `MURMUR_HASH_2`; the points are sorted ascending by hash. `Pick(hashKey, hasHash)` binary-searches (`sort.Search`) for the first ring point `>= hashKey`, wrapping to index 0 past the end. The no-hash fallback (`hasHash == false`) draws a UNIFORM random ring position from the injected rng — Envoy's documented "effectively the random LB" fallback (`thread_aware_lb_impl.cc`). For the default 3-equal-host cluster: `size = 3 * ceil(1024/3) = 3 * 342 = 1026`, `min = max = 342` (matched against the live reference — D-S36-5). Both hash functions are IMPLEMENTED (parse + ring build); the differential fixtures use the `XX_HASH` default (cross-side-reproducible), `MURMUR_HASH_2` is unit-level.

**The seam EXTENSION (ADR-0235; the ADR-0232 PICK-INPUT half; the ctx-carried hash key).** The unexported `loadBalancer.Pick` widens from `Pick() (Endpoint, func(), error)` to `Pick(hashKey uint64, hasHash bool) (Endpoint, func(), error)` — the two-scalar `(value, ok)` form (chosen over `*uint64` and a `pickOptions` struct). The three incumbent policies (roundRobin/leastRequest/randomLB) add two IGNORED params — behavior-neutral, so all prior fixtures stay byte-identical. The hash key rides `context.Context`: an unexported `hashKeyCtxKey struct{}` + an EXPORTED additive `cluster.WithHashKey(ctx, key)` (the producers live in OTHER packages) + an unexported `hashKeyFrom(ctx) (uint64, bool)`, all in `cluster.go` (the ADR-0219 ctx-carry precedent). `Dial`/`AcquireH1` extract the key and thread it to `c.lb.Pick(hk, ok)` in 2 changed lines each; their EXPORTED signatures — and `PickEndpoint()` (which passes `(0, false)` → the no-hash fallback) — stay BYTE-STABLE (the OPTION-C discipline preserved). The TWO new exported symbols are the additive `cluster.WithHashKey` (the ctx stuffer) + `cluster.HashSourceIP(addr string) uint64` (the bare-client-IP `xxHash64` helper the tcp plane uses); NO existing method signature changes. The RELEASE half (ADR-0232) is REUSED unchanged (`ringHashLB` returns the shared `noopRelease` — the ring is immutable, no per-pick state). This is the seam's FIRST extension and the durable asset maglev (and any future hash policy) reuses unchanged — the analogue of ADR-0232 (the RELEASE half) for the PICK-INPUT half.

**The two data planes (tcp `source_ip` at 36.1; HTTP route `hash_policy` at 36.2).** The hash key is supplied by BOTH planes. The 36.1 tcp plane: `tcp_proxy` parses `hash_policy: [{source_ip: {}}]` and, per new connection, computes `cluster.HashSourceIP(downstream.RemoteAddr)` = `xxHash64(bare client IP, NO port)` seed 0 and stuffs it via `cluster.WithHashKey` before `Dial(ctx)` (a non-source_ip tcp `hash_policy` specifier — e.g. filter_state — is DEPARTURE-rejected).
