The 36.2 HTTP plane (deferred to the 36.2 IMPL): the router route-level `hash_policy` — HEADER (`xxHash64(value)`) + connection-properties `source_ip` (the tcp-identical compute), combined `hash = rotl64(prev, 1) ^ new_hash` (rotate-left-1 then XOR, policy-list order, first contributor seeded from 0) with a `terminal=true` short-circuit; cookie / query_parameter / filter_state DEPARTURE-rejected (they need cookie-generation callbacks / query-string parsing / filter-state plumbing — out of envelope).

**Per-side affinity (deterministic) vs cross-side host-identity NON-reproducibility (the documented harness boundary; AMEND-RH8).** Each side's ring is internally byte-exact (every ring input is data envoy-go has), so affinity is DETERMINISTIC: the same hash key → the same ring point → the same backend, ALWAYS (an equality, not a band). BUT cross-side host IDENTITY (does key X hit the "same" backend index on both sides?) does NOT hold — (1) the reference proxy runs Docker-mapped, so Docker NATs every client connection to ONE bridge-gateway source IP (a cross-side source_ip SPREAD is infeasible — N keys on the subject, 1 on the reference), and (2) the two sides build the ring over DIFFERENT endpoint address strings (subject STATIC `127.0.0.1:port`; reference STRICT_DNS container-IP:port) → the ring LAYOUTS differ. Therefore the differential asserts PER-SIDE affinity + spread + cross-side byte-equivalence + cross-side `StatsAsserter` (the 0059/0060 per-side precedent), NOT cross-side host identity. Fixture `0061-lb-ring-hash` (tcp source_ip; 36.1): the driver binds outgoing conns to source IPs `127.0.0.2..5` (16 conns each = 64 total) via `net.Dialer{LocalAddr}`; the SUBJECT-side affinity manifests in the aggregate per-backend counts as a MODULAR INVARIANT — every per-backend count `% 16 == 0` (one source IP → one key → one ring point → one backend, all-16-or-0; D-S36-4), the EXACT affinity leg; spread `>= 2` distinct nonzero backends; conservation `sum == 64`. The reference (Docker-NAT'd to one source IP → all 64 on ONE backend) is asserted on `sum == 64` + cross-side byte-equivalence + cross-side stats only. (The 36.2 `0062-lb-ring-hash-http` keys on a NAT-transparent REQUEST HEADER → a TRUE cross-side affinity+spread differential — both sides assert affinity.)

**Healthy-set boundary (no health checking → all-hosts ring).** Healthy-host filtering happens upstream of the pick in the reference's shared base (priority/healthy/panic); with no health checking, the ring is built over the full static endpoint set (the same Upstream-robustness-family boundary as least_request + random).

**Departures + coverage boundaries:**
- **The 3 mirrored `ring_hash_lb.*` gauges (the FIRST non-zero LB-stat delta; stat surface 1116 → 1119).** RING_HASH is the FIRST LB policy to move the stat surface (least_request + random were both zero-delta). Three new MIRRORED per-cluster gauges `cluster.<name>.ring_hash_lb.{size, min_hashes_per_host, max_hashes_per_host}` (registered + Set once at ring build via `registerClusterMetrics`'s `*ringHashLB` type-assert — ONLY on the RING_HASH path, reference parity; D-S36-6). They are STATIC (immutable ring) and CROSS-SIDE-EXACT — keyed only on `(minimum_ring_size, hash_function, host count, weights)`, NOT on endpoint addresses (1026 / 342 / 342 on BOTH sides) — the strong `0061` `StatsAsserter` cross-equal prong. Live-proven REFUTING the BRAINSTORM's anticipated zero delta (the `/stats` name-set diff RING_HASH-vs-ROUND_ROBIN is exactly these three names, 458 vs 455). See the `## Stat-name mapping` "Phase 36.1 extension" block.
- **`upstream_rq_total` per-side on the TCP path.** On `0061`'s stats prong: cross-equal `ring_hash_lb.{size=1026, min=342, max=342}` + `upstream_cx_total` + `membership_total == 3` + `upstream_cx_active == 0` (quiesced); PER-SIDE `upstream_rq_total` (reference = conn count; subject = 0 — the tcpproxy path never calls `IncUpstreamRqTotal`, the same boundary `0059`/`0060` pin; on the 36.2 HTTP plane the router DOES increment it → cross-equal there).
- **Mismatched `lb_config` oneof member — silent-ignore (PARITY).** A stray `ring_hash_lb_config` under a non-RING_HASH cluster, or a mismatched member (e.g. `least_request_lb_config`) under `RING_HASH`, is silently ignored — reference parity AND behavior-inert (the manager reads `GetRingHashLbConfig()` only on the RING_HASH path).
- **`MURMUR_HASH_2` / cookie / query_parameter / filter_state.** `MURMUR_HASH_2` is implemented (parse + ring build) but unit-level (the fixtures use the `XX_HASH` cross-side-reproducible default). The HTTP `hash_policy` cookie / query_parameter / filter_state sources are DEPARTURE-rejected at 36.2 (out of envelope); a non-source_ip tcp `hash_policy` specifier is DEPARTURE-rejected at 36.1.
- **D-S36-2 shared-RNG-message cosmetic note.** `newRingHash` calls the shared `newPCGRNG()` directly (for the no-hash fallback rng) and ACCEPTS its seed-error message verbatim — `"cluster: least_request: seed rng"`. This path is reachable ONLY on a `crypto/rand` read failure (effectively unreachable on Linux `getrandom`) AND only when a RING_HASH cluster receives a no-hash pick; the `least_request:` prefix under a RING_HASH cluster is a recorded COSMETIC note, NOT a behavior divergence (the random-35 D-S35-2 disposition; a wrapper would force editing `newPCGRNG`).
- **D-S36-4 modular-invariant coverage note.** The subject affinity leg asserts `count[i] % 16 == 0` (the all-16-or-0 invariant from binding exactly 16 conns per source IP). This is necessary-and-overwhelmingly-discriminating against the random-scatter break (a random multinomial(64, 1/3) landing all-multiples-of-16 is < 1%), NOT a tight proof against an adversarial even-split — a documented coverage boundary, since `TCPEcho` carries no backend identifier so per-source-IP→backend attribution is not directly observable.
- **The 4 deliberate-break liveness proofs (`-count=1`, go-test caching defeated).** (i) scatter the key (`Pick` draws random, ignores `hashKey`) → a source IP's 16 conns spread → the subject affinity (`% 16`) leg FAILS; (ii) collapse the ring (all picks → `ring[0]`) → the spread (`>= 2`) leg FAILS (affinity stays intact at 64 % 16 == 0 → spread bites independently, proving it non-vacuous); (iii) corrupt a `StatsAsserter` want (`upstream_cx_total` 64 → 99) → the stats cross-equal prong FAILS; (iv) corrupt the `ring_hash_lb.size` gauge (`rh.size + 1`) → BOTH the cross-side `ref != subj` mismatch AND the `subj != want` value check FAIL. Each: applied → `-count=1` FAIL → `git restore` → diff-clean; never committed broken. Flake check 20/20 (affinity is deterministic; spread `>= 2` over 4 keys / 3 backends is overwhelmingly stable).
- **NO new fuzzer / NO new BackendKind (family expectations).** RING_HASH decodes no untrusted wire bytes (the hash key derives from a source IP / a parsed header value, not a wire frame) → NO new fuzzer (a ring-LOOKUP property test is unit-level — fuzzers STAY 42). `0061` reuses `TCPEcho` → NO new BackendKind (tail STAYS 33). ZERO new packages (`ringhash.go` + `hash.go` in the existing `internal/cluster`) + ZERO new go.mod deps (`xxHash64`/`murmurHash2` hand-rolled — `cespare/xxhash` is absent from go.mod and a new dep for one call site is unwarranted; `go mod tidy -diff` EMPTY).

#### The HTTP route `hash_policy` producer plane (phase 36.2; the SECOND producer — ADR-0237)

*Added by phase 36.2 (the SECOND leg of the CONSUMED 36.1/36.2 by-plane split). The 36.1 leg above lands the seam + the `ringHashLB` + the manager gate + the tcp `source_ip` plane; this 36.2 leg adds the HTTP router's route-level `RouteAction.hash_policy` producer against that ALREADY-LANDED seam. Justified by ADR-0237. A PRODUCER-ONLY leg: NO LB policy / seam / manager / stat-name change — it only STUFFS a ctx-carried hash key before the existing dial.*

**Supported specifiers + the per-request fold (the upstream `HashPolicyImpl::generateHash` mirror).** Per matched route, if `RouteAction.hash_policy[]` (proto field 15) is non-empty, the router folds each supported policy's contribution into a `uint64` ring_hash key and threads it via the LANDED `cluster.WithHashKey(ctx, key)` into `AcquireH1`/`Dial`/`DialH2` → `ringHashLB.Pick`. TWO specifiers are SUPPORTED: **`header`** — `xxHash64` over the matched request-header value (the single-value case, the fixture path); the FULL multi-value case is the seed-chained `XXH64` fold over BYTE-SORTED values (`seed = XXH64(value_i, seed)`, NO separator — NOT a concatenation), via the additive `cluster.HashHeaderValues(values []string) uint64`. The producer shims feed a SINGLE header value (H1 `req.Header.Get`; H2 an hpack-field scan, both lowercased), so the producer plane is single-value; the digest SUPPORTS multi-value and is unit-tested. **`connection_properties.source_ip`** — REUSES the tcp plane's `cluster.HashSourceIP(remoteAddr)` VERBATIM (`xxHash64` of the bare client IP, no port). The multi-policy combine is `hash = rotl64(prev, 1) ^ new` (rotate-left-1 then XOR, policy-list order) with the FIRST contributor taken VERBATIM (`0 ^ new`, NOT rotated — the accumulator starts empty); a `nullopt` policy (absent header / no source IP) is SKIPPED ENTIRELY (no rotate, no XOR); a `terminal=true` policy SHORT-CIRCUITS once the accumulator is non-empty (it checks the ACCUMULATOR, so a terminal policy that itself contributes nothing does NOT short-circuit). A route with no `hash_policy` leaves `ctx` untouched → the LB sees `hasHash==false` → the ring_hash random fallback (byte-stable; every prior fixture unaffected).

**DEPARTURE-rejected specifiers + the empty-`header_name` parity reject.** Parsed + validated at config-build (`hcm/config.go parseRouteHashPolicies`, the tcp_proxy `NewFilter` fail-fast precedent — the proto-read stays in `hcm` so the `router` package stays proto-free; the lowered descriptor `router.HashPolicy` is router-owned). FIVE arms reject: `cookie` / `query_parameter` / `filter_state` (the reference validate-ACCEPTS all three — a RECORDED DEPARTURE, fail-fast: `router: hash_policy specifier %T is not supported (only header, connection_properties.source_ip)`); a configured `regex_rewrite` on a `header` (DEPARTURE — it alters the hashed value); a `source_ip==false` `connection_properties` (DEPARTURE — inert upstream, Envoy adds no hash method). An empty `header_name` PARITY-rejects mirroring the PGV `min_len=1` — `value length must be at least 1 runes` (the go-binding PGV form; envoy-go hand-rolls against the go module). All reject arms land UNIT-LEVEL in `hcm`/`router` config tests (NO cross-side boot-reject dir — the reference accepts, so a cross-side boot-reject is asymmetric; the `0062` fixture is an ACCEPT path).

**NAT-transparent TRUE cross-side affinity (`0062-lb-ring-hash-http`; vs the tcp plane's subject-side-only).** The `X-Hash` request-header key survives Docker's source-IP NAT UNTOUCHED → a SYMMETRIC cross-side proof, the TRUE cross-side affinity differential the tcp `source_ip` plane could NOT be (AMEND-RH8). `0062` routes N=16 distinct `X-Hash` values × K=16 repeats each (256 routed requests) to a 3-endpoint RING_HASH cluster (`ring_hash_lb_config: {}` defaults). The assertions: per-value affinity asserted on BOTH sides via the 36.1 aggregate-count MODULAR INVARIANT (each backend's per-value count is a multiple of K=16, so every per-backend aggregate `% 16 == 0`; a scattered key breaks it); spread `>= 2` distinct backends per side; cross-side byte-equivalence; a cross-side `StatsAsserter`. Cross-side host IDENTITY stays INFEASIBLE (the two sides build the ring over different endpoint address strings) — the pinned property is per-value affinity + spread + byte-equiv + cross-equal stats, NOT host identity. The N=16 (not N=4) workload is a flake-margin choice: with N=4 over 3 backends the values occasionally all land on one backend (spread collapses, `P ≈ 3.7%`/side); N=16 drops the per-side collapse probability to `≈ 7e-8` (past the 5σ-equivalent margin).

**`upstream_rq_total` is CROSS-EQUAL on the HTTP plane (the new prong vs `0061`).** The HTTP router calls `IncUpstreamRqTotal` → BOTH subject and reference increment `cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_total` (= N*K = 256), UNLIKE the tcp plane where the subject stays 0 (the `0059`/`0060`/`0061` boundary). The `0062` `StatsAsserter` reuses the 36.1 cross-equal prongs (the 3 `ring_hash_lb.{size=1026, min=342, max=342}` gauges + `membership_total=3` + quiesced `upstream_cx_active=0`) AND adds the `upstream_rq_total` cross-equal.

**ZERO new stat names — surface STAYS 1119 (the FIRST LB producer reusing the prior plane's stat surface entirely).** The 36.2 HTTP `hash_policy` plane adds NO new stat names — it reuses the 3 `ring_hash_lb.*` gauges (LANDED at 36.1) + the existing `cluster.<name>.*` cx/rq roster. Live-confirmed: the `/stats` name-set subset matching `hash_policy` is EMPTY (`grep -ic hash_policy /stats` = 0). The ONE candidate additive exported `cluster` symbol is `cluster.HashHeaderValues` (the header digest) — additive, no existing-symbol change, the exported `Cluster` surface stays BYTE-STABLE. NO new fuzzer (the HTTP hash key derives from a parsed header value / source IP, not an untrusted wire frame — a key-fold property test is unit-level; fuzzers STAY 42) + NO new BackendKind (`0062` reuses the existing HTTP backends — tail STAYS 33) + ZERO new packages + ZERO new go.mod deps (`RouteAction.HashPolicy` is already on the import graph — `go mod tidy -diff` EMPTY). The conformance gates RE-RAN green (h2spec 53/53 + proxy-wasm 10/10) — NOT zero-touch-by-construction like 36.1 (36.2 DOES touch the H1/H2 router path), but the request/response wire path is byte-identical when no `hash_policy` is configured (every conformance config); the full 64-dir differential is the real guard (the 63 prior dirs byte-exact through the constructor signature change).

### Load balancer — maglev (MAGLEV)

*Introduced by phase 37 (the Load-balancing family's FOURTH row; the project's SECOND consistent-hashing policy). Justified by ADR-0238 (the maglev policy). The seam's FIRST hash-policy REUSE: maglev consumes the ADR-0235 LB hash-key seam + BOTH ADR-0237 producer planes (tcp `source_ip` + HTTP route `hash_policy`) UNCHANGED — swapping the Ketama RING for a fixed-size Maglev lookup table behind the SAME `Pick(hashKey, hasHash)` seam (NO seam ADR, NO producer ADR — the phase-35 single-ADR-on-reuse shape).*

Phase 37 lands the project's FIFTH LB policy (after phase-02 ROUND_ROBIN + phase-34 LEAST_REQUEST + phase-35 RANDOM + phase-36 RING_HASH) and its SECOND consistent-hashing policy. `cluster.Manager` accepts `Cluster.LbPolicy MAGLEV` (`envoy.config.cluster.v3`, enum value 5) on the LEGACY enum path (the same path the other four use; the `Cluster.load_balancing_policy` extension point stays deferred).

**Acceptance + the `MaglevLbConfig` gate (cap + primality — both reference PARITY).** `lb_policy: MAGLEV` with no `maglev_lb_config` (or with `maglev_lb_config: {}` / `table_size` unset) is accepted with the default `table_size 65537` (the manager self-supplies the doc-comment default — the v1.32.4 zero value is nil, NOT generated; 65537 is the Fermat prime 2^16+1). `maglev_lb_config` carries a SINGLE field `table_size` (proto field 1, `UInt64Value`); there is NO `hash_function` field (maglev always uses xxHash64). The HAND-ROLLED gate (the manager calls no PGV — the ring_hash precedent) mirrors the reference's TWO validation layers: (a) the PGV cap — `table_size > 5000011` → `cluster: %q: maglev_lb_config.table_size: value must be less than or equal to 5000011` (the PGV-parity wording); (b) the PRIMALITY gate (checked AFTER the cap, mirroring the reference's PGV-fires-before-app-layer order) — a composite `table_size` (≤ cap, incl 0/1) → `cluster: %q: maglev_lb_config.table_size (%d) must be a prime number` (the house-prefixed form). The primality gate is reference PARITY, NOT an envoy-go-strict departure: the reference itself rejects a non-prime `table_size` with `The table size of maglev must be prime number` (a `--mode validate` matrix confirmed `table_size: 100` → REJECT). The maglev permutation REQUIRES `M` prime for a terminating full-cycle fill (`skip ∈ [1, M-1]` is coprime to a prime `M`, so every per-host permutation is a full `M`-cycle reaching every empty slot). All reject arms land UNIT-LEVEL in `manager_test.go` (NO cross-side boot-reject dir — no fixture pins them; both sides reject identically — a cross-side boot-reject dir is now FEASIBLE but NOT taken, the unit tests are sufficient and lower-cost).

**Maglev lookup-table semantics (the upstream v1.37.2 mirror).** The `maglevLB` (`internal/cluster/maglev.go`) builds an immutable fixed-size `table []int` (each slot an endpoint index) ONCE at construction, mirroring `MaglevTable` EXACTLY: endpoints SORTED by `Addr()` (`"IP:PORT"` = `host->address()->asString()`, port-inclusive) ascending BEFORE the populate loop (the Envoy `std::sort` pre-build — the one structural detail ring_hash did not need; the table layout is sort-order-sensitive); per host `offset = xxHash64(addr) % M` (seed 0) + `skip = (xxHash64Seed(addr,1) % (M-1)) + 1` (seed 1, ∈ `[1, M-1]`); the canonical populate loop fills `table[(offset + skip·next) % M]` host-by-host (in sorted order, one slot per host per iteration under equal weight) until all `M` slots fill (it TERMINATES because `M` prime → each `skip` coprime to `M` → a full `M`-cycle reaches every empty slot). `Pick(hashKey, hasHash)`: `hasHash == true` → `table[hashKey % M]`; `hasHash == false` → a uniform random table index from the injected rng (Envoy's documented no-hash fallback, "effectively the random LB"). For the default 3-equal-host 65537 cluster the per-host slot tallies are 21845 / 21846 (`floor(65537/3)` / `ceil(65537/3)`). The build reuses the existing `xxHash64`/`xxHash64Seed` digests in `hash.go` (ZERO new hash code — the only deviation from ring_hash's per-replica `_<i>`-suffixed key is that maglev hashes the bare `Addr()` with seeds 0 and 1). The table is immutable post-build → `Pick` is read-only / concurrent-safe.

**The seam + producer REUSE (ADR-0235 + ADR-0237 UNCHANGED).** `maglevLB` implements the existing unexported `loadBalancer` interface (`Pick(hashKey uint64, hasHash bool) (Endpoint, func(), error)`) and returns the shared `noopRelease` — exactly as `ringHashLB` does. NO interface change, NO `cluster.go` / pick-funnel / `Dial` / `AcquireH1` change, NO producer-site change. The ADR-0235 PICK-INPUT seam delivers the ctx-carried key to `maglevLB.Pick` IDENTICALLY to `ringHashLB.Pick`; the ADR-0237 HTTP `hash_policy` producer + the tcp `source_ip` producer are policy-AGNOSTIC and UNTOUCHED — they stuff a key into `ctx`; maglev indexes a different structure with it. This is the seam's FIRST hash-policy REUSE (the hash-policy analogue of phase-35 reusing the ADR-0232 release seam) — ZERO seam code/ADR, ZERO producer code/ADR; the single ADR is the policy (ADR-0238). It validates ADR-0235's "the durable asset maglev reuses unchanged" §Consequences claim.

**Healthy-set boundary (no health checking → all-hosts table).** Healthy-host filtering happens upstream of the table lookup in the reference's shared base (priority/healthy/panic); with no health checking, the table is built over the full static endpoint set (the same Upstream-robustness-family boundary as least_request + random + ring_hash).

**Departures + coverage boundaries:**
- **The 2 mirrored `maglev_lb.*` gauges (the SECOND non-zero LB-stat delta; stat surface 1119 → 1121).** MAGLEV is the SECOND LB policy to move the stat surface (after ring_hash; least_request + random were both zero-delta). Two new MIRRORED per-cluster gauges `cluster.<name>.maglev_lb.{min,max}_entries_per_host` (registered + Set once at table build via `registerClusterMetrics`'s `*maglevLB` type-assert — ONLY on the MAGLEV path, reference parity). They are STATIC (immutable table) and CROSS-SIDE-EXACT — `min = floor(M/N)`, `max = ceil(M/N)`, keyed only on `(table_size, host count, weights)`, NOT on endpoint addresses (21845 / 21846 on BOTH sides) — the strong `0063` `StatsAsserter` cross-equal prong (the strong maglev-specific prong). There is NO `size` gauge (the table size is config-known — confirmed absent live). See the `## Stat-name mapping` "Phase 37 extension" block.
- **`upstream_rq_total` cross-equal on the HTTP plane.** On `0063`'s stats prong: cross-equal `maglev_lb.{min=21845, max=21846}` + `upstream_cx_total` (= N·K = 256) + `upstream_rq_total` (= 256, the HTTP router increments it both sides) + `membership_total == 3` + `upstream_cx_active == 0` (quiesced post-drain).
- **Mismatched `lb_config` oneof member — silent-ignore (PARITY).** A stray `lb_config` oneof member under a MAGLEV cluster (e.g. `ring_hash_lb_config` or `least_request_lb_config`) is silently ignored — reference parity (the `--mode validate` matrix accepted `MAGLEV` + a stray `ring_hash_lb_config` SILENTLY, zero warnings) AND behavior-inert (the manager reads `GetMaglevLbConfig()` only on the MAGLEV path).
- **The unused `attempt` retry boundary.** The reference's `attempt > 0` retry-hash mutation (`hash ^= …`) is UNUSED — envoy-go's `Pick` has no `attempt` argument (the single-pick funnel; the ring_hash precedent).
- **The 3 deliberate-break liveness proofs (`-count=1`, go-test caching defeated).** (i) scatter the key (`Pick` draws random, ignores `hashKey`) → an `X-Hash` value's 16 requests spread → the affinity (`≡ 0 mod 16`) leg FAILS; (ii) collapse the BUILT table to host-0 AND corrupt the build gauge tallies (min→0, max→65537) → the spread (`≥ 2`) leg FAILS AND BOTH `maglev_lb.*` gauge cross-equal prongs FAIL — the gauges are the per-host SLOT tally over M slots (figures 65537/0, NOT per-request counts), so the break is deliberately BUILD-level (a weaker Pick-level `table[0]` short-circuit would bite spread ONLY and leave the gauges vacuously green); (iii) corrupt a `StatsAsserter` want (`upstream_cx_total` 256 → 257) → the stats cross-equal prong FAILS. Each: applied → `-count=1` FAIL → `git restore` → diff-clean; never committed broken. Flake check 20/20 (affinity is deterministic; spread `≥ 2` over 16 values / 3 backends collapses with `P ≈ 7e-8`/side).
- **Cross-side host IDENTITY is INFEASIBLE — affinity-provable (the `0062` posture).** The subject/reference tables are built over DIFFERENT endpoint address strings (`"IP:PORT"` differs cross-side), so a given `X-Hash` value may land on a DIFFERENT backend idx per side; the differential asserts the PER-SIDE modular invariant (each per-backend count `≡ 0 mod K`, BOTH sides — the `X-Hash` header is NAT-transparent) + spread (`≥ 2`) + conservation (256) + cross-side `/health` byte-equivalence + a cross-side `StatsAsserter`, NOT host identity. `0063-lb-maglev`: N=16 distinct `X-Hash` values × K=16 repeats (256 routed `GET /get` + 8 `/health`).
- **NO new fuzzer / NO new BackendKind (family expectations).** MAGLEV decodes no untrusted wire bytes (the hash key derives from a parsed header value / source IP, not a wire frame) → NO new fuzzer (a table-build/lookup property test is unit-level, FOLDED into `maglev_test.go` — fuzzers STAY 42). `0063` reuses the `0062` `HTTPEcho` → NO new BackendKind (tail STAYS 33). ZERO new packages (`maglev.go` in the existing `internal/cluster`) + ZERO new go.mod deps (the enum + config are in the pinned `/envoy v1.32.4`; ZERO new hash code — `xxHash64`/`xxHash64Seed` reused; `go mod tidy -diff` EMPTY).

### Load balancer — subset (lb_subset_config)

*Introduced by phase 38.1 (the Load-balancing family's FIFTH construct; the family's FIRST WRAPPER — NOT a `LbPolicy` enum value). Justified by ADR-0239 (the subset-match seam-input extension + the HTTP `RouteAction.metadata_match` producer) + ADR-0240 (the subset LB policy + the `Endpoint.Metadata` dimension). The seam's SECOND pick-input: subset matching widens `Pick(hashKey, hasHash)` → `Pick(hashKey, hasHash, match, hasMatch)`, validating ADR-0235's "future pick-inputs widen `Pick` behind a byte-stable surface" generality.*

Phase 38.1 lands `Cluster.lb_subset_config` (`envoy.config.cluster.v3`, proto field 22) — the project's FIFTH LB construct (after phase-02 ROUND_ROBIN + phase-34 LEAST_REQUEST + phase-35 RANDOM + phase-36 RING_HASH + phase-37 MAGLEV) and the family's FIRST wrapper.

**The wrapper-not-an-enum acceptance (wrap-after-switch, NOT a sixth `case`).** Unlike the five incumbent leaf `LbPolicy` enum values, `lb_subset_config` is an orthogonal `Cluster` field; its presence WRAPS whatever child the `lb_policy` switch produced. `cluster.Manager` builds the leaf LB via the EXTRACTED `buildLeafLB` factory (the `lb_policy` switch lifted to run over an arbitrary endpoint sub-slice), then — when `lb_subset_config` is present — wraps it in a `subsetLB` AFTER the switch (`manager.go buildCluster`). The `Cluster.LbPolicy` supported-list + `TestManager_Error_UnsupportedLBPolicy` are UNTOUCHED — subset is not an enum value, so the phase-34/35/36/37 doubly-hit reject-text-retarget lineage BREAKS (there is no enum value to retire from the rejected set).

**Subset enumeration semantics (the upstream v1.37.2 `SubsetLoadBalancer` mirror).** The `subsetLB` (`internal/cluster/subset.go`) enumerates subsets at construction: per `subset_selectors[].keys` × distinct `envoy.lb` endpoint-metadata value-tuple. Only hosts carrying ALL of a selector's keys participate in that selector's subsets; a host may appear in multiple subsets (it matches every selector whose keys it carries). Each distinct value-tuple under a selector becomes ONE subset; `subsetLB` builds a child `loadBalancer` over that subset's sub-slice via `buildLeafLB`. Scalar values only in the MVP (string / number / bool — list/struct DEPARTURE-rejected on the route side, silently dropped on the endpoint side).

**Value-equality (`ValueUtil::equal` mirror — double-valued numbers, EXACT key-set match).** Numbers are double-valued — int `1` ≡ `1.0` (the reference's `ValueUtil::equal` uses a SINGLE numeric kind, no int/float canonicalization step); bool and string compare by typed direct equality. A route's `metadata_match` resolves to a subset by an EXACT key-set match (the reference's `findSubset` tree walk — NO partial / longest-prefix / superset match): the match's key-set must equal a built subset's selector key-set AND every value must `valueEqual`.

**The 3-way cluster-level fallback.** On a resolution miss, `subsetLB.Pick` applies the cluster-level `fallback_policy`:
- **NO_FALLBACK** → `errNoEndpoints` → the existing 503 `no healthy upstream` / response-flag `UH`. A no-host outcome is NOT a fallback — `lb_subsets_fallback` STAYS 0 on this path (only an ANY_ENDPOINT/DEFAULT_SUBSET fallback host-selection increments it).
- **ANY_ENDPOINT** → a child `loadBalancer` over the FULL endpoint set (spread across all hosts).
- **DEFAULT_SUBSET** → a child over the `default_subset` match; DEGRADES to NO_FALLBACK when the `default_subset` matches zero hosts.

**The per-subset child honours `lb_policy` (all five children).** Because each subset's child is built by `buildLeafLB`, all five children (roundRobin / leastRequest / randomLB / ringHashLB / maglevLB) are exercisable over a subset's sub-slice. A ring_hash / maglev subset child builds its ring / table over JUST that subset's hosts, and the ctx-carried hashKey routes WITHIN the subset (the hashKey passes straight through `subsetLB.Pick` → `child.Pick(hashKey, hasHash, …)`).

**The seam + producer (ADR-0239).** `loadBalancer.Pick` widens to `Pick(hashKey uint64, hasHash bool, match SubsetMatch, hasMatch bool)` — the SECOND pick-input after the ADR-0235 hash key. The five leaf policies absorb `(match, hasMatch)` behaviour-neutrally; only `subsetLB` consumes it. The PRODUCER is the HTTP router's ROUTE-STATIC `RouteAction.metadata_match["envoy.lb"]`, parsed ONCE at config-build (`buildRouterAction` → `parseRouteSubsetMatch` in `hcm/config.go`) into a proto-free `cluster.SubsetMatch` stored on `clusterRouteAction.subsetMatch`. Because the match is ROUTE-STATIC (not request-derived like the `hash_policy` header fold), it is threaded VERBATIM per request via `cluster.WithSubsetMatch` with NO per-request computation — the contrast with ADR-0237's `applyHashKey` fold.

**Healthy-set boundary (no health checking → subsets over the full set).** Healthy-host filtering happens upstream of subset selection in the reference; with no health checking the subsets are computed over the full static endpoint set (the same Upstream-robustness-family boundary as least_request + random + ring_hash + maglev).

**Departures + coverage boundaries:**
- **The 4 mirrored `lb_subsets_*` stats (the FIRST LB stats Inc'd from a `loadBalancer`'s own `Pick`; stat surface 1121 → 1125).** Four per-cluster `cluster.<name>.lb_subsets_*`, subset-only (registered via the `*subsetLB` type-assert in `registerClusterMetrics`): `lb_subsets_active` (gauge) + `lb_subsets_created` (counter) — both Set / Add at build to the distinct-subset count (×1, NOT the reference's 33× artifact); `lb_subsets_selected` (counter, +1 per subset hit from `subsetLB.Pick`) + `lb_subsets_fallback` (counter, +1 per fallback path from `subsetLB.Pick`). The `selected` / `fallback` counters are the FIRST stats a `loadBalancer` increments from its OWN `Pick` path (the maglev/ring_hash gauges are Set at build, not per-pick). See the `## Stat-name mapping` "Phase 38.1 extension" block.
- **The scalar-value-only `metadata_match` MVP boundary.** `parseRouteSubsetMatch` REJECTS a `metadata_match envoy.lb` entry carrying a list / struct value with `router: metadata_match envoy.lb key %q: only scalar values (string, number, bool) are supported` (the `router-metadata-match-nonscalar` arm — unit-level). List / struct values + `list_as_any` are DEFERRED. On the endpoint side `extractEndpoints` silently DROPS non-scalar `envoy.lb` values (a non-scalar endpoint metadata entry simply does not participate in any value-tuple).
- **The `active` / `created` 33×-reference-artifact-vs-×1 magnitude DEPARTURE.** The reference reports `lb_subsets_active` / `lb_subsets_created` with a 33× magnitude artifact; envoy-go pins the semantically-correct ×1 distinct-subset count. This is a RECORDED departure — envoy-go matches the subset SEMANTICS (the distinct-subset count), NOT the reference's 33× figure. Consequently `active` / `created` are NOT cross-side-equal in `0064` (only the request-counted `selected` / `fallback` are asserted cross-side-equal).
- **`CLUSTER_PROVIDED + lb_subset_config` — parity in OUTCOME, ZERO new reject arm.** The reference rejects this combination with `cluster: LB policy CLUSTER_PROVIDED cannot be combined with lb_subset_config`. envoy-go achieves PARITY IN OUTCOME via the pre-existing unsupported-policy gate — CLUSTER_PROVIDED already rejects in `buildLeafLB` (the `default` arm, `unsupported lb_policy …`) BEFORE the wrap is reached. ZERO new reject arm; the message diverges (the policy being unimplemented), the outcome (boot-reject) matches.
- **The NEW `Endpoint.Metadata` dimension.** `Endpoint` grows a `Metadata` field — the parsed `envoy.lb` scalar key→value map captured at `extractEndpoints` — the FIRST per-endpoint dimension beyond `Host:Port`. Locality / weight / priority stay discarded (the locality-weighted / priority candidates' territory). `Addr()` is UNCHANGED, so ring_hash / maglev table keys stay `"IP:PORT"` — a subset child's ring / table is over the same address strings, keyed identically.
- **The TRUE cross-side SET-membership affinity posture (cleaner than maglev/ring_hash).** The `0064-lb-subset` differential is the static-config NAT-transparent TRUE cross-side subset-affinity SET-membership arm: HTTP routes carrying `metadata_match` over `envoy.lb`-tagged endpoints, asserting every served backend ∈ the route's expected subset on BOTH sides + a fallback arm (ANY_ENDPOINT) + cross-side byte-equivalence + the cross-side `selected` / `fallback` stats prong. Because the `metadata_match` is STATIC config (identical on both sides), it is NAT-transparent → the SET-membership property holds TRUE cross-side — strictly CLEANER than maglev/ring_hash's host-identity-infeasible modular-invariant posture (`reference_differential_hash_key_cross_side_infeasible` is INVERTED here — no host-identity obstacle).
- **NO new fuzzer / NO new BackendKind.** Subset decodes no untrusted wire bytes (the metadata derives from validated xDS config) → NO new fuzzer (a subset-resolution property test is unit-level, FOLDED into `subset_test.go` — fuzzers STAY 42). `0064` reuses the `0063` `HTTPEcho` → NO new BackendKind (tail STAYS 33). ZERO new packages (`subset.go` in the existing `internal/cluster`) + ZERO new go.mod deps (the proto fields are in the pinned `/envoy v1.32.4`; `go mod tidy -diff` EMPTY).
- **Deferred surface.** The per-selector fallback machinery (`KEYS_SUBSET` / `fallback_keys_subset`), `single_host_per_subset`, `locality_weight_aware` / `scale_locality_weight`, `panic_mode_any`, `list_as_any`, `metadata_fallback_policy`; the deferred stats `lb_subsets_removed` (no churn) / `fallback_panic` (panic deferred) / `single_host_per_subset_duplicate` (single_host deferred); the `RouteAction.weighted_clusters` + `WeightedCluster.ClusterWeight.metadata_match` producer plane (landed at 38.2 — see `### Route action — weighted clusters` below).

### Load balancer — locality-weighted (locality_weighted_lb_config)

*Introduced by phase 52 (ADR-0269) — the Load-balancing family's SIXTH construct and the family's FIRST to consume per-host health state as a CONTINUOUS weight rather than a binary include/exclude filter. Reuses the phase 38.1 `subsetLB` wrapper-not-an-enum precedent: a construct owning per-group child `loadBalancer`s built by the EXISTING `buildLeafLB` factory, wrapping whatever child the `lb_policy` switch produced. UNLIKE `subsetLB`, this wrapper needs ZERO new `Pick` parameters (D-LW7) — `loadBalancer.Pick(hashKey uint64, hasHash bool, match SubsetMatch, hasMatch bool)` (`loadbalancer.go:16-23`) stays byte-for-byte unchanged; locality selection resolves entirely from per-cluster build-time state plus the EXISTING `clusterHealth` (ADR-0242/0243), consulted via a NEW per-locality aggregation read.*

Phase 52 lands `Cluster.CommonLbConfig.locality_weighted_lb_config` (`envoy.config.cluster.v3`, an EMPTY marker message toggling a distinct weighting MODE) as `internal/cluster/locality.go`'s `localityWeightedLB`.

**The wrap-after-switch acceptance (a SECOND wrap site).** `manager.go`'s `buildCluster` hoists `sc := c.GetLbSubsetConfig()` ONCE (the phase-38.1 hoist, reused as-is), then reads `lwc := c.GetCommonLbConfig().GetLocalityWeightedLbConfig()` and `zac := c.GetCommonLbConfig().GetZoneAwareLbConfig()` — the two arms of the SAME `CommonLbConfig.LocalityConfigSpecifier` oneof (mutually exclusive by construction) — and `switch`es: a combined-config reject, a `zone_aware_lb_config` reject, then the `locality_weighted_lb_config` wrap. Like `subsetLB`, the wrap happens AFTER `buildLeafLB` has already produced the leaf `lb` from the `lb_policy` switch — `localityWeightedLB` REPLACES `cl.lb`, not composes alongside it.

**The `Endpoint.Locality`/`Endpoint.LocalityWeight` dimension (the SECOND per-endpoint dimension after `Metadata`).** `extractEndpoints` captures `LocalityID{Region, Zone, SubZone}` (from `LocalityLbEndpoints.locality`) and the RAW `load_balancing_weight` `uint32` (0 when unset — NO default-to-1 substitution) onto every `Endpoint` it builds. `newLocalityWeightedLBWithRNG` groups endpoints by `Locality` identity in encounter order, building one child `loadBalancer` per distinct locality (via the caller-bound `buildLeafLB` closure — all five leaf policies supported uniformly) plus one `flat` child spanning ALL endpoints (the panic-mode + zero-total-weight fallback).

**The confirmed effective-weight formula.** `effectiveWeight(weight uint32, healthyFraction float64, overprovisioningFactor uint32) float64` computes `configured_weight × min(1, (overprovisioning_factor/100) × healthy_fraction)` — live-probed and CONFIRMED against `contrib-v1.37.2` across a 6-point degradation curve (SPEC §11.3: 100%/80%/60%/40%/20%/0% healthy → 67.00%/66.00%/62.80%/52.80%/36.00%/0.00% observed A-share, matching predicted values within probe noise, with the 40%-healthy point landing an EXACT 52.8% match) plus an OPF-100-vs-140 A/B at an IDENTICAL 60%-healthy state (62.8% at OPF=140 vs 54.0% at OPF=100 — proving `overprovisioning_factor` must be genuinely READ, not hardcoded). Three findings from the live probes:
- **AMEND-LW2 (weight default/mixed-presence, REFUTING the natural "defaults to 1" assumption):** an omitted `load_balancing_weight` is assigned ZERO load when a sibling locality declares an explicit weight (matching the reference's own doc comment, quoted verbatim: *"If no weights are specified when locality weighted load balancing is enabled, the locality is assigned no load."*); when NO locality anywhere declares a weight, the mechanism degrades to a FLAT round-robin across the WHOLE endpoint set. envoy-go reproduces BOTH outcomes from ONE unified rule — `Pick` sums each locality's `effectiveWeight` into `total`; a locality with `eff <= 0` never enters the cumulative-bucket walk, and when `total <= 0` (every raw weight is 0, or every nonzero-weight locality degraded to fully unavailable) `Pick` falls back to the pre-built `flat` child.
- **AMEND-LW3 (the formula itself, per above) — `overprovisioning_factor` default confirmed 140**, applied only when `ClusterLoadAssignment.Policy.overprovisioning_factor` is ABSENT (see D-LW-OPF0 below).
- **AMEND-LW4 (panic-mode interaction, CONFIRMED hypothesis (a)):** cluster-wide panic (the EXISTING `clusterHealth.inPanic` gate, evaluated over `lw.allEndpoints`) FULLY BYPASSES BOTH health-filtering AND locality-weighting — `Pick` delegates straight to the `flat` child and increments the shared `lb_healthy_panic` counter via the EXISTING `panicInc()` convention every leaf policy already uses at its own panic branch, reused here unmodified at `localityWeightedLB`'s own panic branch.

**The two explicit rejects (§6.1, both CONFIRMED live departures — the reference accepts both configurations but behaves confusingly, replicating neither):**
- `cluster: %q: common_lb_config.zone_aware_lb_config is not supported` — `zone_aware_lb_config` is a distinct, unimplemented local-zone-percentage-redirect algorithm; rejected rather than silently falling through, per this project's established sibling-reject discipline for a oneof arm lifted out of a shared silent-ignore set.
- `cluster: %q: lb_subset_config cannot be combined with common_lb_config.locality_weighted_lb_config` — a LIVE boot test against the reference (a cluster with BOTH configs set, weights 3:1, all endpoints tagged to the SAME subset) showed the reference silently OVERRIDES/IGNORES locality weighting once subset load-balancing engages (400 requests split an exact 1:1, not the configured 3:1, while `lb_subsets_selected` stayed live throughout); envoy-go rejects the combination outright rather than replicating that silent override.

**The confirmed-zero stat delta, PLUS the D-LW-HEALTHALLOC side effect.** A full `/stats` scrape of a traffic-served `locality_weighted_lb_config`-active reference cluster found NO dedicated locality-weighted-specific stat — the stat surface gains **ZERO new stats** (the THIRD zero-stat-delta phase in the Load-balancing family, stat surface STAYS **1200**). However, `manager.go`'s `buildCluster` must allocate `clusterHealth` UNCONDITIONALLY when `locality_weighted_lb_config` is present (`if health == nil { health = newClusterHealth(...) }`), even for a cluster configured with ZERO `health_checks` — `localityWeightedLB.Pick` needs `clusterHealth.availableCount`/`inPanic` to be CALLABLE regardless. This is a deliberate departure from the nil-health-fast-path convention every other LB construct follows, and it has a discovered side effect: `registerClusterMetrics`'s PRE-EXISTING, unconditional `if c.health != nil { ... }` block (`manager.go:163-169`) now ALSO registers `membership_healthy`/`lb_healthy_panic` for a locality-weighted cluster with no `health_checks` configured. This WIDENS the CONDITION under which two pre-existing stat NAMES appear — it is NOT a new stat name and NOT a stat-surface COUNT change (every host reports permanently healthy via `newHostHealth`'s `healthy.Store(true)` default, so `membership_healthy` simply equals the endpoint count and `lb_healthy_panic` never increments in that no-health-check configuration).

**The D-LW-OPF0 resolution (absent vs. explicit-zero, honored LITERALLY).** `manager.go` checks `la.GetPolicy().GetOverprovisioningFactor()`'s pointer PRESENCE before calling `.GetValue()` — a free distinction between "absent" (nil `*wrapperspb.UInt32Value`) and "explicit `{value: 0}`" (non-nil, `GetValue()==0`) — and threads `(opf uint32, hasOPF bool)` into `newLocalityWeightedLB`. `hasOPF=false` defaults to 140 inside the constructor; `hasOPF=true, opf=0` is honored LITERALLY: per the confirmed formula, `min(1, 0×frac) == 0` for every locality whenever `frac < 1`, so an explicit `overprovisioning_factor: 0` degrades the entire mechanism to the flat fallback the instant ANY host in ANY locality is unhealthy.

**The child-local-panic coverage boundary (documented, tested, NOT fixed).** A locality's own leaf child (built by `buildLeafLB` over that locality's endpoint sub-slice) evaluates its OWN `clusterHealth.inPanic` over its OWN sub-slice when picking WITHIN that locality — independent of `localityWeightedLB`'s cluster-wide panic gate (AMEND-LW4), which operates over `lw.allEndpoints`. A locality can enter its own child's local panic mode (all of ITS hosts unhealthy) while the cluster as a whole stays well above the panic threshold; the wrapper does not special-case this — the child simply falls back to ITS OWN full sub-slice as any leaf policy already does in isolation. Documented via a dedicated unit test (Task 6); not treated as a defect.

**The differential proof shape.** `0095-lb-locality-weighted` (fixture 97) — a 2-locality × 5-host topology, 2:1 configured weight — proves two arms cross-side: a static-ratio band (~66.7%/33.3% region-A/region-B share at 100% healthy, matching the D-LW3 100%-healthy probe point) and a health-degradation shift band (~52.8%/47.2% region-A/region-B share with region A degraded to 40% healthy, matching the D-LW3 40%-healthy probe point exactly), reusing the phase-39 poll-to-convergence-and-warmup pattern for the degradation arm. Both bands proven LIVE via 2 deliberate breaks (skip-the-wrap; freeze-effective-weight-at-100%-healthy), each observed FAILING under `-count=1` then restored; 20/20 flake-free, `-race` clean.

**No new fuzzer / no new BackendKind / zero new packages.** Locality weighting decodes no untrusted wire bytes (the locality/weight fields derive from validated xDS config) → NO new fuzzer (fuzzers STAY 52). `0095` reuses existing `HTTPEcho`-family backends → NO new `BackendKind` (tail STAYS 38). `locality.go` lives in the EXISTING `internal/cluster` package → ZERO new Go packages, ZERO new go.mod deps.

**Deferred surface.** `zone_aware_lb_config` (rejected, §6.1 above); composing `locality_weighted_lb_config` with `lb_subset_config` (rejected, §6.1 above); `priority`/`proximity`-based locality selection; the EDS-churn fields (dynamic locality membership/weight updates post-boot — this construct's locality membership and weights are captured once at cluster construction); `consistent_hashing_lb_config`/`override_host_status`.

### Route action — weighted clusters (weighted_clusters)

*Introduced by phase 38.2 (the pre-authorized SECOND leg of the phase-38 by-plane split; the 36.1/36.2 precedent). Justified by ADR-0241 (the weighted-cluster routing primitive + the `ClusterWeight.metadata_match` merge composition). The project's FIRST per-request cluster-SELECTION primitive: the SECOND `RouteAction.ClusterSpecifier` arm (after `RouteAction_Cluster`); the FIRST router-layer use of the `randomLB` per-request RNG model OUTSIDE the cluster LB.*

Phase 38.2 lands `RouteAction.weighted_clusters` routing — a NEW per-request weighted-random cluster-SELECTION primitive — plus `WeightedCluster.ClusterWeight.metadata_match`, the per-weighted-cluster subset match that COMPOSES with the 38.1 subset LB (ADR-0239/ADR-0240). Where every prior route resolves a SINGLE `*cluster.Cluster` at config-build (`buildRouterAction` accepted ONLY `RouteAction_Cluster`; `clusterRouteAction` held one cluster), 38.2 adds the SECOND `ClusterSpecifier` arm: a route fans across N weighted clusters, ONE chosen per request by integer weight.

**The SECOND `ClusterSpecifier` arm (a route fans across N weighted clusters, ONE chosen per request by integer weight).** The `RouteAction_WeightedClusters` oneof member → `*WeightedCluster` (`Clusters []*WeightedCluster_ClusterWeight`). Parsed ONCE at config-build by `buildWeightedRouterAction` (the `buildRouterAction` `RouteAction_WeightedClusters` switch arm) into a `weightedClusterRouteAction` (the `clusterRouteAction` sibling): N entries `{cluster *cluster.Cluster, weight uint32, subsetMatch cluster.SubsetMatch}` + the route-level `hashPolicies` (shared across entries) + a per-action `weightedSelector`.

**The selection semantics — weighted-RANDOM (per-request random in `[0, Σweight)` + cumulative walk; `total_weight` deprecated/ignored; explicit `weight: 0` never selected; per-action crypto-seeded PCG RNG — the `randomLB` model).** Each request the selector draws a random value in `[0, Σweight)` and walks the cumulative-weight array to find the chosen entry index. `total_weight` (`WeightedCluster.TotalWeight`, a deprecated `UInt32Value` field) is IGNORED — the client uses the SUM of per-cluster weights (LIVE-confirmed: a non-matching `total_weight` value is accepted-and-ignored; envoy-go matches this outcome). An explicit `weight: 0` on an entry is a valid presence (the `weight` field is a `UInt32Value` PRESENCE-required — total OMISSION rejects; explicit `{value:0}` ACCEPTS) but it can never win the walk while the sum is positive. envoy-go realizes the draw with a `weightedSelector` mirroring `randomLB` (`internal/cluster/random.go`): a per-action mutex-guarded `newPCGRNG()` (`math/rand/v2` PCG seeded from `crypto/rand`, mutex-guarded; boot-fail on the crypto/rand error — the `randomLB` precedent): `idx = walk(cumulativeWeights, uint32(rng() % uint64(Σweight)))`. This is the FIRST use of the per-request RNG model OUTSIDE the cluster LB — a router-layer RNG.

**The `ClusterWeight.metadata_match` merge (merged over route-level `RouteAction.metadata_match`, ENTRY precedence; composes with the 38.1 subset LB via the unchanged ADR-0239 ctx seam; behavior-neutral on a non-subset cluster).** Each `ClusterWeight.metadata_match` (proto field 3 — `*core.Metadata`) MERGES over the route-level `RouteAction.metadata_match` with ENTRY values taking precedence (LIVE-confirmed from the proto semantics). Both are STATIC route config → the merge is ONCE at config-build per entry: `routeScalars ⊕ entryScalars (entry wins on key collision)` → `cluster.NewSubsetMatch(merged)` stored on the entry. Per request, the chosen entry's merged `SubsetMatch` rides the EXISTING ADR-0239 `cluster.WithSubsetMatch` ctx seam UNCHANGED into the chosen cluster's subset selector — NO new seam, NO `loadBalancer.Pick` change, NO per-request fold. On a non-subset cluster the merged match is absorbed behaviour-neutrally (the 38.1 leaf widening ignores the ctx match — the five incumbent leaf policies absorb `(match, hasMatch)` per ADR-0239). On a subset cluster the merged match selects the subset WITHIN the chosen cluster — the full 38.1+38.2 composition. Non-scalar `envoy.lb` values DEPARTURE-reject via the existing `parseRouteSubsetMatch` path (the 38.1 `router-metadata-match-nonscalar` arm, reused per entry + route-level).

**The SIX-arm reject roster (empty-clusters / name-required / cluster_header-unsupported / weight-required / sum-0 / dangling).** envoy-go authors ALL producer rejects (it does NOT run PGV beyond the `clusters min_items:1` already expressed). The rejects (OUTCOME-parity with the reference per ADR-0080; message wording diverges):
- **empty clusters** — `wc.GetClusters()` is empty (the PGV `value must contain at least 1 item(s)` gate is mirrored in OUTCOME).
- **name required** — `ClusterWeight.Name` is empty AND `ClusterHeader` is also empty (covers both the neither-set and the `name: ""` cases; reference: `At least one of name or cluster_header need to be specified`).
- **cluster_header unsupported** — `ClusterWeight.ClusterHeader` is non-empty: REJECTED as unsupported (`cluster_header` is DEFERRED in 38.2; reference: `Only one of name or cluster_header can be specified` when both set; envoy-go rejects `cluster_header` whether or not `name` is also set — a departure-reject).
- **weight required** — `ClusterWeight.Weight` (`*wrapperspb.UInt32Value`) is nil (total omission — a presence check; an explicit `{value:0}` ACCEPTS).
- **sum-0** — the sum of all entry weights equals zero (reference: `Sum of weights in the weighted_cluster must be greater than 0.`).
- **dangling** — a `ClusterWeight.Name` that is not found in the cluster manager (reference: `route: unknown weighted cluster '<name>'`; caught at config-init, NOT deferred to a runtime 404/503).

Reject PRECEDENCE: name/header presence check → weight-required → cluster-exists → sum>0.

**The stat surface is UNCHANGED (1125): weighted selection introduces NO new stat names.** The reference emits NO `*weighted*` stat anywhere (LIVE-confirmed: a `/stats` scrape of a 70/30 weighted-route bootstrap found zero `*weighted*` hits; `grep -i weight` matched ONLY `cluster.<name>.max_host_weight` — an ENDPOINT host-weight gauge present on EVERY cluster, value 1, UNRELATED to the route weight; NOT reflecting the 70/30 config). The per-request cluster selection is observable purely through the PRE-EXISTING per-cluster `upstream_rq_total` counters (which envoy-go already emits per phase 06.1); the split across clusters tracks the configured weights. **38.2 adds ZERO new stat names; surface STAYS 1125.** The `max_host_weight` gauge is NOT mirrored (it is an endpoint host-weight gauge present on every cluster regardless of routing policy — not route-weight-related; unasserted).

**The deferred surface (cluster_header / header-mutation / typed_per_filter_config / host_rewrite / runtime_key_prefix / random_value_specifier.header_name / tcp_proxy plane).**
- `ClusterWeight.cluster_header` (header-named cluster; field 12) — DEFERRED; a `cluster_header`-bearing entry REJECTS as unsupported.
- `ClusterWeight.request_headers_to_add` / `request_headers_to_remove` / `response_headers_to_add` / `response_headers_to_remove` — per-weighted header mutation; DEFERRED; silently IGNORED (accepted-but-inert, orthogonal to the selection primitive).
- `ClusterWeight.typed_per_filter_config` — per-weighted-cluster filter config override; DEFERRED; silently IGNORED.
- `ClusterWeight.host_rewrite_specifier` (`host_rewrite_literal`) — per-weighted host rewrite; DEFERRED; silently IGNORED.
- `WeightedCluster.runtime_key_prefix` — runtime-overridable per-cluster weights (the RTDS/runtime layer); DEFERRED.
- `WeightedCluster.random_value_specifier` (`header_name`) — header-seeded selection RNG (deterministic-by-header selection); DEFERRED; the MVP uses the per-action PCG RNG (per-request random, the `randomLB` model).
- The `TcpProxy.weighted_clusters` plane — weighted clusters on the L4 tcp_proxy; DEFERRED entirely (the HTTP-router plane is the 38.2 leg).

**Departures + coverage boundaries:**
- **The `cluster_header`-unsupported departure-reject.** `ClusterWeight.cluster_header` is ACCEPTED by the reference; envoy-go REJECTS it as unsupported (38.2 does not implement the header-named cluster path). This is a DEPARTURE-reject (the reference accepts; envoy-go over-rejects vs the reference but within the ADR-0080 OUTCOME-parity framing — the outcome on a `cluster_header` route is a boot-reject rather than runtime behavior). Recorded here; to be lifted when `cluster_header` is implemented.
- **Header-mutation / `typed_per_filter_config` / `host_rewrite` silent-ignore.** The reference ACCEPTS entries carrying `request/response_headers_to_*` / `typed_per_filter_config` / `host_rewrite` and applies them; envoy-go ACCEPTS but IGNORES them silently (the accepted-but-inert posture — orthogonal to the selection primitive; no mutation is applied). A narrow coverage boundary: the selection + routing behavior is unaffected; the suppressed mutation is a known gap, to be lifted when per-weighted mutation is implemented.
- **`total_weight` ignored.** `WeightedCluster.TotalWeight` is DEPRECATED upstream; the client uses the SUM of cluster weights. envoy-go IGNORES it unconditionally (no cross-check against the sum, no reject on mismatch). OUTCOME-parity with the reference (the reference deprecation-warns but also ignores it for routing math).
- **The scalar-only `metadata_match` boundary (reusing the 38.1 reject).** `parseRouteSubsetMatch` (reused per entry + route-level) REJECTS a non-scalar `envoy.lb` value (list/struct) with the `router-metadata-match-nonscalar` arm. ZERO new reject arm — the 38.1 boundary extends naturally to the per-entry merge.
- **The per-side-distribution-band differential posture.** The `0065-weighted-clusters` fixture asserts a PER-SIDE distribution band (each cluster's `upstream_rq_total` within ~4–5σ of `N · weight/Σweight`) NOT cross-side per-request equality — because the independent per-request RNG makes cross-side per-request identity infeasible for a randomized policy (the `0060-lb-random` lineage; `reference_differential_band_sigma_margin` discipline). Cross-side per-request identity is infeasible and is NOT asserted.
- **ZERO new stat names.** The FIRST LB-family leg to add NO stat surface (38.2 contributes nothing to the stat surface; 38.1 added the 4 `lb_subsets_*` stats). Observable only through the pre-existing per-cluster `upstream_rq_*`. See the `## Stat-name mapping` Phase 38.2 note.
- **NO new fuzzer.** Weighted-cluster selection decodes no untrusted wire bytes (the weights + cluster names derive from validated xDS config); a selection-distribution property test is unit-level, FOLDED into `router_weighted_test.go` — fuzzers STAY 42.
- **NO new BackendKind.** `0065` reuses the `0063`/`0064` `HTTPEcho` — tail STAYS 33.
- **The FIRST per-request cluster-selection primitive + the FIRST router-layer per-request RNG.** Every prior route resolved a SINGLE cluster at config-build; 38.2 is the FIRST per-request choice among clusters (a new SELECT-then-DISPATCH model). The `weightedSelector`'s `newPCGRNG()` is the FIRST use of the per-request RNG model OUTSIDE the cluster LB.

### Cluster — active health checks

*Introduced by phase 39.1 (active HTTP health checking; the keystone leg of the phase-39 by-checker split — 39.1 = the state+runtime+HTTP-checker, 39.2 = the TCP + gRPC checkers reusing the 39.1 substrate). Extended by phase 39.2 (TCP + gRPC checker codecs; the pre-authorized second leg; the active-HC checker roster HTTP+TCP+gRPC is NOW COMPLETE). Justified by ADR-0242 (the host health-state dimension + the cluster-level checker runtime) + ADR-0243 (the health-aware LB pick — Approach A, the build-time-injected health view + panic threshold) + ADR-0244 (the multi-codec prober dispatch; this phase). The project's FIRST per-host MUTABLE state + the FIRST cluster-level BACKGROUND runtime.*

Phase 39.1 lands `Cluster.health_checks` (`envoy.config.cluster.v3`, proto field 8) — active HTTP health checking. Where `Endpoint` was the project's only per-host construct (immutable; `cluster.go:33`) and `internal/cluster` had no background runtime, 39.1 adds BOTH a mutable per-host health dimension and a timer-driven cluster subsystem, then makes the six LB constructs route only to healthy hosts.

**The host health-state model (start-healthy, first-check-immediate, threshold-gated).** A per-cluster `clusterHealth` registry holds a `map[string]*hostHealth` keyed by `Endpoint.Addr()`; each `hostHealth` carries an atomic `healthy` bit + `consecutiveFailures`/`consecutiveSuccesses` counters. `Endpoint` stays an immutable value type — health is CLUSTER state, NOT a field on the picked endpoint copy; the registry is seeded at `extractEndpoints` (one `hostHealth` per endpoint). **Hosts START healthy.** The FIRST check applies its result IMMEDIATELY (no threshold gating on the first observation — healthy on first success, unhealthy on first failure); thereafter the thresholds gate transitions: `consecutiveFailures == unhealthy_threshold` flips healthy → unhealthy (resets the success counter), `consecutiveSuccesses == healthy_threshold` flips unhealthy → healthy (resets the failure counter).

**The HTTP checker (GET path; expected_statuses default 200; interval/timeout; the project's FIRST cluster-level background runtime).** Per cluster × per configured `health_check`, a background goroutine (`healthChecker` in `internal/cluster/health.go`): a ticker at `interval` (after the ~immediate first check); each tick probes every host with a `timeout`-bounded context, classifies the result (success / failure / network_failure), applies the transition, and Inc's the stats. The HTTP probe sends `GET <path>` over a fresh dial (the configured `host` header; default H1), succeeding iff the response status ∈ `expected_statuses` (default `[200,200]`); a connection failure is a `network_failure` (a sub-class of `failure`). The lifecycle: `Manager.StartHealthChecks(ctx)` is called from `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` AFTER `Freeze` (so the host set + stats are immutable/allocated) — every existing unit/differential test that does NOT call it gets NO checkers (zero behavior change); `Manager.Drain()` cancels the root context and WaitGroup-waits for the goroutines to exit (no goroutine leak).

**The TCP checker — connect-only (phase 39.2; ADR-0244).** `tcp_health_check{}` (empty = connect-only; the MVP liveness signal) uses a `net.Dialer{Timeout}.Dial("tcp", addr)` then immediate close. A successful TCP connect ⇒ `(ok=true)` — the `health_check.success` counter increments and the transition model records a healthy result. A refused or timed-out connect ⇒ `(failure, network_failure)` — BOTH `health_check.failure` AND `health_check.network_failure` increment, matching the HTTP checker's dial-failure classification (L4 unreachability is a `network_failure` in both codecs). The result flows through the UNCHANGED `applyResult`/`recordResult` transition model. **`send`/`receive` payload matching is NOT supported** — a `tcp_health_check` that sets `send` or `receive` is DEPARTURE-rejected at config-build: `cluster: %q: health_check: tcp_health_check send/receive payload matching is not supported` (the connect-only MVP boundary; payload send/receive is deferred). `proxy_protocol_config` is also deferred (silently ignored).

**The gRPC checker — `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check` over H2 (phase 39.2; ADR-0244).** `grpc_health_check` issues a unary `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check` RPC over HTTP/2 (insecure h2c; a fresh `grpc.ClientConn` per probe). Classification (the application-vs-network `network_failure` discriminator): a transport/RPC error (`err != nil` — e.g. `codes.Unavailable` on a refused/dead port) ⇒ BOTH `health_check.failure` AND `health_check.network_failure` increment; a completed `Check` with `resp.Status == SERVING` ⇒ `health_check.success` increments (healthy); a completed `Check` with `resp.Status != SERVING` (NOT_SERVING / SERVICE_UNKNOWN / UNKNOWN) ⇒ only `health_check.failure` increments (`network_failure` stays 0 — the backend is reachable but reports unhealthy: an APPLICATION failure, not a network failure). `service_name` (proto field 1) IS SUPPORTED: empty = the overall `""` service; a non-empty `service_name` is sent as `HealthCheckRequest.Service`. `authority` (field 2) and `initial_metadata` (field 3) are DEFERRED — both are silently ignored (no reject). **The cluster MUST declare HTTP/2 support**: a `grpc_health_check` on a cluster WITHOUT HTTP/2 is rejected at config-build: `cluster: %q: grpc_health_check requires the cluster to support HTTP/2` (a config-init reject, NOT PGV — it fires under `--mode validate` as a plain error string).

**The health-aware pick + the panic threshold (default 50%, strict `<`; build-time-injected — NOT a `Pick`-signature widening).** Each of the six LB constructs (`roundRobin`/`randomLB`/`leastRequest`/`ringHashLB`/`maglevLB`; `subsetLB` inherits via its children) carries a build-time-injected `*clusterHealth` view consulted at `Pick`. A construct picks a candidate by its normal rule; if unhealthy it advances (round_robin: next index; least_request: choose the least-loaded HEALTHY host; random: re-draw; ring_hash/maglev: WALK FORWARD on the ring/table to the next healthy host — preserving the key→host stability that defines those policies). When the healthy FRACTION is strictly `< healthy_panic_threshold` (`Cluster.common_lb_config.healthy_panic_threshold`, default 50%) the construct enters PANIC mode: it routes to ALL hosts (better to spread load over a possibly-degraded set than to overload the few healthy ones) and increments `lb_healthy_panic`. The comparison is STRICT `<` (exactly-50% healthy does NOT panic). The health view is build-time-injected — NOT a per-request value — because host health is CLUSTER state: the `loadBalancer.Pick(hashKey, hasHash, match, hasMatch)` signature + the exported `Cluster` surface stay BYTE-STABLE. This is the deliberate CONTRAST with the ADR-0235 hash-key + ADR-0239 subset-match per-request ctx-carry pick-inputs (those WIDENED the pick path; health does NOT). **Behavior-neutral when `health == nil`** (a cluster with no `health_checks`) → the skip loop never fires, panic never triggers; every existing fixture + h2spec 53/53 + proxy-wasm 10/10 stays byte-identical.

**The parse-reject roster (envoy-go's own, no PGV — the 38.2 precedent; byte-stable; all config-build/boot rejects; unit-level).** OUTCOME-parity with the reference per ADR-0080; the IMPL pins exact byte-stable strings. The 39.1 `only http_health_check is supported` DEPARTURE-reject is LIFTED at 39.2 — `tcp_health_check` and `grpc_health_check` are now ACCEPTED:
- **health_checker oneof missing** (reference: `field: "health_checker", reason: is required`).
- **HTTP empty `path`** (reference: `HttpHealthCheckValidationError.Path: value length must be at least 1 characters`).
- **`interval` missing** (reference: `HealthCheckValidationError.Interval: value is required`).
- **`timeout` missing** (reference: `HealthCheckValidationError.Timeout: value is required`).
- **`unhealthy_threshold` (and `healthy_threshold`) missing** (reference: `HealthCheckValidationError.UnhealthyThreshold: value is required`).
- **`tcp_health_check` with `send`/`receive` set** (phase 39.2 DEPARTURE-reject — the deferred-feature boundary): `cluster: %q: health_check: tcp_health_check send/receive payload matching is not supported`.
- **`grpc_health_check` on a non-H2 cluster** (phase 39.2 config-init reject): `cluster: %q: grpc_health_check requires the cluster to support HTTP/2`.

**Departures + coverage boundaries:**
- **The +7 stats (emitted ONLY on clusters with `health_checks`; surface 1125 → 1132; 39.2 adds ZERO new stats — surface STAYS 1132).** Four `cluster.<name>.health_check.{attempt,success,failure,network_failure}` (counters, Inc'd per probe per the ADR-0242 runtime) + `health_check.healthy` (gauge — count of healthy hosts per checker) + `membership_healthy` (gauge) + `lb_healthy_panic` (counter — Inc'd by the ADR-0243 health-aware pick when the healthy fraction is strictly `< healthy_panic_threshold`). Existing fixtures (no `health_checks`) are unaffected. The `0066`/`0067`/`0068` `StatsAsserter` cross-equals the deterministically-converging subset (`membership_healthy`, `health_check.attempt`/`success`/`failure`). The stat set is CODEC-AGNOSTIC — the TCP and gRPC checkers (phase 39.2) add ZERO new stat names; the same seven-name set is emitted regardless of checker codec; stat surface 1132 → 1132 (AMEND-TG4). See the `## Stat-name mapping` Phase 39.1 block.
- **The 39.1 tcp/grpc-checker DEPARTURE-reject is LIFTED at 39.2 (ADR-0244).** In 39.1 a `tcp_health_check` / `grpc_health_check` checker was DEPARTURE-rejected with `only http_health_check is supported`. That reject is LIFTED at 39.2 — both checkers now ACCEPTED (tcp: connect-only; grpc: `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check` over H2). The remaining rejects for these codecs are the 39.2-specific ones listed in the reject roster above.
- **D-S39.2-3 recorded departure (gRPC `err != nil` MVP — every transport error maps to `network_failure`).** The `grpcProber` MVP classifies ALL `err != nil` results as `networkFailure=true`. A codes-based refinement (transport/`codes.Unavailable` ⇒ `network_failure`; a returned gRPC status e.g. `codes.Unimplemented` ⇒ application failure, `networkFailure=false`) is deferred. The `0068` fixture exercises only connect-refused + SERVING; the `codes.Unimplemented` edge is not exercised. Recorded here per ADR-0244 §Consequences.
- **The build-time-injected health view (NOT a `Pick`-signature widening) — the deliberate CONTRAST with ADR-0235/0239.** Host health is injected at BUILD because it is cluster state, NOT a per-request ctx value; the `Pick` signature + the exported `Cluster` surface stay byte-stable. This deliberately CONTRASTS with the ADR-0235 hash-key + ADR-0239 subset-match per-request pick-inputs (which widened `Pick`). The axes compose: a ring_hash/maglev pick resolves the hash key then the walk-to-next-healthy filters the result; a subset child applies the subset match then its injected view filters within the subset.
- **The first per-host mutable state + the first cluster-level background runtime.** `Endpoint` stays immutable (health lives off-`Endpoint` on the `clusterHealth` registry). The `Start.../Drain` runtime lifecycle (post-`Freeze` start; context-cancel + WaitGroup-wait drain) is the TEMPLATE for future timer-driven cluster subsystems.
- **The poll-to-convergence differential posture.** The `0066-health-check-http` / `0067-health-check-tcp` / `0068-health-check-grpc` fixtures (cross-side) each use a poll-to-converge + warmup determinism shape (poll `/stats` on both sides until `membership_healthy == 2` and `health_check.failure ≥ 1`; then a load phase asserting 100% of traffic lands on LIVE backends, the dead host filtered) over endpoints = {2 LIVE backends, 1 DEAD unbound endpoint} (66% healthy > 50% → asserts FILTERING, not panic). 20/20 flake-free each.
- **NO new fuzzer.** The health checker decodes no untrusted wire bytes — the probe targets are validated xDS config; the HTTP + TCP probes classify status/connect results; the gRPC probe decodes via the `grpc_health_v1` library (not hand-rolled). Fuzzers STAY 42. ZERO new packages (`health.go` in the existing `internal/cluster`) + ZERO new go.mod deps (`HealthCheck` in the pinned `/envoy v1.32.4`; `grpc_health_v1` a subpackage of the already-direct `google.golang.org/grpc v1.70.0`).
- **+1 BackendKind at 39.2 (GRPCHealthResponder = 34).** `0068-health-check-grpc` introduces the `GRPCHealthResponder` backend — an h2c server that answers `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check` ⇒ SERVING AND returns 200 to plain-H2 data-plane requests. BackendKind tail 33 → 34. (`0067-health-check-tcp` reuses the existing `HTTPEcho` backend — a TCP connect to its port succeeds; tail STAYS 33 at `0067`.)
- **Deferred surface (recorded departures).** TCP `send`/`receive` payload matching + `proxy_protocol_config`; gRPC `authority` + `initial_metadata` (both silently ignored) + the codes-based `network_failure` refinement (D-S39.2-3); degraded / draining states (`HealthStatus` DEGRADED/DRAINING — MVP HEALTHY/UNHEALTHY only); jitter / interval variants (`no_traffic_interval`, the jitter fields); EDS `health_status`; health-check event logging; the deferred stats (`health_check.{passive_failure,verify_cluster,degraded}`, `membership_{change,degraded,excluded}`, `update_no_rebuild`). Outlier (passive) detection — a future Upstream-robustness row — will feed the SAME `clusterHealth` registry as a passive input. The 3 health-gated Load-balancing-family candidates (locality-weighted LB, priority load balancing, panic thresholds) are UNBLOCKED — the health dimension they depend on exists.

### Cluster — passive health (outlier detection)

*Introduced by phase 40.1 (`consecutive_5xx` keystone — the first leg of the pre-authorized phase-40 by-detector-class split). Justified by ADR-0245 (the `RecordUpstreamResult` seam + the per-host ejection dimension + the `available` LB-pick predicate + the `consecutive_5xx` detector). Builds over the SAME `clusterHealth`/`hostHealth` registry (ADR-0242) + the SAME build-time-injected health-aware LB pick (ADR-0243) established at phase 39. The project's FIRST passive upstream-health construct + the FIRST per-request router→cluster health callback.*

Phase 40.1 lands `Cluster.outlier_detection` (`envoy.config.cluster.v3`, proto field 19) — passive ejection of hosts that return consecutive 5xx responses on real traffic. Where active health checking (phase 39) uses out-of-band probes to drive the `healthy` bit, outlier detection is driven by in-band request outcomes. The two dimensions compose independently: a host is available to the LB only if BOTH `isHealthy` AND NOT `isEjected`.

**The `RecordUpstreamResult` seam (the per-request router→cluster health callback).** `Cluster.RecordUpstreamResult(ep Endpoint, r UpstreamResult)` is called on EVERY upstream response from the TWO LIVE router success sites — `doH1ClusterAction` (`router.go`) and `doH2ClusterAction` (`router_h2.go`), beside the existing `IncStatusClass` call — where `picked` is non-zero and the upstream status code is known. The legacy test-only `(*routerAction).do` / `(*routerActionH2).doH2` drivers are NOT called. Weighted-cluster routes reuse the same `do*ClusterAction` → covered for free. `RecordUpstreamResult` is a **no-op when `c.outlier == nil`** — the hot path for clusters without `outlier_detection` is a single nil check (byte-identical to pre-40.1). `UpstreamResult.LocalOriginErr` (a connect/reset pre-pick failure) is tracked but UNREAD at 40.1 — reserved for the 40.2 local-origin detector.

**The `consecutive_5xx` detector — eject on N consecutive 5xx; reset only by a 2xx from that host.** On each `RecordUpstreamResult` when `c.outlier != nil`: (a) if 5xx (`StatusCode >= 500 && StatusCode < 600`): `consec5xx++`; if `consec5xx >= consecutive_5xx` → a candidate ejection fires (see §cap + §enforce below); (b) if non-5xx (2xx/3xx/4xx): `consec5xx = 0` (reset; ONLY a response FROM THIS HOST resets it — responses from other hosts have no effect). `consecutive_5xx == 0` (or absent when `outlier_detection` is set without the field; the proto default is 5 when the block is present) disables the detector. The per-host counter accumulates across all downstream connections — there is no per-connection isolation.

**The `max_ejection_percent` cap + `ejections_overflow`.** A candidate ejection fires the cap check: `(currentlyEjected + 1) × 100 / totalHosts <= max_ejection_percent` (default 10%). If the cap PERMITS: the host is ejected, the five `ejections_*` stats update (see §stats below). If the cap BLOCKS: `ejections_overflow` increments and the host STAYS in rotation (the counter-reset/threshold side of the detector continues, but no actual ejection occurs). Boundary pinned LIVE: for 1-of-3 hosts (33.33%) a cap of ≥ 34 ejects; cap 33 → overflow. `max_ejection_percent > 100` is PARSE-REJECTED.

**The `enforcing_consecutive_5xx` roll.** Default 100 (always enforce). A value of 0 detects but never enforces (detect-only: `ejections_detected_consecutive_5xx` increments but the cap check and eject are skipped). Intermediate values are a percentage roll. `enforcing_consecutive_5xx > 100` is PARSE-REJECTED.

**The lazy time-based un-eject (recorded departure from the reference sweep).** `clusterHealth.isEjected(ep)` checks the ejected state lazily: if `ejected` is set and `now >= unejectAtNanos`, it atomically clears `ejected`, decrements `ejections_active`, and returns false (un-eject); else returns `ejected.Load()`. Because `isEjected` is called on the pick path for every candidate the LB scans (via `available`), an ejected host automatically rejoins on the next LB scan past it once its `base_ejection_time` elapses — even with NO further traffic to that host (an ejected host gets no requests, so the pick-path check is the load-bearing un-eject path). The ejection duration is `now + base_ejection_time` (flat; NO backoff — AMEND-OD2). **Recorded departure:** the reference un-ejects via a periodic `interval` sweep (measured un-eject ≈ `base_ejection_time + ≤1×interval`); envoy-go uses a lazy, observation-driven un-eject — goroutine-free at 40.1 (the first new outlier goroutine is the 40.3 statistical sweep). `interval` is PARSE-ACCEPTED + validated (`> 0s`) but its sweep-cadence role is DEFERRED. `base_ejection_time` set and `<= 0s` is PARSE-REJECTED.

**The `available = isHealthy && !isEjected` LB predicate (the byte-stable extension).** The five leaf LB consult sites (`loadbalancer.go` round_robin, `random.go`, `ringhash.go`, `maglev.go`, `leastrequest.go`) move their per-pick filter from `isHealthy → available`; `subsetLB` inherits the move via its children. The **panic-fraction denominator** moves from `healthyCount` to `availableCount` (so an all-ejected cluster panics → routes to all, matching the reference); the **`membership_healthy` gauge STAYS `healthyCount`** (active-HC-only — outlier ejection is NOT reflected in `membership_healthy`, matching the reference). When no `outlier_detection` is configured `isEjected` is always false ⇒ `available == isHealthy`, `availableCount == healthyCount`, the panic denominator is unchanged — **byte-identical to pre-40.1** (every pre-40.1 fixture stays green).

**The stats — emitted ONLY on clusters with `outlier_detection`; surface 1132 → 1137 (40.1, +5) → 1141 (40.2, +4) → 1149 (40.3, +8).** Scoped `cluster.<name>.outlier_detection.`. The 40.1 set (+5):
- `ejections_active` — **gauge** (current ejected host count; 0→1 on eject, →0 on un-eject; cross-detector).
- `ejections_enforced_total` — counter (total enforced ejections across all detectors; cross-detector).
- `ejections_overflow` — counter (cap-blocked ejections — the host stays in rotation; these do NOT increment `ejections_enforced_total`; cross-detector).
- `ejections_detected_consecutive_5xx` — counter (threshold crossings, regardless of cap/enforcement).
- `ejections_enforced_consecutive_5xx` — counter (actual 5xx-triggered ejections).

The 40.2 set (+4 — the gateway + local-origin detector pairs; registered unconditionally on any outlier cluster, matching the reference):
- `ejections_detected_consecutive_gateway_failure` — counter (gateway threshold crossings; increments on gateway-class 5xx `{502,503,504}` even when detect-only, i.e. `enforcing_consecutive_gateway_failure == 0`).
- `ejections_enforced_consecutive_gateway_failure` — counter (actual gateway-triggered ejections).
- `ejections_detected_consecutive_local_origin_failure` — counter (local-origin threshold crossings; split=true only).
- `ejections_enforced_consecutive_local_origin_failure` — counter (actual local-origin-triggered ejections; split=true only).

The 40.3 set (+8 — the statistical detector pairs; 4 external DRIVEN + 4 local-origin name-present-logic-deferred emitting 0; registered unconditionally on any outlier cluster):
- `ejections_detected_success_rate` — counter (success_rate threshold crossings).
- `ejections_enforced_success_rate` — counter (actual success_rate ejections).
- `ejections_detected_failure_percentage` — counter (failure_percentage threshold crossings; increments even when detect-only at `enforcing_failure_percentage == 0`).
- `ejections_enforced_failure_percentage` — counter (actual failure_percentage ejections).
- `ejections_detected_local_origin_success_rate` — counter (LOGIC DEFERRED — emits 0; name registered for surface parity).
- `ejections_enforced_local_origin_success_rate` — counter (LOGIC DEFERRED — emits 0).
- `ejections_detected_local_origin_failure_percentage` — counter (LOGIC DEFERRED — emits 0).
- `ejections_enforced_local_origin_failure_percentage` — counter (LOGIC DEFERRED — emits 0).

The **double-count** is REPLICATED for EVERY detector: a single ejection increments BOTH `ejections_enforced_total` AND the per-detector `ejections_enforced_consecutive_{5xx,gateway_failure,local_origin_failure}` counter (40.1/40.2) OR `ejections_enforced_{success_rate,failure_percentage}` counter (40.3, the statistical detectors below). Existing fixtures (no `outlier_detection`) are unaffected. The `0069-outlier-detection-consecutive-5xx` `StatsAsserter` (40.1) cross-equals `{ejections_active, ejections_enforced_total, ejections_enforced_consecutive_5xx, ejections_detected_consecutive_5xx}` and at 40.2 is WIDENED to ALSO cross-assert `ejections_detected_consecutive_gateway_failure` (the reference always trips it on a 503, and envoy-go now does too — AMEND-OD2-1; this was a 40.1 departure, AMEND-OD4, now LIFTED).

*Extended by phase 40.2 (the other consecutive detectors — `consecutive_gateway_failure` + `consecutive_local_origin_failure` + `split_external_local_origin_errors`). Justified by ADR-0246. Builds over the SAME 40.1 substrate (ADR-0245): the `RecordUpstreamResult` seam, the ejection dimension on `hostHealth`, the `available` LB-pick predicate, the `max_ejection_percent` cap, and the lazy un-eject are REUSED UNCHANGED — 40.2 adds the two detectors, the split accounting, and the live `LocalOriginErr` population.*

**The `consecutive_gateway_failure` detector — gateway-class 5xx `{502,503,504}`; active-by-default, detect-only by default.** Whenever `outlier_detection` is present the gateway detector is active (the proto default `consecutive_gateway_failure: 5`), but `enforcing_consecutive_gateway_failure` defaults to **0** ⇒ DETECT-ONLY by default: a gateway-class 5xx increments `consecGw` and (at the threshold) `ejections_detected_consecutive_gateway_failure`, but the host is NOT ejected unless `enforcing_consecutive_gateway_failure > 0`. A non-gateway 5xx (`{500,501,505..599}`) RESETS `consecGw` (it breaks the gateway streak) but still advances the 5xx detector. `consecutive_gateway_failure == 0` disables the gateway detector. `enforcing_consecutive_gateway_failure > 100` is PARSE-REJECTED.

**Gateway-checked-FIRST + the once-ejected short-circuit (AMEND-OD2-2).** On an external gateway-class 5xx the gateway detector is evaluated BEFORE the 5xx detector. If the gateway detector EJECTS the host on this call, control short-circuits and the 5xx detector does NOT run this call — so `consec5xx` never reaches its threshold and `ejections_detected_consecutive_5xx` stays 0 (the live `detected_consecutive_5xx: 0`-on-gateway-eject pin: this is the gateway-`enforcing: 100` case). If the gateway detector does NOT eject (the common DEFAULT-config case where `enforcing_consecutive_gateway_failure == 0`/detect-only), control FALLS THROUGH and `consec5xx++` runs — so on the default config BOTH consecutive counters advance on every gateway-class 5xx and the 5xx detector (at `enforcing` 100) is the one that ejects. Only an actual EJECTION clears the streaks (the eject clears the host's consecutive counters + removes it from rotation, the 40.1 lifecycle); a mere detection does not.
