- **The four active features are PARSE-ACCEPTED-behavior-DEFERRED.** `force_response_rewrite` / `id_based_broker_address_rewrite_spec` / `api_keys_allowed` / `api_keys_denied` are parsed but inert; the broker-address-rewrite WRITE-MUTATION is a future framework-surgery sub-phase (it would mutate the write buffer — a capability never built).
- **The "leftover-body-bytes → unknown" sub-case is UNMIRRORED.** A request whose header parses but whose body has trailing bytes upstream routes to `unknown`; the header-only sniffer does not body-decode, so it cannot detect this (the one true body-decode coverage boundary; D31-4).
- **The deprecated-low-version → unknown sub-case is UNMIRRORED (D-PLAN-1).** `minVersion` is treated as 0; an `api_version` below a key's real minVersion is counted as the key (not `unknown`). The `0053` unknown-version arm tests the HIGH side (`0x7FFF`) only.
- **The eager-vs-per-connection boot-window difference.** envoy-go creates the 176-counter roster EAGERLY at config-load (exist-at-zero from boot); upstream creates per-connection. UNOBSERVABLE to the differential (every `0053` assertion runs post-first-connection) — a recorded boundary, not a silent gap (the mongo D-P1 precedent).
- **The per-exception-reset decode posture (D-PLAN-2).** A decode exception resets the offending direction's buffer (resync) + Continue — NOT lifetime sniffing-off (the mongo posture); matches upstream `broker/filter.cc` `decoder->reset()`. The correlation map survives a reset.
- **The response-side tagged-fields no-op (D-PLAN-3).** The response decoder reads `correlation_id` ONLY (count-and-frame-skip) → never reads response tagged-fields → the ApiVersions(18) response special-case is immaterial to the count path (implemented + table-tested for completeness).
- **The `*.failure` cross-side asymmetry** (ref=2 / subj=1 abandon-at-close; see the dedicated paragraph above).
- **Runtime-key gating unmirrored; api_keys 71/72 telemetry-EXCLUDED** (86 of 88 keys carry counters — upstream parity; the two excluded keys are upstream's telemetry/push-telemetry pair).

### envoy.filters.network.redis_proxy

*Introduced by phase 32.1 (`network-filter-redis-upstream-pool-seam-and-codec`) — the first half of the SIXTH §9 Network-filters-family row (a parent pre-split row 32 with sub-rows 32.1 + 32.2 per ADR-0106(d); after the phase-26 family-parent, the phase-27 `sni_cluster` row, the phase-28 `zookeeper_proxy` parent, the phase-29 `mongo_proxy` parent, and the phase-31 `kafka_broker` flat row; the phase-30 pin-refresh was an infra row). EXTENDED by phase 32.2 (`network-filter-redis-commands-and-stats`) — the second half: the full command set + the per-command/splitter/cluster roster + the `redis.` Prometheus arm + the 2 lifecycle gauges' inc/dec + the differential command matrix + the 41st fuzzer + the parent-row-32 ROLLUP. The project's FIRST terminal routing proxy. Justified by ADR-0229 (the redis_proxy filter umbrella — ACCEPTED; both halves landed). Cross-side-PROVEN by the now-green `0055-redis-roundtrip` (the 32.1 PING/SET/GET round-trip arms + the 32.2 command matrix [GET-miss/INCR/DEL/ECHO/QUIT/HELLO-err/UNKNOWN/PING-arg] + the per-command/splitter `/stats/prometheus` assertions + the `cx_active` held-open gauge arm + the downstream-RESP byte-equivalence prong) + `0056-redis-boot-reject` fixtures.*

`redis_proxy` (`@type` `type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.redis_proxy.v3.RedisProxy` — type URL DERIVED via `proto.MessageName` on `redis_proxyv3.RedisProxy`, NOT hand-typed; the `extensions.` segment is intrinsic per `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions`) is the project's FIRST **terminal routing proxy**. It IS the connection terminator — implements `network.TerminalFilter` and owns the downstream `net.Conn` via `Handle(ctx, conn)`. There is NO `tcp_proxy` behind it. Every prior §9 network filter either OBSERVED a `tcp_proxy`-owned connection (zookeeper/mongo/kafka_broker) or published an override the `tcp_proxy` consumed (sni_cluster); redis_proxy IS the terminator.

- **Terminal-routing-proxy semantics.** `Handle` owns the downstream `net.Conn` for its lifetime. It reads RESP request frames from a `bufio.Reader` over the downstream conn (blocking on partial frames — the STREAMING-READER model, contrasted with the mongo/kafka observer PRIVATE-BUFFER model; D-P32-4), dispatches each command to either a local-reply path (PING/AUTH) or the upstream-pool seam (all other commands), and writes replies back to the downstream conn. On `io.EOF` → clean close. On decode error → close (the `downstream_cx_protocol_error` counter increment path is 32.2). The async halt/resume seam (ADR-0226) is NOT consumed — redis_proxy injects no fault delay at 32.1 (the MVP has no `MayHalt()` implementation → never-halting → byte-identical R1).

- **The RESP codec (SPEC §3.5; `resp.go`).** Request decode recognizes two frame shapes: INLINE (`<cmd>\r\n` — e.g. `PING\r\n`) and ARRAY-OF-BULK (`*<n>\r\n$<len>\r\n<bytes>\r\n...` — the canonical command encoding). Reply decode reads one frame keyed on the RESP value-type first byte: `+` (simple string — framing-only; whole line), `-` (error — framing-only), `:` (integer — `strconv.Atoi`-validated; `errProtocol` on non-numeric — the Task 6 deviation from a strict framing-only parse), `$<len>` (bulk string + null sentinel `$-1\r\n`), `*<n>` (array, recursive). Wire bytes are forwarded VERBATIM to downstream (`reference_wire_format_both_sides_see_same_bytes`, EXTENDED to the downstream RESPONSE the proxy generates — the §9 FIRST). The inline request path guards against reply-type first bytes (`+`/`-`/`:`/`$`/`@`) → `errProtocol` (a downstream reply cannot be parsed as a command — the Task 5 inline guard; controller-approved deviation).

- **`catch_all` single-cluster routing + unknown-cluster tolerance (§3.3; §4.3).** `prefix_routes.catch_all_route.cluster` is the ONLY routing target at 32.1 (`prefix_routes.routes[]` longest-prefix multi-cluster routing is 32.2). The cluster name is stored at config-parse time; on the FIRST proxied command `Handle` resolves it lazily via `cm.Get(name)` → a miss (unknown cluster at runtime) → graceful downstream close, NO `-ERR` reply (the unknown-cluster-tolerance posture; D-S32.1-6). This contrasts with `tcp_proxy`, which rejects an unknown cluster reference AT BOOT (the `tcpproxy: cluster %q not found` reject). The dial closure over the resolved `cluster.Cluster.Dial` is built at first-proxied-command time and passed to the upstream-pool seam (`network.NewUpstreamConn`).

- **PING/AUTH local-reply set (AMEND-R5; `commands.go`).** PING → `+PONG\r\n` (7 bytes); AUTH with no configured password → `-ERR Client sent AUTH, but no password is set\r\n`. Both answered LOCALLY — ZERO upstream traffic (the seam is never dialed for PING/AUTH-only connections). Both increment `downstream_rq_total` + the rx/tx byte counters. The 32.1 local-reply set is PING + AUTH; ECHO/TIME/QUIT/HELLO are 32.2 (proxied through the seam at 32.1 if a client issues them — they reach the backend).

- **Config parse + PGV/runtime reject arms (ADR-0080 byte-stable; SPEC §6).** THREE PGV hard rejects: (a) `stat_prefix` min-1 → `redis_proxy: stat_prefix is required`; (b) `settings` nil → `redis_proxy: settings is required`; (c) `settings.op_timeout` nil → `redis_proxy: settings.op_timeout is required`. ONE runtime reject: `catch_all_route.cluster` absent AND no `routes[]` → `redis_proxy: cannot configure a redis-proxy without any upstream`. The `stats.IsValidName(stat_prefix)` guard fires before stat creation (the `reference_dynamic_stat_name_charset_guard` applied at the config-parse boundary). `0056-redis-boot-reject` carries the `stat_prefix`-required arm (both sides reject at boot with a common substring `redis_proxy` in their real boot stderr — liveness proven by R6 break-liveness with `-count=1`); the other arms are unit-test-only (the `0047`/`0050`/`0054` boot-reject precedent).

- **Stats: 10 fixed downstream cx/rq counters + gauges (SPEC §7.2).** All 10 created EAGERLY at config-parse under `redis.<stat_prefix>.` via `NewCounterIfAbsent`/`NewGaugeIfAbsent`. **4 counters increment at 32.1:** `downstream_cx_total` (+1 per accepted downstream connection), `downstream_cx_rx_bytes_total` (+= raw request bytes read from downstream), `downstream_cx_tx_bytes_total` (+= reply bytes written to downstream), `downstream_rq_total` (+1 per decoded request, including PING/AUTH). **2 counters created-not-incremented (32.2):** `downstream_cx_drain_close` (drain path), `downstream_cx_protocol_error` (decode-error path). **4 gauges created-not-incremented (32.2):** `downstream_cx_active`, `downstream_cx_rx_bytes_buffered`, `downstream_cx_tx_bytes_buffered`, `downstream_rq_active` — the project's SECOND differentially-mirrored gauge family (after mongo's `op_query_active`); their inc/dec lands at 32.2. Normatively defined by `internal/filter/network/redisproxy/stats.go::rosterSuffixes()` + `TestStatRoster32_1_MatchesUpstream`. Project stat surface **536 → 546** (+10).

- **Upstream traffic stats via the EXISTING cluster roster (AMEND-R6).** `upstream_cx_total`/`upstream_cx_active`/`upstream_rq_total` are the cluster's OWN traffic stats under `cluster.<name>.*` (`internal/cluster/manager.go` — the per-cluster roster, NOT a new redis namespace). The seam reuses them: `Cluster.Dial` Incs `upstream_cx_total`/`active` on the lazy dial; the per-request hook (`Cluster.IncUpstreamRqTotal`) Incs `upstream_rq_total` per proxied command. The `0055` proxied arm asserts `cluster.redis_cluster.upstream_cx_total == 1` (one lazy dial) + `upstream_rq_total == 2` (SET + GET) cross-side EQUAL (single-conn scenario; the multi-conn divergence is 32.2, D-P32-9).

- **Differential: `0055-redis-roundtrip` (cross-side) + `0056-redis-boot-reject` (boot-reject).** `0055`: chain `[redis_proxy]` as TERMINAL on BOTH sides (no `tcp_proxy` behind it); `TCPRedisResponder` BackendKind **32** (FIFO/positional canned RESP replies: SET→`+OK\r\n`, GET→`$3\r\nbar\r\n`). Implements `fixture.StatsAsserter` (the `0053`/`0053-kafka-requests` precedent — cross-side dispatch per `reference_differential_asserter_dispatch`) scraping the flat `GET /stats` admin endpoint on both sides. 32.1 arms: (a) PING local-reply: `+PONG\r\n` byte-identical cross-side + `downstream_rq_total` +1 + `upstream_cx_total == 0`; (b) proxied SET→`+OK\r\n`, GET→`$3\r\nbar\r\n` byte-identical cross-side + stats cross-side equal. The downstream-RESP byte-equivalence prong is load-bearing (the §9 FIRST — redis_proxy GENERATES the downstream response; `reference_wire_format_both_sides_see_same_bytes`, extended). R4 deliberate-break liveness recorded with `-count=1` (5 breaks: counter==99, wrong-byte PONG, wrong-byte OK, wrong-byte GET reply, upstream_cx_total==2 — each FAIL then revert→PASS). 32.2 extends `0055` with the command matrix + splitter arms (same dir). `0056`: symmetric `BootRejectFixture` (`stat_prefix` missing → both sides reject at boot).

- **The 10th built-in + ZERO new go.mod dep (AMEND-R1 / D32-1).** Registered in `internal/filter/network/builtins/builtins.go` (doc "nine" → "ten") + `main.go` parity; the `redis_proxy/v3` blank-import in `internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go` holds the TypeURL in the proto registry. redis_proxy/v3 is a subpackage of the ALREADY-DIRECT `/envoy v1.32.4` module → `go mod tidy` adds NOTHING (the opposite of kafka_broker's first-`/contrib` dep).

- **Close-direction-zero-touch (AMEND-R9).** NO close-direction-keyed counters (only `downstream_cx_drain_close` — a drain counter — NOT a `cx_destroy_*` keyed on LOCAL/REMOTE). The 29.3 `CloseDirection()` machinery is NOT consumed at 32.1 (`reference_close_direction_framework_gap` does not bite).

**Coverage boundaries / departures (phase 32.1):**
- **`op_timeout` parsed-not-consumed.** PGV-REQUIRED at boot; not wired to a dial/write deadline at 32.1.
- **4 gauges created-not-incremented (32.2).** `downstream_cx_active` / `downstream_cx_rx_bytes_buffered` / `downstream_cx_tx_bytes_buffered` / `downstream_rq_active` exist-at-zero from boot; their inc/dec paths are 32.2.
- **2 counters created-not-incremented (32.2).** `downstream_cx_drain_close` + `downstream_cx_protocol_error` exist-at-zero; increment wiring is 32.2.
- **Boot-window eager-vs-per-connection difference (unobservable).** envoy-go creates the 10 stats eagerly at config-load; upstream creates per-connection. UNOBSERVABLE to the differential (every `0055` assertion is post-connection — the D-P32-1 precedent).
- **Runtime-keys-at-defaults.** The filter behaves at the proto-configured values; runtime keys are at defaults (the §9 family boundary).
- **Close-direction-zero-touch (AMEND-R9).** No `cx_destroy_*` close-direction counters → framework ZERO-touch (the `reference_close_direction_framework_gap` does not bite).
- **The `redis.` LABEL-HOISTED Prometheus tag-extractor arm is 32.2.** The 32.1 differential uses the flat `GET /stats` internal-name scrape; `/stats/prometheus` omits `redis.*` until the arm lands.
- **Unknown-cluster graceful-close-no-`-ERR` (D-S32.1-6).** A runtime cluster-miss on `cm.Get(catchAllCluster)` → clean downstream TCP close, no `-ERR` reply.
- **One-conn-per-downstream pooling divergence (D-P32-9, forward-pointer 32.2).** The reference multiplexes all downstream conns onto one upstream conn per host; envoy-go creates one upstream conn per downstream conn. Unobservable in the single-connection 32.1 differential; pinned per-side at the 32.2 SPEC.
- **The HTTP-shaped `cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_2xx..5xx` have no RESP analog** — they stay at 0 per-side (not asserted in `0055`).
- **`prefix_routes.routes[]` longest-prefix multi-cluster routing is 32.2+.** Only `catch_all_route` is consumed at 32.1.
- **The deferred active features are PARSE-ACCEPTED-behavior-DEFERRED.** `prefix_routes` multi-cluster, hash-ring sharding + `enable_redirection`, multi-key fragmentation, `downstream_auth_*`, `faults`, request mirroring, replica `read_policy`, `custom_commands`, the full `ConnPoolSettings` surface — all parse-accepted at boot, not consumed at runtime.

**Phase 32.2 extension — the full command set, the per-command/splitter/cluster roster, the gauges' inc/dec, the `redis.` Prometheus arm, and the command matrix.**

- **The full single-route command set + the unknown/bad-arity dispatch (`commands.go`, `filter.go`).** A static 180-command supported-commands table (`supportedCommandList`/`supportedCommands`; lower-cased once at dispatch — the table member IS the `command.<cmd>.*` stat segment, so `IsValidName` holds by construction). `classify(cmd, args)` returns a `commandVerdict{action, reply, closeAfter, statCmd}` driving: an UNKNOWN command (not in the table) → `splitter.unsupported_command` + a byte-stable `-ERR unknown command…` reply; a bad-arity command → `splitter.invalid_request` + a byte-stable `-invalid request` reply; a valid command → proxied through the seam.

- **Per-command `command.<cmd>.{total,success,error}` + single-server semantics.** For each proxied command: `command.<cmd>.total` increments at dispatch; `command.<cmd>.success` on ANY decoded reply (including `-ERR`, `$-1`, `*-1` — a redis-server-level error is still a successfully round-tripped reply); `command.<cmd>.error` ONLY on a transport-or-pool failure (Send/decode error, conn closed before reply, unresolvable cluster). This is the single-server success-on-any-reply / error-on-transport-failure model (multi-key fragmentation is DEFERRED — MGET/MSET/DEL proxy single-server).

- **The extended local-reply set ECHO/TIME/QUIT/HELLO (`commands.go`).** ECHO echoes its arg (arity≠2 → `splitter.invalid_request`); QUIT writes `+OK\r\n` then closes (the `commandVerdict.closeAfter` signal); TIME returns a wall-clock 2-element array (NON-deterministic → UNIT-test-only, NOT a differential arm); HELLO is SPLIT — `>2` args → an options-error, a non-"2" protocol arg (incl. "3") → NOPROTO, BUT `HELLO 2`/no-arg is PROXIED (`command.hello.*` + forwarded). Because HELLO with no args is a valid proxied command, `commandsWithoutMandatoryArgs = {hello}` (HELLO must NOT be a bad-arity reject). PING/AUTH/ECHO/TIME/QUIT emit NO `command.*`; HELLO error-paths emit no `command.hello.*`. **The UNKNOWN-command error wording APPENDS the request args** (NOT an empty suffix — the reference is the source of truth; `unknownCommandError` joins `args[1:]` with `", "`); byte-exact confirmed cross-side for `BOGUSCMD x`: `-ERR unknown command 'BOGUSCMD', with args beginning with: x\r\n`.

- **The 2 lifecycle gauges' inc/dec + the `downstream_cx_protocol_error` wiring.** `downstream_cx_active` is inc'd at `Handle` entry and dec'd at exit (MIRRORED — the `0055` held-open arm asserts == 1 live on both sides); `downstream_rq_active` is per-request defer-balanced in `serveRequest` (QUIESCED — asserted == 0 at every measured point). `downstream_cx_protocol_error` increments on a non-EOF decode error (a clean EOF close leaves it at 0). The 2 `*_bytes_buffered` gauges remain a SUBJECT-SIDE coverage boundary (see below).

- **The EAGER 545 new stats.** Created at config-parse under `redis.<stat_prefix>.` via `NewCounterIfAbsent`: 180 × 3 = 540 per-command `command.<cmd>.{total,success,error}` + 2 `splitter.{unsupported_command,invalid_request}` + 3 `REDIS_CLUSTER_STATS`. Project stat surface **546 → 1091** (+545: 2 splitter + 3 cluster + 540 per-command; the 180 `command.<cmd>.latency` histograms + the `*_fault` counters are NOT counted per ADR-0060).

#### Prometheus exposition — the `redis.` tag-extractor arm

A `redis.`-prefixed internal name renders with a SINGLE-label hoist: `envoy_redis_<leaf>{envoy_redis_prefix="<stat_prefix>"}`. The `<stat_prefix>` segment is HOISTED into one `envoy_redis_prefix` label; the command name STAYS in the metric leaf (e.g. `redis.default.command.get.total` → `envoy_redis_command_get_total{envoy_redis_prefix="default"}`). Shape-detected via `strings.CutPrefix(internal, "redis.")` at `internal/stats/name.go`. Contrast: the kafka arm is INLINE (fully inlined `envoy_kafka_<sp>_<rest>{}`, EMPTY labels); the mongo arm is MULTI-label (multiple tag-extracted dimensions). The `redis.` arm is the mongo `.rbac.` SINGLE-label-hoist shape.

**Coverage boundaries / departures (phase 32.2):**
- **The 180 `command.<cmd>.latency` histograms are UNMIRRORED (ADR-0060).** The project-wide histogram deferral; only the 540 counters are created.
- **The `*_fault` counters are DEFERRED.** Faults are parse-accepted-behavior-deferred; their counter family is not created.
- **The 2 `*_bytes_buffered` gauges are a SUBJECT-SIDE coverage boundary.** The reference legitimately tracks them (`downstream_cx_rx_bytes_buffered == 14` — the held PING request frame parked unconsumed); the subject never wires them. Asserted SUBJECT == 0 only (non-vacuous — proves rendered + not spuriously incremented); the reference is not asserted.
- **The 3 REDIS_CLUSTER_STATS exist-at-0.** Created eagerly; the cluster-mode redirection paths that would increment them are deferred (single-route MVP).
- **TIME is unit-test-only** (wall-clock NON-deterministic — shape-only goldens, no differential arm).
- **HELLO 2/no-arg is PROXIED** (`command.hello.*` + forwarded); only the HELLO error-paths are local.
- **Multi-key fragmentation DEFERRED** (MGET/MSET/DEL proxied single-server).
- **One-conn-per-downstream per-side `upstream_cx_total` divergence (D-P32-9).** The `0055` command matrix exposes the documented seam divergence: the reference POOLS the upstream (`cluster.redis_cluster.upstream_cx_total == 1`); the subject lazy-dials one upstream conn per proxied-command downstream conn (`== 4`: SET/GET + GET-miss + INCR + DEL). PINNED per-side (ref=1/subj=4). The pooling-independent `upstream_rq_total == 5` stays cross-side EQUAL.
- **`op_timeout` parsed-not-consumed** (PGV-REQUIRED at boot; still not wired to a deadline at 32.2).
- **`enable_command_stats` is a no-op** (gates neither presence nor increment in v1.37.2 — the eager roster + increments are unconditional).
- **Close-direction-zero-touch (AMEND-R9).** Still no close-direction-keyed counters → framework ZERO-touch (the `reference_close_direction_framework_gap` does not bite).

### envoy.filters.network.thrift_proxy

*Introduced by phase 33 (`network-filter-thrift-proxy`) — the SEVENTH §9 Network-filters-family row (a flat top-level row per ADR-0106; after the phase-26 family-parent, the phase-27 `sni_cluster` row, the phase-28 `zookeeper_proxy` parent, the phase-29 `mongo_proxy` parent, the phase-31 `kafka_broker` flat row, and the phase-32 `redis_proxy` parent). The project's SECOND terminal routing proxy (after redis_proxy at phase 32) and the LAST §9 candidate — the §9 Network-filters family CLOSES after this phase. Justified by ADR-0231 (the `thrift_proxy` filter umbrella — ACCEPTED; §Decision/§Consequences body landed at this IMPL per ADR-0044). The FIRST row to REUSE a prior framework seam UNCHANGED (the ADR-0230 upstream connection-pool / cluster-routing seam — thrift is its anticipated SECOND consumer, validating the redis-scoped YAGNI sizing). Cross-side-PROVEN by the now-green `0057-thrift-roundtrip` (route-HIT round-trip + route-MISS local-exception + reply-EXCEPTION arms; downstream-Thrift-response byte-equivalence + `StatsAsserter`) + `0058-thrift-boot-reject` fixtures.*

`thrift_proxy` (`@type` `type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.thrift_proxy.v3.ThriftProxy` — type URL DERIVED via `proto.MessageName` on `thrift_proxyv3.ThriftProxy`, NOT hand-typed; the `extensions.` segment is intrinsic per `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions`, D-T1) is the project's SECOND **terminal routing proxy**. It IS the connection terminator — implements `network.TerminalFilter` and owns the downstream `net.Conn` via `Handle(ctx, conn)`. There is NO `tcp_proxy` behind it (the redis_proxy precedent).

- **Single-pair single-route terminal envelope (SPEC §3; D-T2).** The MVP decodes ONE transport×protocol pair — **framed × binary** (pinned live: framed = 4-byte BE frame-len prefix; binary strict message-begin `0x8001 00 <msgtype>` + i32 name-len + name + i32 `seq_id`) — under `payload_passthrough` (route on the message-begin envelope, forward the struct body opaquely → `request_passthrough`/`response_passthrough` increment). AUTO_TRANSPORT/AUTO_PROTOCOL auto-detect framed-binary identically. The `Handle` pump reads message-begin frames from a `bufio.Reader` over the downstream conn (the streaming-reader model — the redis precedent).

- **`route_config` method-routing (`route.go`; SPEC §4).** A single exact-match (or match-all) method route → ONE upstream cluster. First-match wins; on a method routing MISS → a LOCAL `UnknownMethod` Thrift EXCEPTION (zero upstream — the redis-PING analogue, D-T5; `encodeUnknownMethod(method, seqID)` builds the byte-identical reference miss-path reply; the MVP keeps the connection open). `route_config` is NOT a hard PGV gate (absent → all methods miss → all local exceptions).

- **The REUSED ADR-0230 upstream round-trip (`filter.go`; Q-seam).** Each `Handle` builds a `network.NewUpstreamConn(dial, cl.IncUpstreamRqTotal)` over a dial closure (`Cluster.Dial`, keeping `internal/filter/network` free of an `internal/cluster` import); the synchronous single-flight pump reads one request frame → `up.Send` → reads one reply frame from `up.Reader()` → classifies (success/error first-field peek) → writes the reply downstream. ZERO new seam code; the seam is UNCHANGED. `seq_id` is parse-validated + passed-through (NOT demux-load-bearing — the reference remaps the upstream `seq_id` to 0 + restores the original downstream, so downstream byte-equivalence holds under pass-through; the upstream `seq_id` is a per-side boundary). A defensive cross-cluster re-dial branch (a second route resolving a different cluster mid-connection) is unit-tested live (the Task-8-followup test).

- **Config parse + PGV/departure reject arms (ADR-0080 byte-stable; SPEC §6; D-T4/AMEND-T7).** ONE hard PGV gate: `stat_prefix` min-1 → `thrift_proxy: stat_prefix is required` (+ the `stats.IsValidName(stat_prefix)` guard at the config boundary per `reference_dynamic_stat_name_charset_guard`). The un-chosen transport/protocol enum values are **envoy-go-strict DEPARTURE rejects** (the reference parse-ACCEPTS them — so these are unit-tested, NOT cross-side boot-reject arms): `thrift_proxy: unsupported transport (only AUTO_TRANSPORT and FRAMED are supported)` + `thrift_proxy: unsupported protocol (only AUTO_PROTOCOL and BINARY are supported)`. `0058-thrift-boot-reject` carries the `stat_prefix`-required arm (both sides reject at boot with a common substring in their real boot stderr; liveness proven by R6 break-liveness with `-count=1`).

- **The malformed-frame silent-close departure (D-S33-6).** A framing error (`errDecode`) counts `request_decoding_error` then SILENTLY CLOSES — NO local `ProtocolError` exception (a documented coverage-boundary departure). A distinct `errInvalidType` sentinel splits invalid-msgtype → `request_invalid_type`.

- **Stats: the EAGER 25-name roster under `thrift.<stat_prefix>.` (SPEC §7; D-T3).** 24 counters + 1 GAUGE `request_active` created EAGERLY at config-parse via `NewCounterIfAbsent`/`NewGaugeIfAbsent`. The 24 counters: `request`, `request_call`, `request_oneway`, `request_passthrough`, `request_decoding_error`, `request_invalid_type`, `request_internal_error`, `response`, `response_reply`, `response_success`, `response_error`, `response_exception`, `response_passthrough`, `response_decoding_error`, `response_invalid_type`, `route_missing`, `unknown_cluster`, `no_healthy_upstream`, `shadow_request_submit_failure`, `upstream_rq_maintenance_mode`, `cx_destroy_local_with_active_rq`, `cx_destroy_remote_with_active_rq`, `downstream_cx_max_requests`, `downstream_response_drain_close`. The gauge `request_active` is the project's THIRD differentially-mirrored gauge family (after mongo's `op_query_active` + redis's `downstream_cx_active`); QUIESCED-to-0 post-workload (D-S33-3 — no held-open arm). Normatively defined by `internal/filter/network/thriftproxy/stats.go::counterSuffixes`. Project stat surface **1091 → 1116** (+25). The `request_time_ms` histogram is DEFERRED (ADR-0060 — the registry has no Histogram type).

- **The 11th built-in + ZERO new go.mod dep (D-T1).** Registered in `internal/filter/network/builtins/builtins.go` (the two-dep factory — `ClusterManager` + `StatsRegistry`) + `main.go` parity; the `thrift_proxy/v3` blank-import in `internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go` holds the TypeURL. thrift_proxy/v3 is a subpackage of the ALREADY-DIRECT `/envoy v1.32.4` module → `go mod tidy` adds NOTHING (the redis D32-1 posture — the OPPOSITE of kafka_broker's `/contrib` dep).

- **Differential: `0057-thrift-roundtrip` (cross-side) + `0058-thrift-boot-reject` (boot-reject).** `0057`: chain `[thrift_proxy]` as TERMINAL on BOTH sides; `TCPThriftResponder` BackendKind **33** (framed-binary canned REPLY echoing method + received `seq_id`, seq_id-agnostic; optional exception mode). Implements `fixture.StatsAsserter` scraping the flat `GET /stats` admin endpoint cross-side. Three arms: (a) route-HIT round-trip (Ping) — downstream byte-identical + `request`/`request_call`/`request_passthrough`/`response`/`response_reply`/`response_success`/`response_passthrough` +1 + `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_total`/`upstream_rq_total` +1; (b) route-MISS (Pong) — the local `UnknownMethod` EXCEPTION bytes byte-identical cross-side + `route_missing`/`response_exception` +1; (c) reply-EXCEPTION (boom) — a BACKEND exception, `response_exception` +1 + a second upstream cx/rq. The downstream-Thrift-response byte-equivalence prong is load-bearing (the §9 SECOND after redis-32 — thrift_proxy GENERATES the downstream response). R4 deliberate-break liveness recorded with `-count=1`.

#### Prometheus exposition — the `thrift.` tag-extractor arm

A `thrift.`-prefixed internal name renders with a SINGLE-label hoist: `envoy_thrift_<leaf>{envoy_thrift_prefix="<stat_prefix>"}`. The `<stat_prefix>` segment is HOISTED into one `envoy_thrift_prefix` label; the remaining leaf STAYS in the metric name (e.g. `thrift.default.request_call` → `envoy_thrift_request_call{envoy_thrift_prefix="default"}`). Shape-detected via `strings.CutPrefix(internal, "thrift.")` at `internal/stats/name.go`. The redis-32 / mongo `.rbac.` SINGLE-label-hoist shape — NOT the kafka inline (empty-label) shape.

**Coverage boundaries / departures (phase 33):**
- **The `request_time_ms` histogram is UNMIRRORED (ADR-0060).** The project-wide histogram deferral; only the 24 counters + 1 gauge are created.
- **The 2 close-direction counters + `downstream_response_drain_close` are created-but-NEVER-incremented (the `reference_close_direction_framework_gap` boundary, AMEND-T6/D-T8).** `cx_destroy_local_with_active_rq` + `cx_destroy_remote_with_active_rq` (the framework records close TYPE not DIRECTION) + `downstream_response_drain_close` (the reply-completion drain close). SHARPER than redis-32: the reference DOES fire `cx_destroy_local_with_active_rq` + `downstream_response_drain_close` on the live `0057` routing-MISS arm (where it `FlushWrite`-closes after the local exception) → asserted PER-SIDE on the miss arm (the subject pins 0; the reference moves them). The framework-surgery sub-phase that would key close counters by direction stays deferred project-wide.
- **Per-side `request*` on a routing MISS (a documented behavioral divergence; PINNED per-side in `0057`).** The subject's pump increments `request`/`request_call`/`request_passthrough` at the TOP of the pump — BEFORE the route match — so a routing MISS counts them (count-before-match: Ping + Pong + boom → **subj=3** across the 3-arm workload). The C++ reference does NOT count `request*` on a miss (the miss is accounted ONLY via `route_missing`+`response_exception` per SPEC §7.3 / D-T5, live-confirmed: "request* do NOT move" on the miss → **ref=2**, HIT-only: Ping+boom). Asserted PER-SIDE in `0057` (ref=2/subj=3, NOT cross-equal) — a documented per-side divergence, NOT a subject bug.
- **The subject's cluster package does NOT emit `upstream_cx_rx_bytes_total` (SPEC §7.5).** It reuses ONLY `upstream_cx_total`/`upstream_rq_total` (the redis AMEND-R6 precedent). The decode-ran byte-witness is reference-side only (`cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_rx_bytes_total > 0`, ref=73 observed); the subject witness is `thrift.<sp>.request_call > 0` (both sides asserted). `upstream_cx_total` is PER-SIDE (ref=1 pooled — one upstream conn serves both proxied calls / subj=2 — one-conn-per-downstream, each HIT downstream dials 1 upstream; the redis D-P32-9 precedent, D-T9b); the pooling-independent `upstream_rq_total == 2` stays cross-side EQUAL.
- **The un-chosen transport×protocol pairs are envoy-go-strict DEPARTURE rejects (D-T4/AMEND-T7).** The reference parse-ACCEPTS the full 3×3 matrix; the MVP rejects every pair except framed×binary (+ AUTO) at config-parse → unit-tested, NOT cross-side boot-reject arms.
- **The non-router `thrift_filters` / full `route_config` richness / full struct-body parsing are PARSE-ACCEPTED-behavior-DEFERRED.** Only the implicit router sub-chain runs; `service_name`/header-matches/multi-cluster/mirror, `rate_limit`/`header_to_metadata`/`payload_to_metadata` thrift-filters, and full struct parsing (passthrough off) are parse-accepted, not consumed.
- **The upstream `seq_id` per-side difference.** The reference remaps the upstream `seq_id` to 0 + restores the original downstream; the MVP passes `seq_id` through. Downstream byte-equivalence holds; the upstream `seq_id` value is a per-side boundary (not asserted).
- **Malformed-frame silent-close (no local `ProtocolError`; D-S33-6).** A framing error counts `request_decoding_error` + closes silently — the reference would emit a local `ProtocolError` exception; the MVP does not (a coverage-boundary departure).
- **`seq_id`-keyed multiplexing / `max_requests_per_connection` / `access_log` DEFERRED.** The deferred multiplexing surface (seq_id-keyed demux / shared pool / deep queue / pipelining) stays DEFERRED for a future thrift latency/fan-out sub-phase.
- **Runtime-keys-at-defaults.** The filter behaves at the proto-configured values; runtime keys are at defaults (the §9 family boundary).

## Network filters — upstream connection-pool / cluster-routing seam (32.1)

*Introduced by phase 32.1 (`network-filter-redis-upstream-pool-seam-and-codec`) — the framework's SIXTH structural extension (after the ADR-0221 `network.WriteFilter` conn-wrap seam [28.1], the ADR-0219 upstream-cluster-override seam [27], the ADR-0226 async halt/resume seam [29.3], the ADR-0213 terminal-filter seam [26.2], and the listener/chain dispatch framework [26.1]). Justified by ADR-0230 (ACCEPTED — body LANDED at the 32.1 IMPL). The seam ADR — the analogue of ADR-0221 (the WriteFilter seam) / ADR-0226 (the async halt/resume seam). ADDITIVE: it activates ONLY for a `redis_proxy` terminal → all 56 pre-existing fixture dirs byte-identical (R1).*

The L4 filter framework gains the FIRST primitive for a terminal filter to ACTIVELY manage an upstream connection (dial + per-downstream lifecycle + ordered request↔reply round-trip), rather than OBSERVE a `tcp_proxy`-terminated one. This is the upstream-connection analogue of the ADR-0221 WriteFilter seam (which gave read-side observers a write-side callback) and the ADR-0226 halt/resume seam (which gave read-side observers an async control-flow primitive).

- **The exported surface (`internal/filter/network/upstreampool.go`).** THREE exported identifiers: `UpstreamDialFunc func(ctx context.Context) (net.Conn, error)` (the closure type — the consumer supplies a closure over `Cluster.Dial`, keeping `internal/filter/network` free of an `internal/cluster` import); `UpstreamConn struct` (one downstream connection's dedicated upstream connection: `dial UpstreamDialFunc` + `onRequest func()` hook + `conn net.Conn` + `r *bufio.Reader`); `NewUpstreamConn(dial UpstreamDialFunc, onRequest func()) *UpstreamConn` (binds the closure + the per-proxied-request hook; no dial at construction). THREE methods: `Send(ctx, reqBytes []byte) error` (lazy dial on first call; fires the `onRequest` hook → writes `reqBytes` upstream); `Reader() *bufio.Reader` (returns the stable buffered reader for reply-frame decode — valid after the first `Send`); `Close() error` (idempotent; no-op if never dialed).

- **One-conn-per-downstream multiplexing + synchronous single-flight FIFO (D-P32-3; AMEND-R8).** Each `Handle(ctx, downstream)` creates its own `*UpstreamConn` on the stack and `defer up.Close()`s it. The pump is synchronous: read one request frame → `up.Send` → read one reply frame from `up.Reader()` → write reply → loop. This is a DEGENERATE depth-1 FIFO — the FIFO/positional pop-front CONTRACT (R4) satisfied trivially. A pipelining client (multiple requests in one write before reading) is handled correctly: the requests sit buffered and are processed in order, replies returned in order. No concurrent in-flight upstream requests at 32.1.

- **Lazy dial + PING/AUTH-only connection never dials.** On the FIRST proxied (data) command, `Send` finds `u.conn == nil` and calls the closure → `Cluster.Dial(ctx)` → Incs `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_total`/`upstream_cx_active` → stores the `net.Conn` + builds the `bufio.Reader`. A PING-only or AUTH-only connection never calls `Send` on a data command → `u.conn` stays `nil` → `Close()` is a no-op. The `*connWithGauge` returned by `Cluster.Dial` Decs `upstream_cx_active` on `Close()`.

- **Dial-closure decoupling (the `upstreamcluster.go` discipline preserved).** `internal/filter/network/` gains NO `internal/cluster` import — verified by `go list -deps ./internal/filter/network | grep internal/cluster` → empty (CLEAN). The `redisproxy` filter (which imports both, like `tcp_proxy`) resolves `catch_all_route.cluster` via `cm.Get(name)` and supplies the seam a `func(ctx) (net.Conn, error)` closure over `cl.Dial(ctx)` (endpoint discarded). The seam never sees a cluster name or a `*cluster.Cluster`.

- **The seam knows NOTHING about RESP framing.** `Reader()` returns a `bufio.Reader`; the codec (`decodeReply`) reads reply frames from it. The seam is a connection-lifecycle + ordered-round-trip primitive; it is reusable for any future terminal-proxy protocol (thrift — the last §9 candidate — reuses/extends it at its phase, the extract-at-second-consumer discipline).

- **Redis-scoped boundary (32.1).** NO thrift generalization (YAGNI at 32.1). The seam catches the `redisproxy` filter's routing decision (`catch_all` → `cluster.Manager.Get`) and the specific `onRequest` hook (`Cluster.IncUpstreamRqTotal`). Future consumers extend the seam at their phase; the ADR-0230 deferred boundary records what is intentionally NOT built.

- **No per-connection mutex at 32.1.** The single-flight synchronous pump is single-goroutine (each `Handle` on its own goroutine with its own `*UpstreamConn`); the ADR-0223 per-conn mutex is NOT needed at 32.1. It arrives only with the deferred two-goroutine pipelined model.

**ADDITIVE — existing-fixture byte-equivalence (R1).** The seam activates ONLY inside a `redis_proxy` terminal's `Handle`; it is a NEW file in `internal/filter/network/` with NO modification to any existing file in that package. All 56 pre-existing fixture dirs are byte-identical after the 32.1 IMPL (confirmed by the six-gate 58-dir full differential suite — 56 pre-existing dirs PASS byte-exact).

**Deferred (the consume-at-second-consumer boundary, §4.4):**
- **The shared per-host pool + cross-downstream multiplexing.** The reference's one-client-per-host model (one upstream conn multiplexed across all downstream conns, thread-local) → per-side `upstream_cx_*` divergence under concurrent downstream conns (D-P32-9; pinned per-side at the 32.2 SPEC).
- **The >1-depth pending queue + the two-goroutine read/write split.** A dedicated send goroutine + a receive goroutine with a bounded `[]pendingRequest` queue (the ADR-0223 per-conn mutex guard) — deferred to the pipelined model sub-phase.
- **`op_timeout` enforcement.** Parsed, not consumed at 32.1.

### Network filter chain framework — async halt/resume (29.3 amendment)

*Introduced by phase 29.3 (`network-filter-mongo-fault-delay-and-access-log`). Justified by ADR-0226 (the framework's FIFTH structural extension — the async halt/resume seam) CONSUMING the ADR-0221 §Consequences anticipated-halt-consumer allowance (REFINED to the READ side). NO operator-visible behavior change to any never-halting chain: every chain whose read filters all report `MayHalt()==false` (zookeeper, echo, direct_response, rbac_network, sni_cluster, mongo-without-`delay`) takes the byte-identical pre-29.3 path (R1, ratified by the full 53-dir back-compat suite + h2spec 53/53 + proxy-wasm 10/10 staying green). 29.3 is the framework-SURGERY sub-phase — the ONE consolidated ripple (ADR-0219) that also lands the close-direction recording + the drain-state accessor.*

The L4 chain framework gains a cross-goroutine async halt/resume capability, strictly opt-in behind a construction-time gate. It is the FIRST genuine cross-goroutine concurrency in the chain runtime (a `time.AfterFunc` timer goroutine resumes a chain the read-loop / pump goroutine parked).

- **The `MayHalt` haltable gate (the R1 fast-path).** A read filter may opt in by implementing `HaltingReadFilter` (`MayHalt() bool`). `newChainRuntime` checks it ONCE at construction: if ANY built read filter returns `MayHalt()==true`, the whole `chainRuntime` is `haltable`. When `!haltable`, `runData`/`replayRead`/`readChainConn.Read` take the byte-identical pre-29.3 path — the never-halting hot path pays NO synchronization cost (no lock, no cond, no hold). `mongo_proxy` reports `MayHalt()==true` ONLY when a `delay` is configured; every other network filter reports false.
- **The block-the-dispatcher hold (halt mutex + cond + `resumeReady`).** On a haltable chain, the halt/resume state (`held`/`resumeReady`/`replayIdx`/`replayHeld`) is guarded by a per-`chainRuntime` halt `sync.Mutex` (`haltMu`) + `sync.Cond` (`haltCond`) — the ADR-0223 minimal-critical-section discipline, guarding EXACTLY that state. When a halting filter returns a hold StopIteration, the dispatcher goroutine calls `holdUntilResume` and BLOCKS on `haltCond.Wait()`; the timer goroutine's `ContinueReading` → `releaseResume` broadcasts to unblock it, which then advances PAST the halting filter (upstream `std::next(filter->entry())` parity). Because the dispatcher BLOCKS, the async resume re-enters via the SAME goroutine — `serveNetworkChain`/`handleTerminal` are UNCHANGED (D-S29.3-2). **The `resumeReady` missed-wakeup guard:** a `ContinueReading` firing BETWEEN `OnData`'s return and `holdUntilResume` acquiring `haltMu` sets `resumeReady=true` (no holder to broadcast to); `holdUntilResume` checks `resumeReady` under `haltMu` before `Wait`ing and consumes it (no `Wait`), closing the timer-fires-before-the-holder-blocks race.
- **The post-handoff withhold-until-resume (the 28.1b §3.5 boundary lifted for HALT purposes ONLY).** With the production chain `[mongo_proxy, tcp_proxy]`, terminal handoff happens after the first successful `OnData` pass → in steady state ALL mongo decode runs post-handoff via `replayRead` on the terminal's downstream-pump goroutine, so the post-handoff path is the LOAD-BEARING one. On a haltable chain `replayRead` stops at the halting filter, parks `replayIdx`, and publishes the pinned park-state `replayHeld`; `readChainConn.Read` then holds (`holdUntilResume`) instead of returning the held bytes to the terminal's pump. On resume the parked replay finishes (`finishParkedReplayLocked`) and the bytes flow to the remaining filters + the pump. The three 28.1b post-handoff observational boundaries (StopIteration ignored / Close not acted on / ContinueReading meaningless) are UNCHANGED for never-halting filters — the boundary is lifted for HALT purposes only. **The `replayHeld` publication fence (the real production race the IMPL caught at Task 4):** `replayRead` originally published `rt.replayHeld = true` OUTSIDE `haltMu` while `ContinueReading` reads it UNDER `haltMu`; the halting filter arms its async resume DURING `OnData` (before that write lands), so the resume goroutine's guarded read raced the unguarded write → the fix publishes `replayHeld` UNDER `haltMu` (the fence). Proven NECESSARY by a `-count=1` deliberate-break `-race` DATA RACE (reverted clean; `TestSeamRaceReplayPublication` passes `-race -count=20`).
- **Never-halting byte-identical equivalence (R1).** The whole seam is gated behind the `haltable` flag; the never-halting population (every existing filter + mongo-without-delay) is byte-identical to the pre-29.3 framework. This is the R1 equivalence guarantee made concrete and is the back-compat / non-perturbation gate (the 53-dir suite + the `0052` no-delay arm + h2spec 53/53 + proxy-wasm 10/10).
- **The close-direction accessor (`CloseDirection()`).** A minimal accessor on `ReadFilterCallbacks`/`Connection` returns the post-handoff close direction (LOCAL / REMOTE / unset), backed by `chainRuntime.closeDir` (atomic first-wins CAS, recorded by `tcp_proxy`'s pump goroutines — whichever `io.Copy` EOF'd first; the downstream→upstream pump first = LOCAL, the upstream→downstream pump first = REMOTE). **The non-promoting forwarding trap (`reference_conn_wrap_method_no_promote`):** `prefixConn`/`writeChainConn` embed `net.Conn` as an INTERFACE so `readChainConn.SetCloseDirection` does NOT auto-promote — EXPLICIT forwarding methods on `prefixconn.go`+`writeconn.go` are MANDATORY (`TestCloseDirectionThroughWrapStack` is the through-the-real-wrap-stack guard).
- **The drain-state accessor (`Draining()`).** A minimal structural `DrainState` interface (`Draining() bool`) on `ReadFilterCallbacks`, backed by the phase-08.2 `*drain.Manager` (at the listener `rt.dm`) — NOT a `*drain.Manager` leak; threaded via `SetDrainState(rt.dm)` guarded `if rt.dm != nil` (a typed-nil `*drain.Manager` boxed in the interface is non-nil and would panic in `Draining()`). Folded into the SAME callbacks-extension ripple as `CloseDirection()` (ADR-0219 one ripple).

**New coverage boundaries (29.3):**
- **The access-log timing-bearing differential boundary (AMEND-B10).** The mongo access log's `time` field is per-message wall clock → cross-side log comparison is NOT viable → the proof is formatter unit goldens (timestamp asserted by shape) + this boundary, NO fixture dir.
- **The runtime-key-gating boundary (§2.6).** `mongo.drain_close_enabled` / `mongo.fault.*` / `mongo.logging_enabled` are unmirrored (the filter behaves at the proto-configured values); recorded at 29.3 (the natural home — fault/drain/logging all consult these keys upstream).

### tcp_proxy per-connection cluster resolution — 27 amendment

*Amended by phase 27 (`network-filter-sni-cluster`). Justified by ADR-0219 (the connection-scoped upstream-cluster-override seam). NO operator-visible behavior change to `tcp_proxy` when no override is published — the no-override path is byte-exact with master tip (the existing `tcp_proxy` fixtures `0000`/`0001`/`0002` + the 26.x network fixtures stay green — the regression gate).*

At master tip `tcp_proxy` resolved its upstream cluster ONCE at boot (the configured `cluster:` → a stored `*cluster.Cluster`). Phase 27 makes the resolution per-connection: the `Filter` retains a `*cluster.Manager` + the boot-resolved `defaultCluster` (the configured cluster). At `Handle` (before the Dial), `tcp_proxy` resolves the effective cluster:

- **Override present & non-empty** → `cm.Get(override)`: found → that cluster (even if it equals the configured name — `cm.Get` resolves identically, no special case); MISS (unknown cluster) → close the downstream connection with ZERO application bytes (`log.Printf("tcpproxy: per-connection override cluster %q not found", override)` + `return`). This mirrors Envoy's unknown-override path behaviorally (`getThreadLocalCluster` null → `downstream_cx_no_route` + `NoFlush` close — the downstream sees a zero-byte close; F-NOROUTE / D27-4).
- **Override absent / empty** → `defaultCluster` → byte-exact with master tip (F-RESOLVE).

The override is the envoy-go stand-in for Envoy's `PerConnectionCluster` filter-state entry (key `envoy.tcp_proxy.cluster`), threaded out-of-band on the call `ctx` (`network.UpstreamClusterOverride(ctx)`) so the `TerminalFilter.Handle(ctx, conn)` signature (shared by HCM) is UNCHANGED. The `NewFilter` boot-time parse + the byte-stable `tcpproxy: cluster %q not found` / `weighted_clusters` rejects are UNCHANGED. `weighted_clusters` is moot — envoy-go rejects it at parse, keeping it on the single-cluster path where Envoy honors the override (F-WEIGHTED).

**Coverage boundary — `downstream_cx_no_route` (and the wider `downstream_cx_*` family) is a known-unmirrored upstream counter.** Envoy increments `tcp.<stat_prefix>.downstream_cx_no_route` on the unknown-override path (F-NOROUTE / D27-4). envoy-go's `tcp_proxy` emits NO `downstream_cx_*` counters at all today (a pre-existing gap, NOT introduced by phase 27); adding a single `downstream_cx_no_route` only on the override-miss path would be an inconsistent partial of an absent family. Phase 27 DEFERS the whole `downstream_cx_*` family (+0) and records `downstream_cx_no_route` as a known-unmirrored upstream counter. The unknown-override behavior (downstream close / zero bytes) IS proven cross-side byte-exact (fixture `0045-sni-cluster` arm 3); the stat absence is invisible to a response-body differential. The narrow typed override is the envoy-go stand-in for Envoy's `envoy.tcp_proxy.cluster` filter-state key — there is NO general connection-scoped filter-state primitive (Q2/YAGNI; it generalizes if/when a SECOND override-publishing consumer appears — API-revision allowance). Project stat surface stays **136** (+0).

### Network filter chain framework — terminal-handoff conn-wrap seam (28.1 amendment)

*Introduced by phase 28.1 (write half [28.1a] + read half [28.1b]). Justified by ADR-0221 (the terminal-handoff conn-wrap seam, both directions) — CONSUMING the ADR-0213 §Decision-item-8 API-revision allowance (consumer #1 `zookeeper_proxy`; anticipated #2 `mongo_proxy`). NO operator-visible behavior change to any existing chain: every chain with ZERO write filters gets NEITHER conn-wrap → `handleTerminal` is byte-identical to 26.2/27 (R1, ratified by all 47 pre-existing fixture dirs staying byte-exact green).*

The L4 chain framework gains a symmetric write + read seam at terminal handoff. `NewChainRuntime` classifies a built `[]NetworkFilter` by INDEPENDENT type-asserts into a read set, a write set, and an optional trailing terminal — a filter implementing BOTH (zookeeper_proxy) lands in BOTH sets as the SAME instance (dual callback injection; `OnDestroy` deduped once-per-instance via interface-identity). Both conn-wraps install under ONE shared predicate (`len(writeFilters) > 0`); a chain gets BOTH wraps or NEITHER. The terminal sees `writeChainConn(prefixConn(readChainConn(conn)))` (readChainConn innermost, writeChainConn outermost).

**Write side (28.1a):**

- **REVERSE-chain-order write dispatch (AMEND-A11 LIFO).** `handleTerminal` hands the `writeChainConn` a REVERSED copy of the chain-order write filters: config `[A, B, C]` ⇒ write dispatch `C → B → A` (upstream `addWriteFilter` front-insert / LIFO parity). The `writeChainConn.Write(p)` runs the dispatch-order chain over a fresh per-Write `*Buffer`, then forwards the post-chain buffer to the wrapped conn.
- **`StopIteration`-on-write = the-write-does-not-proceed, documented-UNSUPPORTED-by-consumers.** envoy-go mirrors the upstream no-forward semantic (the bytes never reach the transport); the return is `(len(p), nil)` (the terminal cannot distinguish a stopped write from a delivered one — D-P7, exactly as upstream `ConnectionImpl::write` returns void). No production filter returns it at 28.x (zookeeper always Continues); the no-resume/inject machinery is deferred to the first consumer (mongo fault-delay) under the API-revision allowance.
- **Terminal-originated-writes-only.** A `ReadFilter` writing via `Connection().Write` (echo, direct_response) does NOT pass through the write chain — the `writeChainConn` wraps only the conn handed to the TERMINAL. Sufficient for `[zookeeper_proxy, tcp_proxy]` (all upstream→downstream bytes are produced by tcp_proxy).
- **The write-only-filter boot boundary.** `internal/listener/manager.go` is UNTOUCHED by the seam; a write-ONLY filter (no `ReadFilter` half) leading a chain still fails boot exactly as before. Every 28.x both-directions filter carries a `ReadFilter` half, so this constrains nothing real (lifted under the allowance if a write-only consumer appears).

**Read side (28.1b):**

- **Replay semantics (§3.2).** The `readChainConn.Read` reads the live socket, then `chainRuntime.replayRead` re-iterates EVERY read filter's `OnData` in chain order over the received bytes BEFORE returning them to the terminal (replay-before-return → deterministic stat ordering), then DRAINS the chain buffer fully after the pass (bounded memory). On `io.EOF` a final endStream replay fires (pre-handoff read-loop symmetry). This restores upstream `FilterManagerImpl::onRead` re-iteration parity — without it the chain runtime exits its read loop at handoff and a request-decoding filter sees only the FIRST socket read per connection (the gap that forced the ADR-0045 28.1a/28.1b split). R3 is preserved: filters never drain — the RUNTIME drains.
- **The shared wrap predicate + R1 (§3.4).** Both conn-wraps install IFF `len(writeFilters) > 0`. Equivalent TODAY to "≥1 read-decoding filter" (every planned request-decoding network filter is a both-directions WriteFilter). A hypothetical one-direction read-decoder would miss this predicate and generalize via an opt-in marker interface under the allowance — none exists or is planned; the next consumer `mongo_proxy` must implement `WriteFilter` (even as a no-op) to get the read seam. Hot-path cost is wrapped-chains-only (one indirection + one Append + one read-chain pass + one Drain per socket read); the R1 population pays ZERO.
- **The `TotalAppended` soundness invariant (§3.3).** The decoder's high-water mark is kept against `Buffer.TotalAppended()` (a monotonic int64 appended-bytes counter), NOT the physical buffer length, so the decoder feed is correct regardless of WHO drains the buffer and WHEN. SOUND iff the runtime never drains bytes a filter has not yet been shown — both drain sites (the handoff drain; the post-replay drain) satisfy it by construction. On any never-drained execution `TotalAppended() == Len()`, so the pre-handoff path is byte-identical to 28.1a.
- **The three observational post-handoff boundaries (§3.5).** The replay is OBSERVATIONAL; three pre-handoff callback capabilities have no post-handoff effect (each a documented framework boundary, deferred to the first consumer needing it under the allowance — no production consumer needs any: zookeeper always Continues, never closes, never drains):

| Capability | Post-handoff (the replay) | Why acceptable |
|---|---|---|
| `OnData` → `StopIteration` | **IGNORED** — the bytes are already committed to the terminal (readChainConn returns them regardless) | Upstream divergence (upstream StopIteration blocks tcp_proxy from seeing the bytes). Honoring it would require the seam to suppress the terminal's read — a flow-control surface no 28.x consumer needs. |
| `Connection().Close(...)` | **NOT ACTED ON** — recorded but nothing post-handoff checks it (the terminal owns the conn lifecycle) | No production consumer closes post-handoff; a kill-on-protocol-violation policy would need a terminal-integration surface (deferred). |
| `ContinueReading()` | **MEANINGLESS** — no parked state exists post-handoff (Status is ignored) | Follows from row 1. |

- **The goroutine-placement note + the per-connection decoder mutex (§3.6 — 28.2 LANDED; ADR-0223).** Post-handoff, two pump goroutines run: goroutine A (downstream→upstream) calls `readChainConn.Read → replayRead →` the request decoder; goroutine B (upstream→downstream) calls `writeChainConn.Write →` the write filters' `OnWrite`. At 28.1b they shared NO mutable state (B's `OnWrite` was a no-op; `writeChainConn.Write` allocates a fresh per-Write `Buffer`) — **the 28.1b race surface was EMPTY** (verified `go test -race` + a dedicated concurrent-pumps unit test over `net.Pipe`). **FORWARD-POINTER DISCHARGED (ADR-0223 §Decision item 4):** the 28.2 response decoder lands in `OnWrite`, so goroutine B now READs + ERASEs the correlation structures goroutine A WRITEs. The race is closed by a **per-connection `sync.Mutex mu`** on the decoder guarding EXACTLY the two correlation maps (`requestsByXid` + `controlRequestsByXid`) — nothing else. The reassembly buffers (`readBuf` / `writeBuf`) and `chainConsumed` remain single-goroutine-owned and lock-free. Entries are COPIED OUT under the lock; counter increments + latency math run outside it. The pre-handoff request path locks too (uniformity; uncontended pre-handoff). `OnDestroy` needs no lock (runs strictly after both pumps join — the `wg.Wait()` happens-after edge). Proven by `TestDecoderConcurrentRequestResponseRace` (`-race -count=5`; removing `mu` triggers an immediate race report) + the live `0048` concurrent pumps (R9 ratified). Upstream has no such race only because libevent serializes both directions onto one dispatcher thread.

"not found"`). `echo.TypeURL` was corrected to the `extensions.` form (and the SPEC §3.6/§4.1 lines corrected in-place at 26.1 IMPL Task 17). `direct_response`'s type URL (`...envoy.extensions.filters.network.direct_response.v3.Config`) already carried `extensions.` and was correct.

## HTTPFilterCallbacks

*Introduced by phase 16. Justified by ADR-0144 (TLS-principal accessor framework primitive).*

This section codifies envoy-go-side extensions to the `DecoderFilterCallbacks` + `EncoderFilterCallbacks` interfaces introduced by §9 family-row phases. Each subsection names the accessor / primitive, the phase that introduced it, the justifying ADR, and the cross-phase reuse intent.

### DownstreamPrincipal accessor (per phase 16 ADR-0144)

`DecoderFilterCallbacks.DownstreamPrincipal() []string` returns the priority-ordered list of TLS principal-name candidates for the active downstream client connection:

1. URI SAN values from `tls.ConnectionState.PeerCertificates[0].URIs[].String()` (priority 1 per `rbac.pb.go:1432-1438` proto comment).
2. DNS SAN values from `tls.ConnectionState.PeerCertificates[0].DNSNames` (priority 2).
3. Subject DN Common Name from `tls.ConnectionState.PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName` (priority 3 fallback).

For plaintext or non-mTLS connections OR connections where no client cert was presented, the accessor returns `nil` (or empty slice).

Cross-phase reuse: future filters (jwt_authn, ext_authz, oauth2) consume the same accessor for TLS-principal introspection.

Phase 16 is the FIRST §9 family-row to introduce this accessor.

### 6 new accessors (per phase 18.2 ADR-0165 — the ADR-0044 escape-valve fired at planner-time D3 + D12)

**AMENDMENT to 18.1-anchored claim — `### envoy.filters.http.ext_authz` §13.5 originally pinned "NO new method on `envoyhttp.DecoderFilterCallbacks` lands at 18.2"; that claim is FLIPPED at phase-18.2 PLAN time per planner-time decisions D3 + D12 + IMPL Task 4 landing.** The PLAN-time deviation rationale: at PLAN time the planner re-verified the master-tip callback surface against the 18.2 SPEC's own §15 acceptance item 4 + §11.P4 RATIFICATION (populated `tls_session.sni` / `source.certificate` / source + destination socket addresses / `destination.principal` / `request.http.protocol`) and determined the populated set is UNSATISFIABLE without callback extension — the existing `DownstreamPrincipal()` alone covers only the client-cert principal candidates. The PLAN settled by AMENDING SPEC §13.5 + §6.5 step 5 + §6.6 in-place at Task 4. 6 new methods land on `DecoderFilterCallbacks` at IMPL Task 4 per ADR-0165:

1. **`DownstreamRemoteAddr() net.Addr`** — downstream client remote address (IP + port). Populates `AttributeContext.source.address.socket_address`.
2. **`DownstreamLocalAddr() net.Addr`** — local listener bind address (IP + port). Populates `AttributeContext.destination.address.socket_address`.
3. **`DownstreamTLSServerName() string`** — downstream TLS `ConnectionState.ServerName` (SNI value sent by the client). Populates `AttributeContext.tls_session.sni` when `include_tls_session: true` AND TLS connection. Empty for plaintext.
4. **`DownstreamTLSPeerCertDER() []byte`** — DER-encoded leaf cert of the downstream client (presented during mTLS handshake). Populates `AttributeContext.source.certificate` when `include_peer_certificate: true` AND the client presented a cert. Nil for plaintext / non-mTLS / no-client-cert.
5. **`DownstreamProtocol() string`** — protocol used on the downstream connection (`HTTP/1.1`, `HTTP/2`). Populates `AttributeContext.request.http.protocol`.
6. **`ListenerPrincipal() string`** — listener TLS cert-derived principal (URI SAN | DNS SAN | Subject DN CN, joined per the ADR-0144 priority order applied to the SERVER cert, not the client cert). Populates `AttributeContext.destination.principal` AUTOMATICALLY (NOT gated by `include_peer_certificate` — per the §11.P4 in-session SPEC RATIFICATION). Empty for plaintext listeners.

Plumbing pattern mirrors ADR-0144's `tlsPrincipals` / `SetTLSPrincipals` / `DownstreamPrincipal()` seed-at-HCM-dispatch discipline. The 6 fields are captured at `DecodeHeaders` time in `dispatchOutboundCheck` (per 18.2 IMPL Task 8) and threaded into the extended `*authRequest` struct; the `buildAttributeContext` builder consumes the `*authRequest` + the 4 config booleans (`includePeerCertificate` / `includeTlsSession` / `encodeRawHeaders` / `packAsBytes`) — `DecoderFilterCallbacks` is NOT passed in as a parameter (the §6.5 mode-agnostic-closure invariant is preserved). The SOURCE of the per-stream state capture into `*authRequest` is now those 6 callbacks.

**Cross-phase reuse intent:** ext_proc (next-anticipated §9 row consuming a structured-proto outbound to an upstream service), global_ratelimit (gRPC-trailer-based rate-limiting requiring socket addresses + TLS principal for descriptor evaluation), future ext_authz extensions (non-MVP fields that may require additional cert / connection introspection) all consume the same 6 accessors. The cross-phase-reusable framework primitive lands once at 18.2 IMPL Task 4 + amends in-place if/when additional fields surface.

Phase 18.2 is the SECOND §9 family-row to extend `DecoderFilterCallbacks` (after phase-16's `DownstreamPrincipal()`).

### 6 new EncoderFilterCallbacks accessors — symmetric extension (per phase 19.1 ADR-0174)

**AMENDMENT to 18.2-anchored framing.** ADR-0174 EXTENDS the same 6 socket/TLS/listener accessors landed at 18.2 on `DecoderFilterCallbacks` to the symmetric `EncoderFilterCallbacks` surface. The phase-19 SPEC's §5.P12 in-session empirical scrape REFUTED the BRAINSTORM §3.3 CONDITIONAL hypothesis for encode-side callback symmetry — the master-tip `EncoderFilterCallbacks` carried only `ContinueEncoding` + `EncodeHeaders/Data/Trailers` (encode-side injection) + `OverwriteBody` (ADR-0131); no socket/TLS/listener accessors. Phase 19's `response_attributes` envelope (populated at the response_headers stage per the proto's `ExternalProcessor.response_attributes` doc-comment) requires encode-side access to the same socket/TLS/listener state that decode-side `request_attributes` consumes. The 6 new methods land on `EncoderFilterCallbacks` at IMPL Task 5 per ADR-0174:

1. **`DownstreamRemoteAddr() net.Addr`** — downstream client remote address (IP + port). Populates `ProcessingRequest.attributes.source.address.socket_address` at the response_headers stage.
2. **`DownstreamLocalAddr() net.Addr`** — local listener bind address (IP + port). Populates `ProcessingRequest.attributes.destination.address.socket_address`.
3. **`DownstreamTLSServerName() string`** — downstream TLS `ConnectionState.ServerName` (SNI value sent by the client). Empty for plaintext.
4. **`DownstreamTLSPeerCertDER() []byte`** — DER-encoded leaf cert of the downstream client (presented during mTLS handshake). Nil for plaintext / non-mTLS / no-client-cert.
5. **`DownstreamProtocol() string`** — protocol used on the downstream connection (`HTTP/1.1`, `HTTP/2`).
6. **`ListenerPrincipal() string`** — listener TLS cert-derived principal (URI SAN | DNS SAN | Subject DN CN per ADR-0144 priority order applied to the SERVER cert).

**Chain-side seeding discipline UNCHANGED from ADR-0165.** The 6 chain fields (`downstreamRemoteAddr` / `downstreamLocalAddr` / `downstreamTLSServerName` / `downstreamTLSPeerCertDER` / `downstreamProtocol` / `listenerPrincipal`) already exist per ADR-0165's plumbing — they are SET ONCE at chain build time by HCM dispatch (H1 `connection.go:dispatchRequest` + H2 `h2dispatch.go:WriteH2`) BEFORE either `RunDecodeHeaders` or `RunEncodeHeaders` dispatch. **NO new chain plumbing primitives** — the chain fields are shared; the encoder-side reader methods access the same chain pointer via `*encoderCB`. The 6 NEW `*encoderCB` reader methods (added at 19.1 IMPL Task 5) return the chain field verbatim — no copy, no transformation. This is a thin reader-method extension on top of existing chain plumbing, NOT a new framework primitive.

**Cross-phase reuse intent (per ADR-0174 §Decision):** future encode-side filters consuming socket/TLS/listener state — e.g., a response-validation filter that 500s on schema violations, encode-side rate-limiting based on response shape + listener-cert identity, encode-side header-injection from downstream-cert state — all consume the same 6 accessors. The cross-phase-reusable framework primitive lands once at 19.1 IMPL Task 5 + amends in-place if/when additional fields surface.

Phase 19.1 is the FIRST §9 family-row to extend `EncoderFilterCallbacks` with socket/TLS/listener accessors (phase 14 compressor's `OverwriteBody` per ADR-0131 was the only prior encode-side framework primitive). It is also the SECOND §9 family-row to anchor a cross-phase-reusable callback-surface extension after phase 18.2 ADR-0165 — the pattern (chain-field SET-once-by-HCM-dispatch + READ-by-callback) is now confirmed cross-phase-reusable on BOTH decode + encode sides.

### 7th NEW EncoderFilterCallbacks accessor — `BufferEncodedBody` (per phase 19.2 ADR-0175)

**Phase 19.2 EXTENDS the `EncoderFilterCallbacks` surface with the 7th new accessor** — `BufferEncodedBody() []byte` — the NEW encode-side body-buffering framework primitive. This is envoy-go's FIRST encode-side body-buffering primitive (the symmetric mirror of phase-13 ADR-0128 decode-side `BufferedBody`); it is distinct from + complementary to phase-14 ADR-0131 `OverwriteBody` (which is per-call replacement only, NOT buffer-and-hold). Surface:

- **`BufferEncodedBody() []byte`** — returns the accumulated buffered body bytes captured by the chain on `DataStopIterationAndBuffer` returns from prior `EncodeData` calls. Returns the live buffer slice; the filter mutates in place (subject to the standard "the filter takes ownership of the buffer on resume" discipline). Returns nil before any data has been accumulated, mirroring the decode-side `BufferedBody()` accessor's nil-on-empty convention.

**Chain-side discipline (per `internal/filter/http/chain.go` Run`EncodeData` extension at 19.2 IMPL Task 2):**

- On `DataStopIterationAndBuffer` returns from a filter's `EncodeData`, the chain accumulates the incoming chunk into the per-encoderCB `c.encodeBuf []byte` field AND does NOT forward the chunk downstream. This mirrors `RunDecodeData`'s ADR-0128 accumulation discipline exactly.
- On `ContinueEncoding()` resume, the chain releases the (possibly-mutated) `c.encodeBuf` downstream + clears the field. The filter is responsible for header-state reconciliation (Content-Length on length-change per ADR-0175 §Decision — the encode-side analog of ADR-0128 §Decision's post-body reconciliation).
- End-of-stream signal closes the buffering window — if the filter does NOT resume by end-of-stream, the chain treats the response as truncated per the existing chain-side error path (symmetric to the decode-side discipline).
- Buffer-overflow discipline mirrors `errDecodeBufferOverflow` (per planner-time D7) — when accumulated body exceeds the configured cap, the chain emits a 500 LocalReply via the existing error path. Race-tested at IMPL Task 8 (`TestEncodeBufConcurrency_*` group).

**Cross-phase reuse intent (per ADR-0175 §Decision):** any future encode-side filter requiring full-body inspection or mutation (a hypothetical encode-side content-injection filter; a future encode-side `lua` body callback; an encode-side schema-validation filter) composes against `BufferEncodedBody()` without re-deriving the buffer-and-hold discipline. The primitive lands once at 19.2 IMPL Task 2; future encode-side filters extend in-place.

**NOT-REUSED at 19.2:** phase-14 ADR-0131 `OverwriteBody(b []byte)` per-call replacement primitive — distinct semantics; both stay on `EncoderFilterCallbacks` post-19.2 as complementary primitives.

Phase 19.2 is the SECOND §9 family-row to add a NEW framework primitive on the encode side (phase 19.1 ADR-0174 added the 6 socket/TLS/listener accessors via existing chain plumbing; phase 19.2 ADR-0175 introduces NEW chain-side plumbing — the per-encoderCB `encodeBuf` field + the `RunEncodeData` accumulation extension).

## Matcher engine framework primitive (per phase 16 ADR-0142)

*Introduced by phase 16. Justified by ADR-0142.*

Phase 16 introduces a new top-level `internal/matcher/` package providing a generic `xds.type.matcher.v3.Matcher` match-tree evaluator. The package exports:

- `matcher.New(tree *matchv3.Matcher, supportedActionTypes []string) (*Matcher, error)` — parses the match tree + validates terminal action TypeURLs against the caller's allow-list at config-load time; PARSE-REJECT for unknown TypeURLs with envoy-go-only error.
- `matcher.Evaluate(ctx MatchContext) (*anypb.Any, error)` — walks the match tree at request time + returns the matched terminal action TypedExtensionConfig (wrapped as `Any`) OR `(nil, nil)` for no-match.
- `matcher.MatchContext` interface — the caller (a filter) implements this on its per-stream `*filter` to expose request accessors (headers, IP, principal, etc.).

Phase 16's rbac filter consumes the primitive with `supportedActionTypes = ["type.googleapis.com/envoy.config.rbac.v3.Action"]` (the canonical RBAC terminal; per phase 16 SPEC §11.P3); future filters extend the allow-list as new terminal types land.

Cross-phase reuse intent: ext_authz, jwt_authn, oauth2 all use the same `xds.type.matcher.v3.Matcher` primitive for parts of their config surface. Each future filter extends `supportedActionTypes` + widens `MatchContext` additively.

## JWKS framework primitive (per phase 17 ADR-0150)

*Introduced by phase 17. Justified by ADR-0150.*

Phase 17 introduces a new top-level `internal/jwks/` package providing an HTTP-outbound JWKS fetcher with a thread-safe cache + background refresh. The package exports:

- `jwks.New(uri string, cacheDuration time.Duration, asyncFetch *AsyncFetch, retryPolicy *RetryPolicy) (*Fetcher, error)` — constructs a `Fetcher`; performs a BLOCKING initial fetch when `fast_listener` is unset/false (default — initial-fetch failure returns an error and fails listener-load per ADR-0150 §Decision (iii)), or a non-blocking initial fetch when `fast_listener: true`.
- `(*Fetcher) Get(ctx) (*JWKSet, error)` — returns the cached `*JWKSet`, or `ErrJwksNotReady` while a non-blocking initial fetch is still in flight.
- `(*Fetcher) Close() error` — stops the background refresh goroutine; idempotent.
- `(*JWKSet) Lookup(kid, alg string) (crypto.PublicKey, error)` — Envoy `pickKeyAlgWithKid` lookup (match on `kid` first; fall back to first key with matching `alg`).
- `ParseJWKSet(raw []byte) (*JWKSet, error)` — RFC 7517 §5 JWK Set JSON parsing; RSA + EC (P-256/384/521) key types.

**Refresh schedule:** on a successful fetch, the next refresh is scheduled at `cacheDuration - 5s` via `time.AfterFunc` (clamped to 0 if `cacheDuration < 5s`); default cache duration is 10 minutes. **Failed-refetch schedule:** a fixed 1s interval (configurable via `AsyncFetch.FailedRefetchDuration`); NO exponential backoff (phase 17 SPEC §11.P4 REFUTED the exponential-backoff hypothesis). Inner-HTTP-request retries are honored via the `RetryPolicy` config (NumRetries + BaseInterval + MaxInterval).

**Observability:** each RemoteJwks provider whose initial blocking fetch succeeds credits the filter's `jwks_fetch_success` counter once at filter-load time; a failed request-time `Get()` increments `jwks_fetch_failed` (per ADR-0154 §Decision (vii)). Initial-fetch failure under the default (blocking) mode fails listener-load loudly rather than activating a degraded listener.

**Cross-phase reuse intent:** future filters consuming outbound-HTTP-from-filter primitives — `ext_authz` HTTP-mode, `oauth2` token-endpoint flows — compose against the `Fetcher` type's `http.Client` + retry-policy structure.

**REFACTORED-AT-PHASE-20 (per ADR-0150 §Decision AMENDMENT — landed at phase-20 IMPL Task 2 paired with the ADR-0177 NEW `internal/httpclient/` framework primitive introduction).** The `internal/jwks/Fetcher` constructor no longer owns its own `http.Client`; it now takes a `*httpclient.Client` constructor argument per the ADR-0177 framework-primitive consumption pattern. Concrete signature shift: `jwks.New(httpClient *httpclient.Client, uri string, cacheDuration time.Duration, asyncFetch *AsyncFetch, retryPolicy *RetryPolicy) (*Fetcher, error)` — the `*httpclient.Client` argument is wired at filter-construction time via the boot-shared singleton (per `cmd/envoy-go/main.go`'s shared client + the `FactoryCtx` threading per ADR-0177 §Decision). Inner-HTTP-request retries continue honored via the existing `RetryPolicy` config (no behavioral change at the wire — the refactor is pure thin-wrapper-substitution; `internal/httpclient/Client.Do` is the new dispatch site that was previously inline in the Fetcher). **3 consumers at phase-20 phase-done**: jwks Fetcher (this refactor) + extauthz httpAuthClient (post-ADR-0159 in-place AMENDMENT per the `## HTTP outbound auth-check framework note` CLOSURE-AT-PHASE-20 paragraph below) + oauth2 token_endpoint POST (NEW at phase-20). The cross-phase-consumer disposition CLOSES the implicit forward-pointer to a future httpclient primitive that ADR-0150 §Consequences carried since phase 17. Per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline — NOT a new ADR; ADR-0150 evolves in-place with the AMENDMENT paragraph dated 2026-05-17 and cross-referenced to phase 20 + ADR-0177. Cross-package regression matrix per phase-20 SPEC §12 item C8: fixture-0019 (jwt_authn) GREEN post-refactor (RATIFIED at phase-20 IMPL Task 2b regression check); zero behavioral delta.

## HTTP outbound framework primitive (per phase 20 ADR-0177)

*Introduced by phase 20. Justified by ADR-0177. Related: ADR-0150 §Decision AMENDMENT (jwks Fetcher refactor at phase 20 IMPL Task 2b); ADR-0159 §Decision AMENDMENT (extauthz httpAuthClient refactor at phase 20 IMPL Task 2c) + ADR-0159 §Future Work CLOSURE-AT-PHASE-20 paragraph.*

Phase 20 introduces a new top-level `internal/httpclient/` package providing a generic HTTP-outbound primitive for filters that dispatch synchronous HTTP requests to upstream services. The package exports:

- **`httpclient.New(opts Options) *Client`** — constructs a `*Client` from the `Options` envelope; zero-value `Options` is a no-op (zero `Timeout` = no deadline; zero `RetryPolicy` = no retries; nil `TLSConfig`). The `*Client` is the public surface filters consume.
- **`(*Client) Do(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error)`** — executes the request synchronously over the underlying `*http.Client`; honors `ctx` cancellation propagated through `req.Context()`; applies retries per `Options.RetryPolicy`.
- **`Options`** struct — carries per-Client configuration: `Timeout time.Duration` (applied as `http.Client.Timeout`); `RetryPolicy RetryPolicy` (zero = no retries — matches Envoy v1.37.2 wire default per phase-20 SPEC §20.P1 RATIFIED); `TLSConfig *tls.Config` (wired through the underlying `*http.Transport`).
- **`RetryPolicy`** struct — carries the optional retry envelope: `Attempts int` (0 = no retries); `PerAttemptDelay time.Duration`; `RetryOnStatus []int` (e.g. `[500, 502, 503, 504]` for retry-eligible HTTP statuses).

**3 consumers at introduction time** (the third-consumer trigger condition that fired the extraction per phase-20 BRAINSTORM Q2 + ADR-0159 §Future Work):

1. **jwks Fetcher** (post-ADR-0150 in-place AMENDMENT at phase-20 IMPL Task 2b) — `internal/jwks/fetcher.go` refactored to consume `*httpclient.Client` via constructor argument; REPLACES the inline `http.Client` ownership.
2. **extauthz httpAuthClient** (post-ADR-0159 in-place AMENDMENT at phase-20 IMPL Task 2c) — `internal/filter/http/extauthz/check.go::httpAuthClient` refactored to consume `*httpclient.Client` via constructor argument; REPLACES the inline `http.Client` ownership; **CLOSES the ADR-0159 §Future Work forward-pointer** ("third outbound-HTTP consumer triggers `internal/httpclient/` extraction" — the third-consumer trigger fires exactly as ADR-0159 anticipated; FIRST §9 family-row to CLOSE a prior-phase load-bearing forward-pointer).
3. **oauth2 token_endpoint POST** (NEW at phase 20) — `internal/filter/http/oauth2/oauth_client.go::postTokenEndpoint` consumes the new primitive via `cc.httpClient.Do(req)` at the async-resume continuation site (parked by `StopIteration` per phase-09 async-resume primitive REUSE).

**Cross-phase reuse intent (per ADR-0177 §Future Work — NEW forward-pointer):** future filters consuming outbound-HTTP from a filter compose against `*httpclient.Client` directly. The next-cross-consumer event is anticipated at future ext_authz mTLS (`TLSConfig` field activation), future jwt_authn alternative-issuer fetch (a second JWKS consumer beyond the current single-issuer-per-provider shape), future ratelimit gRPC TLS (when global_ratelimit lands with operator-config-driven TLS-to-rate-limit-cluster), each at its own future trigger condition.

**Singleton boot lifecycle (per ADR-0177 §Decision + the `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` shared-client pattern landed at IMPL Task 2b + 2c):** the `*httpclient.Client` is constructed ONCE at process boot from a base `Options` envelope and threaded through to filter constructors via the `FactoryCtx` carrier — the same `*Client` is shared across all jwks Fetchers + all extauthz httpAuthClient instances + all oauth2 filter instances. The shared client is goroutine-safe (composes around `*http.Client` which is goroutine-safe per the stdlib contract); no per-filter `http.Transport` proliferation. Per-call timeouts ride through `req.Context()` (the per-Filter Options `Timeout` field stays available for per-Client overrides when a filter needs a tighter envelope than the boot default).
